skills.description: Use when synthesising 12CO fluxes for populations of protoplanetary discs (e.g. Lupus, Upper Sco) where running thermochemical codes per disc is prohibitively slow, or when tracing disc surface-area evolution from optically thick CO fluxes.
skills.name: 12co-line-flux-modelling
skills.search_text: 12co-line-flux-modelling Use when synthesising 12CO fluxes for populations of protoplanetary discs (e.g. Lupus, Upper Sco) where running thermochemical codes per disc is prohibitively slow, or when tracing disc surface-area evolution from optically thick CO fluxes. When a full physico-chemical treatment of the disc (thermochemical structure, detailed CO chemistry) is required — DALI-class models, not the semi-analytical flux model, are the right tool When CO is expected to be optically thin or severely depleted such that the optically-thick flux–surface-area scaling no longer holds When interpreting flux ratios for conclusions about viscosity vs MHD-wind disc evolution without acknowledging that initial-condition uncertainties limited interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 A semi-analytical method to compute 12CO line fluxes of protoplanetary discs using power-law surface-density and temperature profiles, avoiding computationally-expensive thermochemical modelling (DALI) for hundreds of discs. It is the core capability of the COpops package for testing disc evolution scenarios with ALMA CO fluxes. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202346164
skills.summary: A semi-analytical method to compute 12CO line fluxes of protoplanetary discs using power-law surface-density and temperature profiles, avoiding computationally-expensive thermochemical modelling (DALI) for hundreds of discs. It is the core capability of the COpops package for testing disc evolution scenarios with ALMA CO fluxes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a full physico-chemical treatment of the disc (thermochemical structure, detailed CO chemistry) is required — DALI-class models, not the semi-analytical flux model, are the right tool When CO is expected to be optically thin or severely depleted such that the optically-thick flux–surface-area scaling no longer holds When interpreting flux ratios for conclusions about viscosity vs MHD-wind disc evolution without acknowledging that initial-condition uncertainties limited interpretation

skills.description: Use when building simulated polarimeter timestreams (signal-only and signal-plus-noise) to test a destriping pipeline, e.g. with B-Machine-like 1/f noise parameters and ~33.4 Hz sampling.
skills.name: 1f-plus-white-noise-synthesis
skills.search_text: 1f-plus-white-noise-synthesis Use when building simulated polarimeter timestreams (signal-only and signal-plus-noise) to test a destriping pipeline, e.g. with B-Machine-like 1/f noise parameters and ~33.4 Hz sampling. The goal is to destripe an existing real timestream rather than synthesize a simulated one (use the dst destriper directly instead). The data format is not the dst single-HDF5 layout with TIME/PHI/THETA/PSI/FLAG/TEMP/Q/U columns, and dst_io.read_data cannot be adapted to it. The 1/f knee frequency is higher than the scan rate — the paper's destriping approach assumes correlated noise with knee frequency lower than the scan rate. Generates realistic simulated timestreams for CMB polarimeter data by scanning a sky map through a pointing model and adding noise whose timeline follows the destriping data model n = Fa + w, i.e. a white noise component plus a correlated 1/f component represented as baselines multiplied by a sparse matrix F. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Generates realistic simulated timestreams for CMB polarimeter data by scanning a sky map through a pointing model and adding noise whose timeline follows the destriping data model n = Fa + w, i.e. a white noise component plus a correlated 1/f component represented as baselines multiplied by a sparse matrix F.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to destripe an existing real timestream rather than synthesize a simulated one (use the dst destriper directly instead). The 1/f knee frequency is higher than the scan rate — the paper's destriping approach assumes correlated noise with knee frequency lower than the scan rate.

skills.description: Use when you have multiwavelength broadband photometry (e.g., a space-separated CSV like example_data/grb_afterglow.csv with GRB afterglow data) and need a joint, data-driven model over both time and frequency axes rather than fitting each band separately.
skills.name: 2d-gp-multiwavelength-surface-modeling
skills.search_text: 2d-gp-multiwavelength-surface-modeling Use when you have multiwavelength broadband photometry (e.g., a space-separated CSV like example_data/grb_afterglow.csv with GRB afterglow data) and need a joint, data-driven model over both time and frequency axes rather than fitting each band separately. You need physically motivated afterglow model parameters (e.g., jet or circumstellar medium parameters) rather than a non-parametric, data-driven interpolation surface. Data are single-band or otherwise unsuited to joint 2D time–frequency GP regression; fit a 1D lightcurve model instead. Input is not multiwavelength photometry (e.g., spectra or X-ray spectral data, which redback routes to spectral template matching / xray_spectral_fitting workflows). http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Fit a 2D Gaussian Process jointly over time and frequency/wavelength axes to multiwavelength photometry using redback's george kernel interface (ConstantKernel x Matern32Kernel), sampling GP hyperparameters with bilby-wrapped samplers such as nestle/dynesty. This recovers a smooth lightcurve/spectrum surface (e.g., for GRB afterglow broadband data) while quantifying uncertainty across all bands simultaneously. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stae1238
skills.summary: Fit a 2D Gaussian Process jointly over time and frequency/wavelength axes to multiwavelength photometry using redback's george kernel interface (ConstantKernel x Matern32Kernel), sampling GP hyperparameters with bilby-wrapped samplers such as nestle/dynesty. This recovers a smooth lightcurve/spectrum surface (e.g., for GRB afterglow broadband data) while quantifying uncertainty across all bands simultaneously.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need physically motivated afterglow model parameters (e.g., jet or circumstellar medium parameters) rather than a non-parametric, data-driven interpolation surface. Data are single-band or otherwise unsuited to joint 2D time–frequency GP regression; fit a 1D lightcurve model instead. Input is not multiwavelength photometry (e.g., spectra or X-ray spectral data, which redback routes to spectral template matching / xray_spectral_fitting workflows).

The goal is a single global (non-individual) time step — the rung scheme only pays off for adaptive per-particle stepping. The target is fluid/relativistic component time-stepping rather than particle rungs; the paper notes an 'Erroneous time-stepping limiter for fluid components' prior to the v0.2.0 fix. You are modelling strongly clustered systems at very high resolution, where CONCEPT 1.0 is slower than GADGET and load imbalance degrades performance. Reconstructs CONCEPT 1.0's hierarchical leapfrog time-stepping scheme in which individual particles are assigned to rungs ℓ (step size Δt/2^ℓ) using the acceleration criterion of eq. 42: a particle must not accelerate across a fraction η of its softening length within its rung's time step. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stac568

skills.search_text: airmass-extinction-trend-modeling Use when fitting ground-based transit light curves that show smooth, airmass-correlated brightness trends (e.g. from differential extinction during the night), and you need unbiased transit parameters and per-transit Tmid via MCMC. skills.name: analytic-inverse-solution-derivation
skills.search_text: analytic-inverse-solution-derivation Use when validating a numerical equilibrium radiative-transfer solver (e.g. rabacus Slab_Pln) against an analytic benchmark, or when a closed-form ionization-fraction-vs-column-depth profile is needed for a uniform pure-H slab under monochromatic plane-parallel illumination. The problem requires non-equilibrium chemistry or metal line cooling, which rabacus explicitly does not yet provide (planned future improvements). The radiation field is polychromatic or the gas includes helium, so the monochromatic pure-hydrogen inversion of Eqs. 23-25 no longer applies. The geometry is spherical (central point source or isotropic background) rather than a plane-parallel slab, where no planar column-depth inversion exists. Derives the algebraic inverse of the hydrogen ionization balance (Eqs. 23-25) for a monochromatic, plane-parallel, uniform pure-hydrogen slab, and uses that closed-form solution as the benchmark for the rabacus Slab_Pln numerical solver. Agreement is quantified by pointwise relative difference on a common column-depth grid and must stay below 7e-3. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.004
skills.summary: Derives the algebraic inverse of the hydrogen ionization balance (Eqs. 23-25) for a monochromatic, plane-parallel, uniform pure-hydrogen slab, and uses that closed-form solution as the benchmark for the rabacus Slab_Pln numerical solver. Agreement is quantified by pointwise relative difference on a common column-depth grid and must stay below 7e-3.

skills.search_text: anisotropic-potential-expansion-interpretation Use when a molscat/BOUND run specifies an anisotropic potential via &POTL (MXLAM, LAMBDA, NTERM, NPOWER, A) and you need to reproduce or replace it with a user-supplied VSTAR routine, or verify the printed POTENL expansion matches documented coefficients. When the interaction potential is a simple one already fully expressible as input data (the README states 'Simple interaction potentials may be specified in input data and more complicated ones may be handled with plug-in routines') When the collision type or external-field treatment is the part being customised — that is handled by basis-set-suite plug-ins, not the VSTAR potential hook When the potential is tabulated data for Mg + NH or H2 + H2 supplied in the data/ directory rather than an analytic expansion Interprets and re-implements the anisotropic interaction-potential expansion read from the molscat/BOUND &POTL namelist (MXLAM, LAMBDA, NTERM, NPOWER, A), including routing selected expansion terms to a user-supplied VINIT/VSTAR plug-in routine instead of direct input coefficients. This lets the same model potential (e.g. two lambda=0 terms plus one lambda=2 term) be supplied either as data or programmatically. astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.1903.06755
skills.summary: Interprets and re-implements the anisotropic interaction-potential expansion read from the molscat/BOUND &POTL namelist (MXLAM, LAMBDA, NTERM, NPOWER, A), including routing selected expansion terms to a user-supplied VINIT/VSTAR plug-in routine instead of direct input coefficients. This lets the same model potential (e.g. two lambda=0 terms plus one lambda=2 term) be supplied either as data or programmatically.

skills.description: Use when estimating a vapour pressure at a temperature below the measured range (e.g. 20°C) for an organometallic compound whose hydrocarbon analogue (Sn→C substitution) has known boiling point data, and no direct measurement is available.
skills.name: antoine-equation-parameterization
skills.search_text: antoine-equation-parameterization Use when estimating a vapour pressure at a temperature below the measured range (e.g. 20°C) for an organometallic compound whose hydrocarbon analogue (Sn→C substitution) has known boiling point data, and no direct measurement is available. When the compound's hydrocarbon analogue lacks appropriate boiling point data — the paper notes adequacy for other tetraalkyl/alkenylstannanes is uncertain 'because of lack of appropriate boiling point data'. When the target property relationship relies on molecular weight — the paper states existing MW-based relationships for hydrocarbons cannot be used with tetraorganostannanes; use the intrinsic molar volume relationship instead. When direct measured vapour pressures within the 40–120°C range are available and no sub-range extrapolation is needed — measured GC values should be used directly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3397 Parameterizes the Antoine equation from the normal boiling point of a hydrocarbon analogue of an organostannane (central Sn treated as carbon) to extrapolate 20°C vapour pressures below the 40–120°C GC measurement range, then compares estimates with experimental values. astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w
skills.summary: Parameterizes the Antoine equation from the normal boiling point of a hydrocarbon analogue of an organostannane (central Sn treated as carbon) to extrapolate 20°C vapour pressures below the 40–120°C GC measurement range, then compares estimates with experimental values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the compound's hydrocarbon analogue lacks appropriate boiling point data — the paper notes adequacy for other tetraalkyl/alkenylstannanes is uncertain 'because of lack of appropriate boiling point data'. When the target property relationship relies on molecular weight — the paper states existing MW-based relationships for hydrocarbons cannot be used with tetraorganostannanes; use the intrinsic molar volume relationship instead. When direct measured vapour pressures within the 40–120°C range are available and no sub-range extrapolation is needed — measured GC values should be used directly.

skills.description: Use when given a weak-lensing galaxy shear catalog (positions and elliptities) and the goal is to produce an aperture mass map over the surveyed field via the Schirmer et al (2007) filter.
skills.name: aperture-mass-map-generation
skills.search_text: aperture-mass-map-generation Use when given a weak-lensing galaxy shear catalog (positions and elliptities) and the goal is to produce an aperture mass map over the surveyed field via the Schirmer et al (2007) filter. The analysis goal is the 2-pt angular correlation function rather than an aperture mass map — use the ccogs angular_correlation package instead, which uses data plus a flat distribution of randomly generated galaxies and a chosen estimator. The input is already a computed aperture mass map (FITS image) rather than a raw shear catalog; this skill reconstructs the map from galaxy positions and elliptities. No GPU execution environment is available, since ccogs packages are designed for computing cosmological quantities on the GPU. http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 http://edamontology.org/topic_3397 Computes a 2-D aperture mass map from a weak-lensing galaxy shear catalog using the aperture_mass package of the ccogs suite, applying the Schirmer et al (2007) filter — an NFW profile with exponential cut-offs at zero and large radii — with GPU-accelerated convolution. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2012.11.001
skills.summary: Computes a 2-D aperture mass map from a weak-lensing galaxy shear catalog using the aperture_mass package of the ccogs suite, applying the Schirmer et al (2007) filter — an NFW profile with exponential cut-offs at zero and large radii — with GPU-accelerated convolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is the 2-pt angular correlation function rather than an aperture mass map — use the ccogs angular_correlation package instead, which uses data plus a flat distribution of randomly generated galaxies and a chosen estimator. The input is already a computed aperture mass map (FITS image) rather than a raw shear catalog; this skill reconstructs the map from galaxy positions and elliptities. No GPU execution environment is available, since ccogs packages are designed for computing cosmological quantities on the GPU.

skills.name: appendix-table-reproduction
skills.search_text: appendix-table-reproduction Use when a paper publishes an appendix results table (e.g. Table B.1 of the SUSHI paper) and the associated artifact (trained models, validation splits) is released in the companion repository, so the numbers can be regenerated and checked. The IAE network weights for a component are not shared in the repository — only the IAE code and training notebooks are available, so reproducing the table would require retraining first. The goal is to validate SUSHI's unmixing output (e.g. RMSE of 0.19 thermal / 0.16 synchrotron vs the classic per-pixel fit) rather than the surrogate spectral model itself. Only the paper's headline results on Cassiopeia A or the Crab Nebula Chandra data are of interest and no appendix table with a reproducible artifact exists. Reproduce a paper's appendix benchmark table — here SUSHI's Table B.1 of per-component IAE held-out reconstruction residuals — by re-running the described computation on the released trained models and comparing the five resulting values to the published reference numbers. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202347518

skills.search_text: ast-channel-text-serialisation Use when you need to generate or validate the human-readable, block-structured AST text description of a Mapping (e.g. a CmpMap of PermMap and ZoomMap) and compare it against a reference listing. You need machine-readable serialisation (e.g. FITS-WCS encoding) rather than the Channel's human-readable block text — AST supports other storage formats for that purpose. The mappings of interest are not AST objects (e.g. arbitrary coordinate transforms outside the AST data model) — Channel only serialises AST Mappings such as PermMap, ZoomMap and CmpMap. skills.description: Use when you need to build or verify an AST compound Mapping (e.g. a CmpMap over PermMap/ZoomMap components) or check its block-structured Channel text output against a reference listing such as the paper's Section 4 output.
skills.name: ast-mapping-construction
skills.search_text: ast-mapping-construction Use when you need to build or verify an AST compound Mapping (e.g. a CmpMap over PermMap/ZoomMap components) or check its block-structured Channel text output against a reference listing such as the paper's Section 4 output. The coordinate information already exists in data files as FITS-WCS — AST's stated strength is retrieving and interpreting such formats, so parse the existing description rather than re-building Mappings by hand. The transformation needed is not expressible as axis permutation with constant substitution plus a uniform zoom — PermMap and ZoomMap cover only those cases, so other AST Mapping classes are required. The goal is building other Starlink components such as the Java applications (TOPCAT/STILTS/SPLAT) — those are built separately via ant per the starjava README and are unrelated to this Mapping-construction skill. Constructs compound coordinate Mappings with the Starlink AST library's Python bindings — combining primitive Mappings such as PermMap([3,1],[2,-1,1],12.2) and ZoomMap(3,4.0) into a CmpMap — and serialises the result through an AST Channel into AST's block-structured text form for inspection, storage, or comparison against a reference listing. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2016.02.003

skills.when_to_use_negative: The coordinate information already exists in data files as FITS-WCS — AST's stated strength is retrieving and interpreting such formats, so parse the existing description rather than re-building Mappings by hand. skills.summary: Defines the input-encoding split for a NeuralPDR-style Latent Augmented Neural ODE surrogate of 3D-PDR chemistry: visual extinction (Av), radiation field (G0), cosmic ray ionisation rate and density are injected as conditioning parameters, while chemical abundances and temperature are evolved as ordinary features of the augmented neural ODE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target is the raw 3D-PDR solver output rather than a learned surrogate — the feature/parameter split only applies to the neural ODE emulator, not to the physical code The dataset has not been processed into training-ready HDF5 format via the header scripts (v1_add_headers.py, workflow_v2.sh, workflow_v3.sh) — the abundance/temperature arrays and parameter fields will not yet be in inspectable shape The surrogate must handle time- or space-varying quantities that the chosen dataset version held constant (e.g. density and cosmic ray rate are constant in v1/v2); re-derive the conditioning split per dataset version

skills.description: Use when a simulation image must be produced without writing Python code — by feeding a YAML config such as demo1.yaml to the galsim executable and writing the rendered galaxy+PSF image to a FITS file.
skills.name: astronomical-fits-image-generation
skills.search_text: astronomical-fits-image-generation Use when a simulation image must be produced without writing Python code — by feeding a YAML config such as demo1.yaml to the galsim executable and writing the rendered galaxy+PSF image to a FITS file. You need interactive, programmatic control inside a Python session (e.g. forming ChromaticObjects by multiplying a GSObject by an SED, or drawImage with a Bandpass) — use the Python API (demo*.py) instead of the config route. The goal is to measure or fit existing images (e.g. shear inference / metacalibration) rather than simulate new ones — this skill only renders and writes simulated FITS images. A custom image, noise, WCS, bandpass, or sensor builder is needed but has not been registered with a type name in an importable module loaded via the top-level modules field — the config parser cannot resolve unknown types on its own. Config-driven generation of simulated astronomical images: a GalSim YAML config (e.g. demo1.yaml, defining a Gaussian galaxy with sigma=2 arcsec and flux=1.e5 convolved with a Gaussian PSF of sigma=1 arcsec) is parsed by the galsim executable, which draws the image and writes it to disk as a FITS file with no Python code required. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.02.002
skills.summary: Config-driven generation of simulated astronomical images: a GalSim YAML config (e.g. demo1.yaml, defining a Gaussian galaxy with sigma=2 arcsec and flux=1.e5 convolved with a Gaussian PSF of sigma=1 arcsec) is parsed by the galsim executable, which draws the image and writes it to disk as a FITS file with no Python code required.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need interactive, programmatic control inside a Python session (e.g. forming ChromaticObjects by multiplying a GSObject by an SED, or drawImage with a Bandpass) — use the Python API (demo*.py) instead of the config route. The goal is to measure or fit existing images (e.g. shear inference / metacalibration) rather than simulate new ones — this skill only renders and writes simulated FITS images. A custom image, noise, WCS, bandpass, or sensor builder is needed but has not been registered with a type name in an importable module loaded via the top-level modules field — the config parser cannot resolve unknown types on its own.

skills.description: Use when you need level population densities of excited hydrogen states (e.g. the 3p state) or hydrogen recombination line emissivities (e.g. H alpha) for gas with specified ne, nHI, nHII, and temperature.
skills.name: atomic-hydrogen-level-population-solving
skills.search_text: atomic-hydrogen-level-population-solving Use when you need level population densities of excited hydrogen states (e.g. the 3p state) or hydrogen recombination line emissivities (e.g. H alpha) for gas with specified ne, nHI, nHII, and temperature. If the gas conditions are far outside typical photoionised nebular conditions (e.g. densities/temperatures where Case B recombination assumptions fail), since HyLight's accuracy claim is stated for typical photoionised nebular conditions only. If you need emission from other species or non-hydrogen recombination lines — the HIAtom model covers only atomic hydrogen excited-state populations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Solves the steady-state rate equations for excited-state level populations of atomic hydrogen using HyLight (hylightpy), given gas density, temperature, and ionization state, and derives recombination line emissivities such as H alpha. Used to reproduce or benchmark Case B hydrogen recombination emission in photoionised nebulae. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stag429
skills.summary: Solves the steady-state rate equations for excited-state level populations of atomic hydrogen using HyLight (hylightpy), given gas density, temperature, and ionization state, and derives recombination line emissivities such as H alpha. Used to reproduce or benchmark Case B hydrogen recombination emission in photoionised nebulae.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the gas conditions are far outside typical photoionised nebular conditions (e.g. densities/temperatures where Case B recombination assumptions fail), since HyLight's accuracy claim is stated for typical photoionised nebular conditions only. If you need emission from other species or non-hydrogen recombination lines — the HIAtom model covers only atomic hydrogen excited-state populations.

skills.description: Use when you have the learned symbolic expression artifact for plin_emulated() and need to demonstrate that individual correction terms carry physical meaning (turnover, spectral index, acoustic/damping, baryonic effects) rather than acting as a black-box fit.
skills.name: baryonic-feature-identification-in-powerspectrum
skills.search_text: baryonic-feature-identification-in-powerspectrum Use when you have the learned symbolic expression artifact for plin_emulated() and need to demonstrate that individual correction terms carry physical meaning (turnover, spectral index, acoustic/damping, baryonic effects) rather than acting as a black-box fit. You only need P(k) values for cosmological inference, not interpretation of the expression's structure — call plin_emulated() directly instead. The emulator is being used with extrapolate=False or outside the trained k range 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc, where the Eisenstein & Hu fit, not the learned symbolic terms, drives the output. You are interpreting the nonlinear emulator (SYREN-HALOFIT) or extended-cosmology emulators (SYREN-NEW, baryonic emulators) rather than the redshift-zero linear LCDM expression. Annotates each additive/multiplicative subterm of the symbolic_pofk linear matter power spectrum emulator (P(k), RMS fractional error 0.2% over k = 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc) with its physical role — turnover scale, spectral index, acoustic/damping features, or baryonic signature — by evaluating subterm contributions over the trained k range and cosmology parameters, and emitting a structured JSON term-to-physics mapping. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202348811
skills.summary: Annotates each additive/multiplicative subterm of the symbolic_pofk linear matter power spectrum emulator (P(k), RMS fractional error 0.2% over k = 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc) with its physical role — turnover scale, spectral index, acoustic/damping features, or baryonic signature — by evaluating subterm contributions over the trained k range and cosmology parameters, and emitting a structured JSON term-to-physics mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need P(k) values for cosmological inference, not interpretation of the expression's structure — call plin_emulated() directly instead. The emulator is being used with extrapolate=False or outside the trained k range 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc, where the Eisenstein & Hu fit, not the learned symbolic terms, drives the output. You are interpreting the nonlinear emulator (SYREN-HALOFIT) or extended-cosmology emulators (SYREN-NEW, baryonic emulators) rather than the redshift-zero linear LCDM expression.

skills.search_text: bayesian-evidence-model-comparison Use when jointly fitting Keplerian signals to HARPS radial velocities and TESS plus ground-based transit photometry, and competing model variants (eccentric vs circular, drift, GP activity) must be compared by Bayesian evidence. Applied to TOI-5005 b, it recovers Rp = 6.25 ± 0.24 R⊕ and Mp = 32.7 ± 5.9 M⊕. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451656

skills.search_text: bin-free-stellar-kinematics-fitting Use when mass-modeling a spherical equilibrium stellar system (dwarf galaxy, star cluster) from discrete tracer positions and individual LOS and/or PM velocities, where binning would discard information and you need the density slope at R1/2. The system is rotating, triaxial, or out of dynamical equilibrium — the method solves spherical higher-order Jeans equations and assumes equilibrium tracers You only hold binned/pre-processed profiles (e.g. the pyGravSphere or binulator hdf5 workflow) rather than individual stellar velocities, so the bin-free likelihood cannot be used Gauss-Hermite velocity models are specifically required — gh_alternative kernels replace them because Gauss-Hermite series are not guaranteed positive-definite Fit individual (unbinned) stellar positions and LOS/proper-motion velocities with GravSphere2's self-consistent, positive-definite non-Gaussian velocity PDFs including kurtosis, solving the fourth-order Jeans equations. This recovers the mass density profile, anisotropy, and the logarithmic density slope at R1/2 with quantified statistical errors. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202557195
skills.summary: Fit individual (unbinned) stellar positions and LOS/proper-motion velocities with GravSphere2's self-consistent, positive-definite non-Gaussian velocity PDFs including kurtosis, solving the fourth-order Jeans equations. This recovers the mass density profile, anisotropy, and the logarithmic density slope at R1/2 with quantified statistical errors.

skills.search_text: binary-cross-entropy-classification-evaluation Use when a two-class, per-timestep sequence classification problem (e.g. 2D spiral clockwise vs anticlockwise) must be solved by a neural CDE and its held-out test accuracy reported against a trained checkpoint. The task is regression or time-series reconstruction (e.g. BIDMC L2-loss experiments) rather than two-class classification — cross-entropy is the wrong loss. Input is a scattering (molscat) run rather than a bound-state (bound) calculation — this skill validates bound-state boundary-condition outputs only. The energy window or JTOT/IBFIX settings differ from the bound-basic1 example, so the section 3.9 reference energies (-4.992074672 and -1.413103892 cm-1) no longer apply as validation targets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 Reproduce and validate converged bound-state energies from the BOUND example bound-basic1 (JTOT=1, IBFIX=2, EMIN=-10 to EMAX=-1 cm-1) by comparing computed state energies against the section 3.9 documented values (-4.992074672 cm-1 for state 4 and -1.413103892 cm-1 for state 5). astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.1903.06755
skills.summary: Reproduce and validate converged bound-state energies from the BOUND example bound-basic1 (JTOT=1, IBFIX=2, EMIN=-10 to EMAX=-1 cm-1) by comparing computed state energies against the section 3.9 documented values (-4.992074672 cm-1 for state 4 and -1.413103892 cm-1 for state 5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a scattering (molscat) run rather than a bound-state (bound) calculation — this skill validates bound-state boundary-condition outputs only. The energy window or JTOT/IBFIX settings differ from the bound-basic1 example, so the section 3.9 reference energies (-4.992074672 and -1.413103892 cm-1) no longer apply as validation targets.

skills.description: Use when you must test whether a kinetic plasma model reproduces non-fluid shock physics at bow-shock-scale resolutions, e.g. comparing magnetic compression ratios and downstream ion distribution non-Maxwellianity across grid resolutions.
skills.name: bow-shock-plasma-parameterization
skills.search_text: bow-shock-plasma-parameterization Use when you must test whether a kinetic plasma model reproduces non-fluid shock physics at bow-shock-scale resolutions, e.g. comparing magnetic compression ratios and downstream ion distribution non-Maxwellianity across grid resolutions. The research question only requires single-fluid MHD behaviour; Vlasiator's hybrid-Vlasov ion-distribution approach is computationally far more expensive than MHD forerunners. The system is not a collisionless shock / near-Earth plasma problem — the article's scope is the Earth's magnetosphere and near-Earth environment, and the hope of extending to astrophysical applications is explicitly future work. Only 3D global magnetosphere dynamics are needed rather than 1D shock-resolved kinetic physics; the immense computational challenges of multi-dimensional ion-scale runs may not be justified. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Parameterize a 1D collisionless shock using the Vlasiator hybrid-Vlasov code at terrestrial bow-shock-like plasma conditions, quantifying kinetic (non-fluid) behaviour via downstream magnetic compression ratio and non-Maxwellianity of the ion distribution at coarse (1000 km) and refined (200 km) resolutions. astronomy/v1 10.1007/s41115-018-0003-2
skills.summary: Parameterize a 1D collisionless shock using the Vlasiator hybrid-Vlasov code at terrestrial bow-shock-like plasma conditions, quantifying kinetic (non-fluid) behaviour via downstream magnetic compression ratio and non-Maxwellianity of the ion distribution at coarse (1000 km) and refined (200 km) resolutions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The research question only requires single-fluid MHD behaviour; Vlasiator's hybrid-Vlasov ion-distribution approach is computationally far more expensive than MHD forerunners. The system is not a collisionless shock / near-Earth plasma problem — the article's scope is the Earth's magnetosphere and near-Earth environment, and the hope of extending to astrophysical applications is explicitly future work. Only 3D global magnetosphere dynamics are needed rather than 1D shock-resolved kinetic physics; the immense computational challenges of multi-dimensional ion-scale runs may not be justified.

skills.description: Use when smoothing noisy astronomical spectra (e.g. quasar spectra before cross-correlation redshifting) where preserving the position of broad emission features matters, or when deciding between an exponential-decay rolling filter and a boxcar baseline.
skills.name: boxcar-baseline-smoothing-comparison
skills.search_text: boxcar-baseline-smoothing-comparison Use when smoothing noisy astronomical spectra (e.g. quasar spectra before cross-correlation redshifting) where preserving the position of broad emission features matters, or when deciding between an exponential-decay rolling filter and a boxcar baseline. The goal is redshift classification or template matching itself (use Marz's autoz cross-correlation workflow; smoothing is only a preprocessing demonstration) The input is already a smoothed or high signal-to-noise spectrum where peak suppression by boxcar averaging is not a concern The signal is not peak-like (e.g. pure continuum estimation), since the skill's validation criterion is specifically peak-location recovery Reconstructs Marz's preprocessing smoother for quasar spectra — a rolling-point exponential decay mean filter (window width 7 pixels, decay factor 0.9, Eq. 2) — and demonstrates against a standard boxcar (moving average) smoother that the exponential decay filter recovers the true signal peak location on Poisson-noised synthetic data (Figure 2 behaviour), while boxcar smoothing depresses the peak. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2016.03.001
skills.summary: Reconstructs Marz's preprocessing smoother for quasar spectra — a rolling-point exponential decay mean filter (window width 7 pixels, decay factor 0.9, Eq. 2) — and demonstrates against a standard boxcar (moving average) smoother that the exponential decay filter recovers the true signal peak location on Poisson-noised synthetic data (Figure 2 behaviour), while boxcar smoothing depresses the peak.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is redshift classification or template matching itself (use Marz's autoz cross-correlation workflow; smoothing is only a preprocessing demonstration) The input is already a smoothed or high signal-to-noise spectrum where peak suppression by boxcar averaging is not a concern The signal is not peak-like (e.g. pure continuum estimation), since the skill's validation criterion is specifically peak-location recovery

skills.description: Use when a task requires generating stochastic Brownian-motion sample paths in JAX, or driving a neural SDE generator with a Brownian control (e.g. diffrax.UnsafeBrownianPath / diffrax.VirtualBrownianTree) to match a reference distribution.
skills.name: brownian-motion-path-simulation
skills.search_text: brownian-motion-path-simulation Use when a task requires generating stochastic Brownian-motion sample paths in JAX, or driving a neural SDE generator with a Brownian control (e.g. diffrax.UnsafeBrownianPath / diffrax.VirtualBrownianTree) to match a reference distribution. The task is predicting on real-world irregularly-sampled time series (e.g. the BIDMC datasets), which calls for neural CDEs with spline interpolation rather than Brownian path simulation. The dynamics are deterministic ODEs with no stochastic Brownian noise component, making SDE machinery unnecessary. The implementation stack is PyTorch rather than JAX, where torchsde would be the appropriate SDE solver library instead of Diffrax. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Simulate Brownian-motion (and neural-SDE-driven) sample paths in JAX using Diffrax, normalising the training series to zero mean and unit variance and integrating with the Reversible Heun solver at unit step size. This reproduces the thesis's Brownian-motion SDE-GAN experiment (Figure 4.3). astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2202.02435
skills.summary: Simulate Brownian-motion (and neural-SDE-driven) sample paths in JAX using Diffrax, normalising the training series to zero mean and unit variance and integrating with the Reversible Heun solver at unit step size. This reproduces the thesis's Brownian-motion SDE-GAN experiment (Figure 4.3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is predicting on real-world irregularly-sampled time series (e.g. the BIDMC datasets), which calls for neural CDEs with spline interpolation rather than Brownian path simulation. The dynamics are deterministic ODEs with no stochastic Brownian noise component, making SDE machinery unnecessary. The implementation stack is PyTorch rather than JAX, where torchsde would be the appropriate SDE solver library instead of Diffrax.

skills.description: Use when parallelised ensemble MCMC chains (e.g. emcee walkers or Metropolis-Hastings chains) must be checked for residual initialisation bias, and a defensible burn-in length must be derived rather than assumed.
skills.name: burn-in-determination-via-standard-error-comparison
skills.search_text: burn-in-determination-via-standard-error-comparison Use when parallelised ensemble MCMC chains (e.g. emcee walkers or Metropolis-Hastings chains) must be checked for residual initialisation bias, and a defensible burn-in length must be derived rather than assumed. The analysis goal is wall-time/scaling performance of the sampler (core-count sweeps), not chain convergence or burn-in length. The chains are already demonstrably converged and only posterior summaries are needed; the burn-in comparison adds no information. skills.description: Use when building language bindings (e.g. Python/Octave) for a C library and you need to automatically enumerate and annotate every exported public constant, function, and class before SWIG's wrapper-generation pass.
skills.name: c-header-annotation-generation
skills.search_text: c-header-annotation-generation Use when building language bindings (e.g. Python/Octave) for a C library and you need to automatically enumerate and annotate every exported public constant, function, and class before SWIG's wrapper-generation pass. The target library already ships hand-maintained SWIG interfaces with explicit SWIGLAL annotations, so automated re-annotation would duplicate or conflict with them. You only need a one-off wrapper for a small C API where manual annotation is cheaper than maintaining the two-pass XML pipeline. The language bindings are for something other than SWIG-supported targets (e.g. ctypes or Cython), since the output is a SWIG interface file, not generic binding code. http://edamontology.org/topic_3344 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Automates annotation of C header files by running SWIG in -xml mode to produce an XML syntax tree, then using the Python script generate_swig_iface.py to insert SWIGLAL directives (from SWIGCommon.i, SWIGLALAlpha.i, SWIGLALOmega.i) into a fully annotated SWIG interface ready for wrapper generation. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.softx.2020.100634
skills.summary: Automates annotation of C header files by running SWIG in -xml mode to produce an XML syntax tree, then using the Python script generate_swig_iface.py to insert SWIGLAL directives (from SWIGCommon.i, SWIGLALAlpha.i, SWIGLALOmega.i) into a fully annotated SWIG interface ready for wrapper generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target library already ships hand-maintained SWIG interfaces with explicit SWIGLAL annotations, so automated re-annotation would duplicate or conflict with them. You only need a one-off wrapper for a small C API where manual annotation is cheaper than maintaining the two-pass XML pipeline. The language bindings are for something other than SWIG-supported targets (e.g. ctypes or Cython), since the output is a SWIG interface file, not generic binding code.

skills.search_text: chain-rule-jacobian-transformation-hyperbolic-systems Use when evolving a coupled hyperbolic conservative system ∂q/∂t + ∂f/∂x = 0 where inverting q→u analytically (or via a polynomial root-find per cell per step) is expensive, and a direct primitive-variable update is acceptable. When the analytic or cheap algebraic recovery u(q) is available at negligible cost, so the Jacobian/A=(∂q/∂u)^−1 machinery is unnecessary When the conservative-to-primitive Jacobian ∂q/∂u is not available symbolically or numerically for the chosen EOS/closure, since the whole update hinges on A=(∂q/∂u)^−1 When enforcing strict conservation of the primitive variables themselves is required — the scheme conserves via the finite-volume flux term, not the primitive update A Primitive Variable Recovery Scheme (PVRS) that transforms conservative charges q into primitive variables u directly via the chain rule on the time term, using the Jacobian matrix A=(∂q/∂u)^−1 evaluated symbolically once, combined with a conservative finite-volume (HLL) spatial update. It avoids solving a costly algebraic recovery system (e.g. a 10th-degree polynomial in relativistic hydrodynamics) at every cell and time step. astronomy/v1 10.1371/journal.pone.0195494
skills.summary: A Primitive Variable Recovery Scheme (PVRS) that transforms conservative charges q into primitive variables u directly via the chain rule on the time term, using the Jacobian matrix A=(∂q/∂u)^−1 evaluated symbolically once, combined with a conservative finite-volume (HLL) spatial update. It avoids solving a costly algebraic recovery system (e.g. a 10th-degree polynomial in relativistic hydrodynamics) at every cell and time step.

skills.search_text: cluster-profile-shape-diversity-analysis Use when you have recovered (nonparametric) mass profiles for multiple clusters and need to test whether a parametric NFW model exhausts their shape variation, e.g. residual analysis over the X-COP 12-cluster sample. The input profiles are themselves parametric NFW fits, so residuals against another NFW fit would be circular — use the nonparametric log-normal mixture reconstruction output instead. The goal is a mean/profile-average comparison with NFW or Einasto (the article already shows <10% average deviation); this skill targets per-cluster residual structure, not ensemble-averaged agreement. Hydrostatic equilibrium cannot be assumed, e.g. major mergers requiring nonthermal pressure support beyond the mild 10-20% marginalization hydromass provides. Quantifies how much shape diversity exists among individually recovered hydrostatic mass profiles of galaxy clusters beyond what an NFW parametric fit can represent, by computing per-cluster fractional residuals (M_recovered - M_NFW)/M_NFW. It operationalizes the X-COP finding that NFW describes average profiles to <10% deviation while individual profiles show residual structure. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202142507

The data are already partitioned or the number of clusters is fixed a priori — the CH sweep is a diagnostic for choosing k, not a clustering method itself The similarity measure between variables is not correlation-based, so the hierarchy being cut differs from AMADA's d(x,y)=1-|corr(x,y)| construction The dataset contains missing values not encoded as NA, since AMADA requires NA marking for missing data before analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduces AMADA's mechanism for guiding the choice of cluster count: the Calinski and Harabasz (1972) index is computed (via the R fpc package) for each candidate partition obtained by cutting the hierarchical clustering tree, and the argmax k is reported to the user as the optimal number of clusters. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.06.006
skills.summary: Reproduces AMADA's mechanism for guiding the choice of cluster count: the Calinski and Harabasz (1972) index is computed (via the R fpc package) for each candidate partition obtained by cutting the hierarchical clustering tree, and the argmax k is reported to the user as the optimal number of clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already partitioned or the number of clusters is fixed a priori — the CH sweep is a diagnostic for choosing k, not a clustering method itself The similarity measure between variables is not correlation-based, so the hierarchy being cut differs from AMADA's d(x,y)=1-|corr(x,y)| construction The dataset contains missing values not encoded as NA, since AMADA requires NA marking for missing data before analysis

skills.description: Use when predicted BBN light-element abundances are available across a grid of eta_B values and you need to check consistency with the CMB-inferred baryon density and quasar absorption deuterium observations.
skills.name: cmb-baryon-density-constraint-comparison
skills.search_text: cmb-baryon-density-constraint-comparison Use when predicted BBN light-element abundances are available across a grid of eta_B values and you need to check consistency with the CMB-inferred baryon density and quasar absorption deuterium observations. The analysis targets New Physics scenarios active during BBN rather than the Standard Model baseline — use the BSM-capable workflow instead, since this skill reproduces the SM PDG benchmark. You need a single-point abundance prediction at one fixed cosmology rather than abundance curves as a function of eta_B with observational overlays. http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Overlays PRyMordial-predicted primordial abundance curves (helium-4, deuterium, helium-3, lithium-7) versus baryon-to-photon ratio eta_B with the CMB baryon-density constraint band, testing whether BBN predictions agree with the independently measured cosmic baryon density. astronomy/v1 10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-12442-0
skills.summary: Overlays PRyMordial-predicted primordial abundance curves (helium-4, deuterium, helium-3, lithium-7) versus baryon-to-photon ratio eta_B with the CMB baryon-density constraint band, testing whether BBN predictions agree with the independently measured cosmic baryon density.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets New Physics scenarios active during BBN rather than the Standard Model baseline — use the BSM-capable workflow instead, since this skill reproduces the SM PDG benchmark. You need a single-point abundance prediction at one fixed cosmology rather than abundance curves as a function of eta_B with observational overlays.

skills.description: Use when the input is a HEALPix FITS sky map from a CMB polarimeter (I, Q, U at Nside 512) and the goal is to extract, inspect, or cut out regions (e.g. 5-degree patches around Tau A) for photometry or comparison.
skills.name: cmb-map-fits-data-handling
skills.search_text: cmb-map-fits-data-handling Use when the input is a HEALPix FITS sky map from a CMB polarimeter (I, Q, U at Nside 512) and the goal is to extract, inspect, or cut out regions (e.g. 5-degree patches around Tau A) for photometry or comparison. Input is still raw polarimeter timestream data (HDF5 timelines) needing destriping rather than already-mapped FITS products — use the dst destriper pipeline instead The target source has significant U emission that must be measured — the Tau A workflow here explicitly skips U because it is too faint to detect Systematic effects such as gain variations or spin-synchronous effects dominate, since destriping/mapping alone cannot correct them and they must be handled before map-making http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Handles CMB polarimeter sky maps stored in HEALPix FITS format (e.g. the B-Machine 40 GHz destriped maps on Figshare), loading I/Q/U fields with healpy and preparing gnomonic patches for follow-on measurements such as Tau A aperture photometry. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Handles CMB polarimeter sky maps stored in HEALPix FITS format (e.g. the B-Machine 40 GHz destriped maps on Figshare), loading I/Q/U fields with healpy and preparing gnomonic patches for follow-on measurements such as Tau A aperture photometry.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw polarimeter timestream data (HDF5 timelines) needing destriping rather than already-mapped FITS products — use the dst destriper pipeline instead The target source has significant U emission that must be measured — the Tau A workflow here explicitly skips U because it is too faint to detect Systematic effects such as gain variations or spin-synchronous effects dominate, since destriping/mapping alone cannot correct them and they must be handled before map-making

skills.description: Use when a CMB polarimeter timestream (e.g. HDF5 with TIME/PHI/THETA/PSI/FLAG/TEMP/Q/U columns) contains 1/f correlated noise with knee frequency below the scan rate and you need a destriped I/Q sky map with minimal signal impact.
skills.name: cmb-mapmaking-destriping
skills.search_text: cmb-mapmaking-destriping Use when a CMB polarimeter timestream (e.g. HDF5 with TIME/PHI/THETA/PSI/FLAG/TEMP/Q/U columns) contains 1/f correlated noise with knee frequency below the scan rate and you need a destriped I/Q sky map with minimal signal impact. The timestream contains systematics destriping cannot handle — e.g. thermally induced gain variations near sunrise/sunset (mask those sections first) or spin-synchronous effects, which 'need to be dealt with before the map-making stage'. The 1/f noise knee frequency is higher than the scan rate, or the scanning strategy lacks frequent crossing points, so baseline-offset destriping cannot recover the correlated noise. The data are not from a polarimeter with Q/U modulation, since the method is specifically tailored to QU-only destriping for polarimeter data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 Map-making skill for CMB polarimeter data that removes low-frequency correlated (1/f) noise by fitting and subtracting 60-second baselines via Maximum Likelihood destriping, implemented in the parallel Python destriper 'dst' with Trilinos/GMRES, validated by reduced chi2 of residual maps against a plain binning baseline. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Map-making skill for CMB polarimeter data that removes low-frequency correlated (1/f) noise by fitting and subtracting 60-second baselines via Maximum Likelihood destriping, implemented in the parallel Python destriper 'dst' with Trilinos/GMRES, validated by reduced chi2 of residual maps against a plain binning baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The timestream contains systematics destriping cannot handle — e.g. thermally induced gain variations near sunrise/sunset (mask those sections first) or spin-synchronous effects, which 'need to be dealt with before the map-making stage'. The 1/f noise knee frequency is higher than the scan rate, or the scanning strategy lacks frequent crossing points, so baseline-offset destriping cannot recover the correlated noise. The data are not from a polarimeter with Q/U modulation, since the method is specifically tailored to QU-only destriping for polarimeter data.

skills.description: Use when polarimeter timestream data (e.g. HDF5 files with TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, Q, U columns) contains correlated 1/f noise to be removed via Maximum Likelihood destriping and the baseline amplitudes must be solved for.
skills.name: cmb-polarimeter-baseline-solving
skills.search_text: cmb-polarimeter-baseline-solving Use when polarimeter timestream data (e.g. HDF5 files with TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, Q, U columns) contains correlated 1/f noise to be removed via Maximum Likelihood destriping and the baseline amplitudes must be solved for. Systematic effects such as gain variations or spin-synchronous effects dominate the timestream — destriping can be ineffective or even harmful and these must be handled before map-making (e.g. sunrise/sunset sections with thermally induced gain variations were masked out) The scanning strategy lacks frequent crossing points, since destriping requires such a strategy to be effective http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Estimates the baseline array of the destriping equation for CMB polarimeter timelines by iteratively applying the left-hand operator with GMRES, avoiding inversion of the dense [n_b, n_b] matrix that is computationally infeasible even for modest datasets. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Estimates the baseline array of the destriping equation for CMB polarimeter timelines by iteratively applying the left-hand operator with GMRES, avoiding inversion of the dense [n_b, n_b] matrix that is computationally infeasible even for modest datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Systematic effects such as gain variations or spin-synchronous effects dominate the timestream — destriping can be ineffective or even harmful and these must be handled before map-making (e.g. sunrise/sunset sections with thermally induced gain variations were masked out) The scanning strategy lacks frequent crossing points, since destriping requires such a strategy to be effective

skills.description: Use when designing or re-binning a CMB power spectrum likelihood (e.g. SPT-3G TT/TE/EE or a mock data set in .yaml form) and you need to choose the band power bin width that minimises parameter sigma errors via Fisher forecasts.
skills.name: cmb-power-spectrum-band-binning
skills.search_text: cmb-power-spectrum-band-binning Use when designing or re-binning a CMB power spectrum likelihood (e.g. SPT-3G TT/TE/EE or a mock data set in .yaml form) and you need to choose the band power bin width that minimises parameter sigma errors via Fisher forecasts. When the goal is posterior sampling or best-fit optimisation rather than forecast errors — Fisher forecasts here assume a Gaussian likelihood around a fixed fiducial cosmology When the likelihood is not JAX-differentiable (e.g. non-candl likelihoods), since the method relies on exact Hessians and would otherwise require finite differences When bin width is already fixed by the published data release and cannot be re-tuned (rebinning requires access to window functions and un-binned model spectra) A Fisher-forecast-based optimisation that scans candidate CMB band power bin widths and selects the one minimising cosmological parameter errors, exploiting candl's JAX-differentiable likelihood for exact Hessians instead of finite differences. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202449432
skills.summary: A Fisher-forecast-based optimisation that scans candidate CMB band power bin widths and selects the one minimising cosmological parameter errors, exploiting candl's JAX-differentiable likelihood for exact Hessians instead of finite differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is posterior sampling or best-fit optimisation rather than forecast errors — Fisher forecasts here assume a Gaussian likelihood around a fixed fiducial cosmology When the likelihood is not JAX-differentiable (e.g. non-candl likelihoods), since the method relies on exact Hessians and would otherwise require finite differences When bin width is already fixed by the published data release and cannot be re-tuned (rebinning requires access to window functions and un-binned model spectra)

skills.description: Use when a CMB TT/TE/EE, BB, lensing (phiphi, kappakappa) likelihood must be evaluated (or differentiated) at a set of cosmological and nuisance parameters, e.g. Planck/SPT/ACT band-power data with .yaml likelihood files.
skills.name: cmb-power-spectrum-likelihood-evaluation
skills.search_text: cmb-power-spectrum-likelihood-evaluation Use when a CMB TT/TE/EE, BB, lensing (phiphi, kappakappa) likelihood must be evaluated (or differentiated) at a set of cosmological and nuisance parameters, e.g. Planck/SPT/ACT band-power data with .yaml likelihood files. The task requires non-CMB likelihoods or data types not supported by candl (primary CMB and lensing power spectra TT/TE/EE/BB/phiphi/kappakappa only) Planck plik-style likelihood files must be used directly without conversion — use clipy (pure-Python JAX-compatible clik replacement) instead Only a coarse goodness-of-fit scan is needed where differentiability and JAX overheads add no value and a 32-bit JAX architecture could introduce ~1e-4 log-likelihood differences http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Evaluate a CMB power spectrum likelihood with candl, a JAX-powered automatically differentiable Python likelihood, by initialising it from an index file (e.g. candl_data.SPT3G_2018_TTTEEE), passing model spectra through window-function binning and data-model transformations, and obtaining a log-likelihood value at a given parameter point. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202449432
skills.summary: Evaluate a CMB power spectrum likelihood with candl, a JAX-powered automatically differentiable Python likelihood, by initialising it from an index file (e.g. candl_data.SPT3G_2018_TTTEEE), passing model spectra through window-function binning and data-model transformations, and obtaining a log-likelihood value at a given parameter point.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires non-CMB likelihoods or data types not supported by candl (primary CMB and lensing power spectra TT/TE/EE/BB/phiphi/kappakappa only) Planck plik-style likelihood files must be used directly without conversion — use clipy (pure-Python JAX-compatible clik replacement) instead Only a coarse goodness-of-fit scan is needed where differentiability and JAX overheads add no value and a 32-bit JAX architecture could introduce ~1e-4 log-likelihood differences

skills.description: Use when you need linear CMB angular power spectra (TT/EE/TE D_l) from a cosmological model, especially when the spectra must be differentiable (ForwardDiff) or compared against CLASS/established Boltzmann codes.
skills.name: cmb-spectrum-computation
skills.search_text: cmb-spectrum-computation Use when you need linear CMB angular power spectra (TT/EE/TE D_l) from a cosmological model, especially when the spectra must be differentiable (ForwardDiff) or compared against CLASS/established Boltzmann codes. You only need the matter power spectrum P(k) over ks = 10^0.5–3.5 — use spectrum_matter instead of spectrum_cmb You need non-linear or lensed spectra, or fast reverse-mode AD of a scalar loss function — the paper states more work is needed for fast reverse-mode automatic differentiation and additional features A model component is not implemented in SymBoltz's src/models/ library and cannot be adapted from existing components Compute CMB temperature and polarization power spectra (D_l for TT, EE, TE) with SymBoltz by solving the approximation-free linear Einstein–Boltzmann equations and projecting with a cached spherical Bessel transform, enabling differentiable spectra validated against CLASS at the 0.1% level. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202557450
skills.summary: Compute CMB temperature and polarization power spectra (D_l for TT, EE, TE) with SymBoltz by solving the approximation-free linear Einstein–Boltzmann equations and projecting with a cached spherical Bessel transform, enabling differentiable spectra validated against CLASS at the 0.1% level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the matter power spectrum P(k) over ks = 10^0.5–3.5 — use spectrum_matter instead of spectrum_cmb You need non-linear or lensed spectra, or fast reverse-mode AD of a scalar loss function — the paper states more work is needed for fast reverse-mode automatic differentiation and additional features A model component is not implemented in SymBoltz's src/models/ library and cannot be adapted from existing components

skills.description: Use when a polarimeter timestream (HDF5 with TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, TEMP, Q, U columns) contains 1/f correlated noise below the scan rate that must be removed before map-making, e.g. for B-Machine 37.5 GHz or LATTE-like data.
skills.name: cmb-timestream-destriping
skills.search_text: cmb-timestream-destriping Use when a polarimeter timestream (HDF5 with TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, TEMP, Q, U columns) contains 1/f correlated noise below the scan rate that must be removed before map-making, e.g. for B-Machine 37.5 GHz or LATTE-like data. When systematic effects such as thermally induced gain variations (e.g. sections near sunrise/sunset) or spin-synchronous effects dominate — the article warns destriping can be ineffective or even harmful and these must be handled before the map-making stage When the correlated noise 1/f knee frequency is higher than the scan rate, or the scanning strategy lacks frequent crossing points, destriping cannot efficiently remove the noise When the goal is to remove signal components rather than noise — destriping is a high-pass filter that only affects the noise in the timestream http://edamontology.org/topic_0593 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Maximum Likelihood destriping of CMB polarimeter timestreams: solve the destriping equation for baseline offsets (60 s baselines, 2000 samples at 33.4 Hz) with GMRES via Trilinos Belos using the dst Python parallel destriper, removing low-frequency correlated noise while leaving sky signal intact. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Maximum Likelihood destriping of CMB polarimeter timestreams: solve the destriping equation for baseline offsets (60 s baselines, 2000 samples at 33.4 Hz) with GMRES via Trilinos Belos using the dst Python parallel destriper, removing low-frequency correlated noise while leaving sky signal intact.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When systematic effects such as thermally induced gain variations (e.g. sections near sunrise/sunset) or spin-synchronous effects dominate — the article warns destriping can be ineffective or even harmful and these must be handled before the map-making stage When the correlated noise 1/f knee frequency is higher than the scan rate, or the scanning strategy lacks frequent crossing points, destriping cannot efficiently remove the noise When the goal is to remove signal components rather than noise — destriping is a high-pass filter that only affects the noise in the timestream

skills.name: cmb-timestream-simulation
skills.search_text: cmb-timestream-simulation Use when validating a destriping pipeline with simulated polarimeter timelines: a signal-only timestream from a known input map, and a signal-plus-noise timestream with white variance and 1/f knee/slope from measured detector noise properties. The goal is to destripe or map real data — this skill only fabricates simulated input timelines; use the dst destriper instead The data contain systematic effects (thermally induced gain variations near sunrise/sunset, spin-synchronous effects) that must be masked or handled separately before map-making — simulation output does not model these Small angular scales matter — the 1-degree smoothing of the input WMAP Q-band map deliberately suppresses structure in map domain http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Generates simulated CMB polarimeter timestreams by scanning a smoothed WMAP 7-year Q-band map through the B-Machine pointing model, then optionally adding white plus 1/f correlated noise (n = Fa + w), serialized as a single HDF5 file readable by dst_io.read_data. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to destripe or map real data — this skill only fabricates simulated input timelines; use the dst destriper instead The data contain systematic effects (thermally induced gain variations near sunrise/sunset, spin-synchronous effects) that must be masked or handled separately before map-making — simulation output does not model these Small angular scales matter — the 1-degree smoothing of the input WMAP Q-band map deliberately suppresses structure in map domain

skills.description: Use when validating a destriped single-dish polarimeter map (e.g. B-Machine 37.5 GHz Q/U HEALPix maps): the measured spectrum must match the predicted white-noise variance so that excess power reveals residual correlated noise.
skills.name: cmb-white-noise-variance-prediction
skills.search_text: cmb-white-noise-variance-prediction Use when validating a destriped single-dish polarimeter map (e.g. B-Machine 37.5 GHz Q/U HEALPix maps): the measured spectrum must match the predicted white-noise variance so that excess power reveals residual correlated noise. When comparing maps observed on different sky cuts, since no cross-scale correlation correction is available and spectra are only comparable on the same cut When the map is dominated by sky signal rather than noise (e.g. foreground-contaminated or beam-smoothed maps where the white-noise null hypothesis does not hold) Before map-making: destriping limitations mean gain variations or spin-synchronous systematic effects must be handled separately and cannot be diagnosed by this white-noise comparison Computes the expected white-noise angular power spectrum of a partially observed CMB polarimetry map as C_l = Omega_pix * sigma^2 * f_samp / hits, and uses it as a null reference against which the measured EE/BB spectra (computed on the partial sky with HEALPix anafast and corrected by sky fraction) are validated. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Computes the expected white-noise angular power spectrum of a partially observed CMB polarimetry map as C_l = Omega_pix * sigma^2 * f_samp / hits, and uses it as a null reference against which the measured EE/BB spectra (computed on the partial sky with HEALPix anafast and corrected by sky fraction) are validated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing maps observed on different sky cuts, since no cross-scale correlation correction is available and spectra are only comparable on the same cut When the map is dominated by sky signal rather than noise (e.g. foreground-contaminated or beam-smoothed maps where the white-noise null hypothesis does not hold) Before map-making: destriping limitations mean gain variations or spin-synchronous systematic effects must be handled separately and cannot be diagnosed by this white-noise comparison

skills.description: Use when a study needs the coronal trajectory of one or more CMEs — final latitude, longitude, and tilt plus profiles vs. distance — from a magnetogram-derived PFSS background, with optional ensemble uncertainty quantification.
skills.name: cme-coronal-deflection-rotation-simulation
skills.search_text: cme-coronal-deflection-rotation-simulation Use when a study needs the coronal trajectory of one or more CMEs — final latitude, longitude, and tilt plus profiles vs. distance — from a magnetogram-derived PFSS background, with optional ensemble uncertainty quantification. The goal is interplanetary arrival time, expansion, or in situ profiles — use the ANTEATR (ANT) or FIDO components, or run models=ALL, rather than FC alone The CME of interest is a slow, streamer-blowout event: the default FCrmax of 10 Rs should not be used and ForeCAT's coronal window must be extended, so the stock configuration is inappropriate No suitable magnetogram/PFSS background exists for the eruption day and building one (30–60 min PFSS.py run) is infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Runs ForeCAT, the coronal component of OSPREI, to simulate how a CME deflects in latitude/longitude and rotates in tilt as it propagates through the PFSS-modeled background magnetic field out to FCrmax (default 10 Rs), optionally as an nRuns>1 ensemble. astronomy/v1 10.1029/2021sw002914

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is interplanetary arrival time, expansion, or in situ profiles — use the ANTEATR (ANT) or FIDO components, or run models=ALL, rather than FC alone The CME of interest is a slow, streamer-blowout event: the default FCrmax of 10 Rs should not be used and ForeCAT's coronal window must be extended, so the stock configuration is inappropriate No suitable magnetogram/PFSS background exists for the eruption day and building one (30–60 min PFSS.py run) is infeasible

skills.description: Use when validating that ForeCAT reproduces known coronal deflection/rotation behavior for specific CMEs — e.g., a near-radial CME should stay within ~0.5° of its seed latitude/longitude/tilt, while a deflecting CME shows multi-degree latitudinal and longitudinal displacement.
skills.name: cme-deflection-validation-against-observations
skills.search_text: cme-deflection-validation-against-observations Use when validating that ForeCAT reproduces known coronal deflection/rotation behavior for specific CMEs — e.g., a near-radial CME should stay within ~0.5° of its seed latitude/longitude/tilt, while a deflecting CME shows multi-degree latitudinal and longitudinal displacement. skills.summary: Runs ForeCAT (the coronal component of OSPREI) as a 100-member ensemble against a PFSS magnetic background to quantify coronal CME deflection and rotation, then validates the mean final latitude, longitude, and tilt against expected values (e.g., <0.5° from seed for undeflecting CMEs, ~9°N/12°E deflection for deflecting CMEs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need interplanetary propagation, arrival time, or in situ profiles — set models to ALL (or IP) rather than FC-only; ForeCAT ends at FCrmax (10 Rs default) and cannot address 1 AU behavior The case is a slow, streamer blowout CME with significant motion beyond 10 Rs — the FCrmax=10 Rs default is inappropriate per the README and must be increased No PFSS background exists for the eruption day and you cannot afford the ~30–60 min PFSS.py run — ForeCAT cannot run without the pickled magnetic field

skills.description: Use when you need predicted in situ profiles (B, Bz, velocity, Kp) at a spacecraft for a CME ensemble, not just an arrival time — e.g., reproducing geomagnetic-storm-relevant properties like max B and peak Kp within the sheath.
skills.name: cme-insitu-profile-simulation
skills.search_text: cme-insitu-profile-simulation Use when you need predicted in situ profiles (B, Bz, velocity, Kp) at a spacecraft for a CME ensemble, not just an arrival time — e.g., reproducing geomagnetic-storm-relevant properties like max B and peak Kp within the sheath. You only need a CME arrival time or speed estimate without magnetic field or Kp profiles — ANTEATR alone suffices. The CME can be treated as a hydrodynamic pressure pulse without an internal magnetic structure, since FIDO's value comes from forward-modeled flux rope in situ profiles. You need predicted in situ magnetic field components beyond a Parker Spiral orientation — the paper notes FIDO currently only assumes a Parker Spiral upstream direction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Simulate synthetic in situ magnetic field, velocity, and Kp profiles of a CME passing over a virtual spacecraft using OSPREI's FIDO component driven by ANTEATR/ForeCAT ensemble outputs, then validate the ensemble profiles (max B, most negative Bz, Kp timing) against OMNI observations. astronomy/v1 10.1029/2021sw002914
skills.summary: Simulate synthetic in situ magnetic field, velocity, and Kp profiles of a CME passing over a virtual spacecraft using OSPREI's FIDO component driven by ANTEATR/ForeCAT ensemble outputs, then validate the ensemble profiles (max B, most negative Bz, Kp timing) against OMNI observations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a CME arrival time or speed estimate without magnetic field or Kp profiles — ANTEATR alone suffices. The CME can be treated as a hydrodynamic pressure pulse without an internal magnetic structure, since FIDO's value comes from forward-modeled flux rope in situ profiles. You need predicted in situ magnetic field components beyond a Parker Spiral orientation — the paper notes FIDO currently only assumes a Parker Spiral upstream direction.

skills.description: Use when you have a ForeCAT far-corona terminal CME state (latitude, longitude, tilt, coronal speed) and need to propagate it through interplanetary space to predict arrival time, speed, size, and internal magnetic/thermal properties at a satellite.
skills.name: cme-interplanetary-propagation-simulation
skills.search_text: cme-interplanetary-propagation-simulation Use when you have a ForeCAT far-corona terminal CME state (latitude, longitude, tilt, coronal speed) and need to propagate it through interplanetary space to predict arrival time, speed, size, and internal magnetic/thermal properties at a satellite. The CME has not yet been simulated through the corona and you need deflection/rotation from the solar surface — run ForeCAT first, since ANTEATR takes the ForeCAT terminal state as its initial condition You need synthetic in situ profiles at a spacecraft (magnetic field vector, velocity, Kp) — that is FIDO's role; ANTEATR only propagates the CME and gives bulk/arrival properties You only need a quick coronagraph-based arrival time estimate without expansion, deformation, or internal properties — simple drag-based or WSA-ENLIL+Cone arrival models may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Simulates interplanetary CME propagation, expansion, and deformation with ANTEATR-PARADE (OSPREI's ANTEATR component, contained in PARADE.py), including drag toward the background solar wind and internal thermal/magnetic evolution, to predict arrival time at a satellite distance. astronomy/v1 10.1029/2021sw002914
skills.summary: Simulates interplanetary CME propagation, expansion, and deformation with ANTEATR-PARADE (OSPREI's ANTEATR component, contained in PARADE.py), including drag toward the background solar wind and internal thermal/magnetic evolution, to predict arrival time at a satellite distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CME has not yet been simulated through the corona and you need deflection/rotation from the solar surface — run ForeCAT first, since ANTEATR takes the ForeCAT terminal state as its initial condition You need synthetic in situ profiles at a spacecraft (magnetic field vector, velocity, Kp) — that is FIDO's role; ANTEATR only propagates the CME and gives bulk/arrival properties You only need a quick coronagraph-based arrival time estimate without expansion, deformation, or internal properties — simple drag-based or WSA-ENLIL+Cone arrival models may suffice

skills.search_text: cme-trajectory-profile-visualization Use when OSPREI (or a ForeCAT/ANTEATR/FIDO ensemble or single run) has produced standardized output data files and you need automated, forecast-ready figures of CME trajectories, parameter profiles, histograms, and ensemble statistics. You only need the underlying numeric data — the standardized output files and results object can be used directly without generating figures Quick turnaround during testing — contour plots and ensemble correlation plots are computationally expensive and should be skipped, not waited on http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 OSPREI's post-processing routine (processOSPREI.py) converts the standardized output data files from ForeCAT, ANTEATR, and FIDO runs into user-friendly figures — profiles of parameters versus distance, histograms, in situ probability contour plots, ensemble correlation plots, and spatial/coronal trajectory maps — via a results object holding all simulation data. astronomy/v1 10.1029/2021sw002914

skills.name: cme-trajectory-sensitivity-interpretation
skills.search_text: cme-trajectory-sensitivity-interpretation Use when OSPREI ensemble output files (from '.ens'-configured runs, e.g., the 22 April and 09 May 2021 CMEs) need input-output correlation analysis to reveal which parameter uncertainties drive forecast outputs like arrival time, speed, and in situ properties. skills.summary: Computes and interprets input-output correlations from OSPREI ensemble runs of Sun-to-Earth CME simulations (ForeCAT + ANTEATR/PARADE + FIDO), identifying which varied input parameters and quantifiable outputs exceed a 0.5 correlation-magnitude cutoff for each CME case.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The run is a single simulation (nRuns = 1) with no ensemble spread — correlations across members are undefined The goal is a best-fit tuning of input parameters to match observations rather than uncertainty/sensitivity probing (the article explicitly avoids fine-tuning inputs) The analysis targets arrival-time error statistics against observational benchmarks (e.g., WSA-ENLIL + Cone comparisons) rather than internal ensemble input-output correlations

skills.name: co-depletion-correction-analysis
skills.search_text: co-depletion-correction-analysis Use when comparing modelled 12CO line fluxes with ALMA disc-survey flux/size samples and you must test whether CO depletion from initial conditions reconciles models with observations. When the question is disc size (887-micron radius) evolution specifically and the sample is already flux-complete — the flux-based approach mainly helps because samples increase by factor 1.3 (Lupus) when using fluxes instead of sizes. When computationally-expensive thermochemical modelling per disc is required and budgeted — this skill exists as a fast, semi-analytical alternative validated against DALI within a factor of three, not a replacement for detailed chemistry. When the available ALMA data are expected to discriminate viscosity vs MHD winds conclusively — the article notes the data have not yet given conclusive answers on the underlying disc evolution mechanism. A method for comparing semi-analytical 12CO flux models (viscous and MHD-wind tracks) against ALMA disc survey data (Lupus, Upper Sco) by bracketing CO-depletion uncertainty, which is the condition under which models and data agree. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202346164
