skills.name: dimension-6-operator-mixing-analysis
skills.search_text: dimension-6-operator-mixing-analysis Use when you have a vector-mediator simplified model defined by the mediator mass and high-energy couplings to SM fields, and you need low-energy couplings to u, d, s quarks and protons/neutrons for direct detection. The model is not a vector-mediator simplified DM model (e.g. scalar or fermion mediators) — runDM's RG evolution is built for dimension-6 operators in vector-mediator simplified models You already have the low-energy couplings and only need direct-detection limits — use a direct-detection code (e.g. interface to NRopsDD) rather than re-running the evolution You need RG running between arbitrary scales in a full UV-complete model rather than the mediator-mass-to-nuclear-scale running of vector-mediator couplings Evolve vector-mediator couplings from the mediator mass scale down to the nuclear energy scale using runDM, which runs the high-energy SM couplings while taking into account the mixing of all dimension-6 operators, and extract the low-energy direct-detection operator coefficients. astronomy/v1 10.1007/jhep08(2016)111
skills.summary: Evolve vector-mediator couplings from the mediator mass scale down to the nuclear energy scale using runDM, which runs the high-energy SM couplings while taking into account the mixing of all dimension-6 operators, and extract the low-energy direct-detection operator coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is not a vector-mediator simplified DM model (e.g. scalar or fermion mediators) — runDM's RG evolution is built for dimension-6 operators in vector-mediator simplified models You already have the low-energy couplings and only need direct-detection limits — use a direct-detection code (e.g. interface to NRopsDD) rather than re-running the evolution You need RG running between arbitrary scales in a full UV-complete model rather than the mediator-mass-to-nuclear-scale running of vector-mediator couplings

skills.description: Use when assembling sparse tau-method matrices for a 1D spectral PDE (e.g. Poisson with Dirichlet/Neumann BCs on x∈[-1,1]) and you need boundary conditions folded into the basis via recombination rather than ad-hoc constraint rows.
skills.name: dirichlet-basis-recombination
skills.search_text: dirichlet-basis-recombination Use when assembling sparse tau-method matrices for a 1D spectral PDE (e.g. Poisson with Dirichlet/Neumann BCs on x∈[-1,1]) and you need boundary conditions folded into the basis via recombination rather than ad-hoc constraint rows. The problem has no boundary conditions to encode in the basis (pure eigenvalue/periodic problems) — recombination rows would over-constrain the system. You need dense collocation-style matrices rather than banded pencil matrices; Dedalus's dense solve path (e.g. solve_dense for Mathieu eigenvalues) does not use this staged banded construction. Multi-dimensional problems where Chebyshev-U interleaving by mode does not directly apply without adaptation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Reconstructs Dedalus's sparse tau-method matrix assembly for the 1D Chebyshev Poisson problem (Eq. 19): converting derivative terms from Chebyshev T to ultraspherical U test bases, appending tau boundary rows for u(±1)=0, applying Dirichlet basis recombination, and interleaving rows/columns by mode to yield a fully banded pencil like Fig. 3. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.023068
skills.summary: Reconstructs Dedalus's sparse tau-method matrix assembly for the 1D Chebyshev Poisson problem (Eq. 19): converting derivative terms from Chebyshev T to ultraspherical U test bases, appending tau boundary rows for u(±1)=0, applying Dirichlet basis recombination, and interleaving rows/columns by mode to yield a fully banded pencil like Fig. 3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The problem has no boundary conditions to encode in the basis (pure eigenvalue/periodic problems) — recombination rows would over-constrain the system. You need dense collocation-style matrices rather than banded pencil matrices; Dedalus's dense solve path (e.g. solve_dense for Mathieu eigenvalues) does not use this staged banded construction. Multi-dimensional problems where Chebyshev-U interleaving by mode does not directly apply without adaptation.

The goal is conclusive determination of the underlying disc evolution mechanism (viscosity or MHD winds) — the article states available ALMA data have not given conclusive answers yet Computationally-expensive thermochemical modelling is feasible for the full disc population — the semi-analytical method exists precisely because running DALI-like models for hundreds of discs is prohibitively time-consuming Compares semi-analytical 12CO flux models (viscous and MHD-wind evolutionary tracks) against ALMA-observed disc samples such as Lupus and Upper Sco, testing whether models and data agree only when CO depletion is included, and quantifying how sample sizes change when fluxes are used instead of disc sizes. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202346164

skills.description: Use when fitting a disc transit light curve attributed to a circumsecondary disc and you need to reduce the parameter space of disc size/orientation configurations by gradient-based rejection.
skills.name: disc-geometry-gradient-mapping
skills.search_text: disc-geometry-gradient-mapping Use when fitting a disc transit light curve attributed to a circumsecondary disc and you need to reduce the parameter space of disc size/orientation configurations by gradient-based rejection. The disc system does not have an azimuthally symmetric, non-uniform optical-depth profile — BeyonCE's rejection logic is defined for azimuthally symmetric disc structures The transit is caused by a bound circular companion or another eclipsing body rather than a circumsecondary disc transit (the method targets CSD transits like J1407 and PDS 110) http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Maps all possible circumsecondary disc geometries and computes the theoretical light-curve gradients for rings crossing the stellar disc, then rejects configurations whose measured light-curve gradient exceeds the theoretical gradient for that disc orientation. Implemented in the BeyonCE package and demonstrated on the J1407 and PDS 110 CSD transit light curves. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202245620
skills.summary: Maps all possible circumsecondary disc geometries and computes the theoretical light-curve gradients for rings crossing the stellar disc, then rejects configurations whose measured light-curve gradient exceeds the theoretical gradient for that disc orientation. The stellar system is not spherical or not in equilibrium — GravSphere2 is designed to mass-model systems of stellar tracers in equilibrium using spherical higher-order Jeans equations You only have binned/binned-summary kinematic data and need the older GravSphere + binulator workflow (justinread/gravsphere), not the bin-free individual-velocity fit You have very few tracers and need tight constraints — with only 100 tracers and no PMs, slope errors grow to ~30% (20%), so the 1000-tracer benchmark expectations do not apply Recover the logarithmic density slope at the half-light radius (R1/2) of a spherical dwarf galaxy mock using GravSphere2, a bin-free fourth-order spherical Jeans solver, and quantify the statistical slope error with and without proper motions. This skill operationalizes the paper's benchmark that 1000-tracer cuspy (cored) mocks yield 12% (25%) LOS-only slope errors, improving to 8% (12%) with PMs. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202557195
skills.summary: Recover the logarithmic density slope at the half-light radius (R1/2) of a spherical dwarf galaxy mock using GravSphere2, a bin-free fourth-order spherical Jeans solver, and quantify the statistical slope error with and without proper motions. This skill operationalizes the paper's benchmark that 1000-tracer cuspy (cored) mocks yield 12% (25%) LOS-only slope errors, improving to 8% (12%) with PMs.

The disk has not been solved yet — Mdot(R) only exists after tho.solve_disk(N=1e4); do not normalize unsolved or partially converged objects. You need absolute luminosities or thermal emission spectra rather than accretion-rate ratios; use pagn's calculate_lum_sum (Eq. 47 sums) instead. The configuration uses a custom Rout/Mdot_out/Rin triple rather than package defaults, in which case the reference normalization 26.29148 MSun/yr and the boundary values above do not apply without recomputation. Normalizes the radially varying accretion-rate profile Mdot(R) of a solved pAGN AGN disk by the Eddington accretion rate (Mdot_Edd ≈ 26.29148 MSun/yr for the Thompson et al. 2005 configuration), yielding a dimensionless profile anchored to boundary values such as Mdot(Rin) = 1.831417e-01 Mdot_Edd. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stae1117

skills.search_text: eigenphase-sum-resonance-analysis Use when a coupled-channel scattering calculation must locate a Feshbach or shape resonance via its signature in the eigenphase sum, e.g. two coupled Lennard-Jones channels with a closed upper channel shifted by ~100 cm-1. The target is bound-state energies rather than scattering resonances — use BOUND instead of the molscat eigenphase-sum scan. The goal is to locate a magnetic-field value at which a bound state exists at a specified energy — FIELD is designed for that, not an energy scan of the eigenphase sum. skills.name: eigenspectrum-spacing-and-mode-trapping-visualization
skills.search_text: eigenspectrum-spacing-and-mode-trapping-visualization Use when a computed wave eigenproblem must be checked against theoretical spectral regularities — constant frequency spacing of acoustic modes, constant period spacing of gravity modes — or when mode trapping regions must be visualized as eigenfrequency vs. horizontal wavenumber. The problem is a time-dependent initial-value simulation rather than a targeted sparse eigenvalue problem — use Dedalus's IVP solvers instead of solve_sparse. The eigenmodes cannot be organized into acoustic/gravity branches with identifiable frequencies near theoretical targets, since the spacing diagnostic requires mode identification per branch. Validation requires dense eigenvalue sweeps over all subproblems (e.g. small test problems like the Mathieu equation) rather than targeted sparse solves near a mode frequency. Computes linear wave eigenmodes of a stratified radiative atmosphere with Dedalus's sparse eigenvalue solver over 20 horizontal wavenumbers and visualizes the eigenspectrum to verify acoustic-mode frequency spacing, gravity-mode period spacing, and gravity-mode trapping in the isothermal upper layer. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.023068

skills.description: Use when equilibrium ionization fractions of H/He gas are needed for given (T, nH, nHe) but eliminating n_e from the implicit photo-collisional equilibrium equations yields an intractable high-order polynomial.
skills.name: electron-density-fixed-point-iteration
skills.search_text: electron-density-fixed-point-iteration Use when equilibrium ionization fractions of H/He gas are needed for given (T, nH, nHe) but eliminating n_e from the implicit photo-collisional equilibrium equations yields an intractable high-order polynomial. Non-equilibrium (time-dependent) ionization states are required — rabacus provides only equilibrium solvers; non-equilibrium solvers are a planned future improvement. Metal line cooling must be included in the thermal balance — it is not yet supported by the solvers. The problem already provides n_e directly or the system reduces to the closed-form pure-hydrogen case, making iteration unnecessary. Robust iterative fixed-point scheme (§4.2 of rabacus) that solves the coupled H/He equilibrium ionization rate equations by repeatedly evaluating ionization fractions (Eqs. 21-22), re-deriving the electron density n_e (Eq. 4), and iterating until changes in n_e fall below a tolerance, avoiding an explicit fourth-order polynomial in n_e with thousands of terms. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.004

Code calls native HDSv4 directly — it already reports through EMS, so there is no separate backend error stack to drain. The consumer does not use Starlink error handling (e.g. a pure-HDF5 reader such as h5py); forwarding into EMS provides no benefit there. A porting technique from the Starlink HDSv5 re-implementation (libhdsh5): every call into the HDF5 backend is guarded by an EMS status check, and on failure the HDF5 error stack is read and stored in the EMS error stack so Starlink applications see backend errors through their native error-handling convention. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.02.003

For tetraalkenylstannanes, where current hydrocarbon vapour pressure estimation methods proved less successful than for tetraalkylstannanes When no boiling point data are available for the compounds and entropy of vaporization is required — lack of appropriate Tb data is an explicit limitation in this study For triorganostannanes, where published vapour pressure data are sparse or vary considerably, so applicability of the relationship is uncertain http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Derives enthalpies (and, where boiling points exist, entropies) of vaporization for tetraorganostannanes by regressing log retention ratios against 1/T from isothermal GC data, anchored to a reference compound (Me4Sn, ΔHv = 31.28 kJ/mol). astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w

skills.description: Use when combining derived or literature ΔHv data for organostannanes and reference hydrocarbons into one dataset and testing descriptor choice (molecular weight vs intrinsic molar volume) via linear regression.
skills.name: enthalpy-of-vaporization-data-compilation
skills.search_text: enthalpy-of-vaporization-data-compilation Use when combining derived or literature ΔHv data for organostannanes and reference hydrocarbons into one dataset and testing descriptor choice (molecular weight vs intrinsic molar volume) via linear regression. When the target property is vapour pressure (lnP vs V) rather than enthalpy of vaporization — use the Equation 9 / vapour-pressure regression workflow instead When the descriptor of interest is molecular weight — the article shows MW relationships for hydrocarbons are distinct from (and inapplicable to) tetraorganostannanes When the dataset contains tetraalkenylstannanes only and no hydrocarbon reference points, since hydrocarbon-based estimation methods were less successful for tetraalkenylstannanes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compiles enthalpies of vaporization (ΔHv) for the seven tetraorganostannanes (Me4Sn, Vi4Sn, Et4Sn, Allyl4Sn, n-Pr4Sn, i-Pr4Sn, n-Bu4Sn) with literature hydrocarbon ΔHv values, and fits a single linear regression of ΔHv (kJ/mol) on intrinsic molar volume V (cm³/mol) to test whether organostannanes and hydrocarbons share one QSPR relationship. astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w
skills.summary: Compiles enthalpies of vaporization (ΔHv) for the seven tetraorganostannanes (Me4Sn, Vi4Sn, Et4Sn, Allyl4Sn, n-Pr4Sn, i-Pr4Sn, n-Bu4Sn) with literature hydrocarbon ΔHv values, and fits a single linear regression of ΔHv (kJ/mol) on intrinsic molar volume V (cm³/mol) to test whether organostannanes and hydrocarbons share one QSPR relationship.

skills.description: Use when you have per-compound enthalpies of vaporization from GC vapour-pressure data plus literature boiling points (Tb), and need ΔSv = ΔHv/Tb for Table 4-style comparisons across organostannanes and hydrocarbons.
skills.name: entropy-of-vaporization-derivation-from-boiling-points
skills.search_text: entropy-of-vaporization-derivation-from-boiling-points Use when you have per-compound enthalpies of vaporization from GC vapour-pressure data plus literature boiling points (Tb), and need ΔSv = ΔHv/Tb for Table 4-style comparisons across organostannanes and hydrocarbons. The compound has no literature boiling point — the article derives entropies only 'where appropriate boiling point information was available', so ΔHv/Tb cannot be populated and should be left blank rather than estimated. The analyte is a tetraalkenylstannane (e.g. Vi4Sn chemistry checks fail) and you intend to substitute hydrocarbon-based vapour-pressure estimation methods — the paper states these 'proved satisfactory for tetraalkylstannanes, but less successful for tetraalkenylstannanes'. The compound is solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) and you need solid-state vapour pressure — Equation (9) data require conversion using entropy of fusion (ΔSf) and melting point, which is beyond this skill's scope. Derives entropies of vaporization for tetraorganostannanes by dividing each compound's recomputed enthalpy of vaporization (from GC retention-ratio van't Hoff regressions anchored to Me4Sn at 31.28 kJ/mol) by its boiling point, yielding the ΔHv/Tb values (89.1–93.4 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹) reported in Table 4. astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w
skills.summary: Derives entropies of vaporization for tetraorganostannanes by dividing each compound's recomputed enthalpy of vaporization (from GC retention-ratio van't Hoff regressions anchored to Me4Sn at 31.28 kJ/mol) by its boiling point, yielding the ΔHv/Tb values (89.1–93.4 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹) reported in Table 4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound has no literature boiling point — the article derives entropies only 'where appropriate boiling point information was available', so ΔHv/Tb cannot be populated and should be left blank rather than estimated. The analyte is a tetraalkenylstannane (e.g. Vi4Sn chemistry checks fail) and you intend to substitute hydrocarbon-based vapour-pressure estimation methods — the paper states these 'proved satisfactory for tetraalkylstannanes, but less successful for tetraalkenylstannanes'. The compound is solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) and you need solid-state vapour pressure — Equation (9) data require conversion using entropy of fusion (ΔSf) and melting point, which is beyond this skill's scope.

skills.description: Use when you need fiducial EOB waveforms as training data for reduced-basis/empirical-interpolant surrogate building, or as a timing and accuracy baseline against a surrogate model.

skills.search_text: eob-waveform-generation Use when you need fiducial EOB waveforms as training data for reduced-basis/empirical-interpolant surrogate building, or as a timing and accuracy baseline against a surrogate model. You only need a fast waveform prediction for downstream analysis — load a pre-built surrogate via gwsurrogate.catalog.pull and gwsurrogate.LoadSurrogate instead of generating EOB-LAL waveforms directly The target binary is precessing or spans parameter regimes outside the nonspinning EOB training space described here (e.g. use NRSur7dq4 or SEOBNRv4PHMSur models instead) You lack the EOB-LAL code or license; offline surrogate building requires fiducial EOB generation that surrogate evaluation was designed to bypass http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Generates fiducial effective-one-body (EOB) gravitational waveforms — e.g. nonspinning BBH EOBNRv2 waveforms across mass ratios q in [1,10] and durations up to 10^5 M — using the EOB solver implemented in the LIGO Analysis Library (EOB-LAL code), serving as the training/validation backbone for reduced-basis surrogate construction. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevx.4.031006

skills.description: Use when you have a set of candidate EOSs each with a mass-radius curve and maximum mass M_TOV, and need to weight them by radio-timing pulsar mass posteriors and NICER M-R constraints as part of a Bayesian EOS-inference run.
skills.name: eos-likelihood-implementation
skills.search_text: eos-likelihood-implementation Use when you have a set of candidate EOSs each with a mass-radius curve and maximum mass M_TOV, and need to weight them by radio-timing pulsar mass posteriors and NICER M-R constraints as part of a Bayesian EOS-inference run. The analysis target is GW/kilonova/GRB afterglow parameter estimation (e.g. GW170817 light-curve fitting) rather than prior-weighting of a discrete EOS sample. You need a continuous EOS-parameter posterior rather than per-candidate-EOS weights; the pulsar/NICER terms here are evaluated per candidate EOS, not over EOS microphysical parameters. No EOS mass-radius curves are available — the likelihoods require R(m) and M_TOV for each candidate EOS to evaluate the truncation and the M-R posterior density. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Implements prior-weighting likelihoods for candidate neutron-star equation-of-state (EOS) samples within the NMMA framework: a Gaussian mass-only pulsar likelihood for PSR J0348+0432 and PSR J1614-2230 (truncated at each EOS's maximum mass M_TOV) plus a joint NICER mass-radius likelihood for PSR J0740+6620, so heavy-pulsar masses can constrain the EOS at densities beyond those probed by inspiral gravitational waves. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6
skills.summary: Implements prior-weighting likelihoods for candidate neutron-star equation-of-state (EOS) samples within the NMMA framework: a Gaussian mass-only pulsar likelihood for PSR J0348+0432 and PSR J1614-2230 (truncated at each EOS's maximum mass M_TOV) plus a joint NICER mass-radius likelihood for PSR J0740+6620, so heavy-pulsar masses can constrain the EOS at densities beyond those probed by inspiral gravitational waves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is GW/kilonova/GRB afterglow parameter estimation (e.g. GW170817 light-curve fitting) rather than prior-weighting of a discrete EOS sample. You need a continuous EOS-parameter posterior rather than per-candidate-EOS weights; the pulsar/NICER terms here are evaluated per candidate EOS, not over EOS microphysical parameters. No EOS mass-radius curves are available — the likelihoods require R(m) and M_TOV for each candidate EOS to evaluate the truncation and the M-R posterior density.

skills.description: Use when you have NMMA posterior samples from a multi-messenger fit (e.g., GW170817 strain + AT2017gfo photometry) and want to test whether adding another messenger (GRB170817A) shifts or tightens posteriors on R_1.4 and ejecta parameters.
skills.name: eos-posterior-comparison-across-analyses
skills.search_text: eos-posterior-comparison-across-analyses Use when you have NMMA posterior samples from a multi-messenger fit (e.g., GW170817 strain + AT2017gfo photometry) and want to test whether adding another messenger (GRB170817A) shifts or tightens posteriors on R_1.4 and ejecta parameters. You only have gravitational-wave data with no kilonova photometry — the comparison hinges on the GW+KN baseline that couples inclination to ejecta masses. The two posterior sets come from analyses with different priors, likelihoods, or samplers, making a credible-interval comparison invalid. You only have published point estimates (e.g., a single R_1.4 value) rather than posterior sample files in JSON/hdf5 format. Compares posterior samples of equation-of-state-relevant parameters (R_1.4, dynamical and wind ejecta masses, jet energy, inclination) between a GW+KN-only NMMA analysis and a joint GW+KN+GRB analysis, quantifying how adding GRB170817A information changes credible-interval widths. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6
skills.summary: Compares posterior samples of equation-of-state-relevant parameters (R_1.4, dynamical and wind ejecta masses, jet energy, inclination) between a GW+KN-only NMMA analysis and a joint GW+KN+GRB analysis, quantifying how adding GRB170817A information changes credible-interval widths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have gravitational-wave data with no kilonova photometry — the comparison hinges on the GW+KN baseline that couples inclination to ejecta masses. The two posterior sets come from analyses with different priors, likelihoods, or samplers, making a credible-interval comparison invalid. You only have published point estimates (e.g., a single R_1.4 value) rather than posterior sample files in JSON/hdf5 format.

skills.description: Use when you must extend a nuclear-physics-constrained EOS (chiral-EFT/AFDMC samples, valid to ~1.5 nsat) to supra-nuclear densities to obtain mass-radius-tidal-deformability families for neutron-star inference.
skills.name: eos-speed-of-sound-extension-modeling
skills.search_text: eos-speed-of-sound-extension-modeling Use when you must extend a nuclear-physics-constrained EOS (chiral-EFT/AFDMC samples, valid to ~1.5 nsat) to supra-nuclear densities to obtain mass-radius-tidal-deformability families for neutron-star inference. The input EOS is already valid across the full density range you need (no supra-nuclear extension required, e.g., EOS bands already tabulated beyond the chiral-EFT limit). The analysis target is kilonova/GRB afterglow light-curve modeling (nmma-generation, lightcurve-analysis entry points) rather than EOS construction. You need EOS constraints only below ~1.5 nsat, where the chiral-EFT band itself suffices without a speed-of-sound model. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs candidate neutron-star equations of state by combining a low-density band constrained by Quantum Monte Carlo calculations with chiral EFT interactions (up to 1.5 nsat) with a parametric speed-of-sound extension at higher densities, within the NMMA framework. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6
skills.summary: Constructs candidate neutron-star equations of state by combining a low-density band constrained by Quantum Monte Carlo calculations with chiral EFT interactions (up to 1.5 nsat) with a parametric speed-of-sound extension at higher densities, within the NMMA framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input EOS is already valid across the full density range you need (no supra-nuclear extension required, e.g., EOS bands already tabulated beyond the chiral-EFT limit). The analysis target is kilonova/GRB afterglow light-curve modeling (nmma-generation, lightcurve-analysis entry points) rather than EOS construction. You need EOS constraints only below ~1.5 nsat, where the chiral-EFT band itself suffices without a speed-of-sound model.

skills.description: Use when a joint GW + kilonova + GRB-afterglow analysis (e.g., GW170817/AT2017gfo/GRB170817A) needs a model afterglow lightcurve from a structured jet to fit observed afterglow flux-density data.
skills.name: equal-arrival-time-flux-integration
skills.search_text: equal-arrival-time-flux-integration Use when a joint GW + kilonova + GRB-afterglow analysis (e.g., GW170817/AT2017gfo/GRB170817A) needs a model afterglow lightcurve from a structured jet to fit observed afterglow flux-density data. The electromagnetic data are kilonova (e.g., AT2017gfo) photometry only — use the kilonova lightcurve models, not the afterglow jet model The analysis targets only the gravitational-wave signal or the EOS constraint without any GRB afterglow component A fully numerical (e.g., hydrodynamical) afterglow simulation is required rather than NMMA's semi-analytic Gaussian jet model Generates a synthetic GRB afterglow lightcurve in NMMA by evolving a Gaussian-structured relativistic jet blast wave (E(θ)=E0·exp(−0.5(θ/θc)²)) with lateral expansion and integrating emission over equal-arrival-time surfaces, producing a time/flux-density table used to fit the GRB170817A afterglow data. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6
skills.summary: Generates a synthetic GRB afterglow lightcurve in NMMA by evolving a Gaussian-structured relativistic jet blast wave (E(θ)=E0·exp(−0.5(θ/θc)²)) with lateral expansion and integrating emission over equal-arrival-time surfaces, producing a time/flux-density table used to fit the GRB170817A afterglow data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The electromagnetic data are kilonova (e.g., AT2017gfo) photometry only — use the kilonova lightcurve models, not the afterglow jet model The analysis targets only the gravitational-wave signal or the EOS constraint without any GRB afterglow component A fully numerical (e.g., hydrodynamical) afterglow simulation is required rather than NMMA's semi-analytic Gaussian jet model

skills.description: Use when a binary-neutron-star event has gravitational-wave data plus kilonova photometry and/or a GRB afterglow light curve, and the goal is a joint EOS/neutron-star-radius posterior rather than per-messenger analyses combined a posteriori.
skills.name: equation-of-state-constraint-analysis
skills.search_text: equation-of-state-constraint-analysis Use when a binary-neutron-star event has gravitational-wave data plus kilonova photometry and/or a GRB afterglow light curve, and the goal is a joint EOS/neutron-star-radius posterior rather than per-messenger analyses combined a posteriori. The event has only gravitational-wave data with no kilonova photometry or GRB afterglow — the joint analysis is designed to exploit the multi-messenger nature of compact-binary mergers, and the workflow steps (lightcurve-analysis, jet-model GRB fit) would be inapplicable. You want the GRB jet energy E0 itself to constrain the EOS — the article states no significant constraint is imposed by E0 because the ratio ξ between E0 and the disk mass mdisk is treated as a free parameter; the EOS constraint instead flows via inclination and kilonova ejecta masses. The target is a parameter-estimation run for a new astrophysical transient model rather than reusing the existing NMMA inference infrastructure — the article notes reliable interpretation requires advancing the models themselves, not just the parameter-estimation machinery. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reproduces the simultaneous multi-messenger inference of GW170817, kilonova AT2017gfo, and GRB170817A afterglow data within the NMMA framework, using chiral-EFT equation-of-state prior sets and the dynesty nested sampler, to constrain neutron-star matter (R of a 1.4 M⊙ star = 11.98 +0.35/-0.40 km). astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6
skills.summary: Reproduces the simultaneous multi-messenger inference of GW170817, kilonova AT2017gfo, and GRB170817A afterglow data within the NMMA framework, using chiral-EFT equation-of-state prior sets and the dynesty nested sampler, to constrain neutron-star matter (R of a 1.4 M⊙ star = 11.98 +0.35/-0.40 km).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The event has only gravitational-wave data with no kilonova photometry or GRB afterglow — the joint analysis is designed to exploit the multi-messenger nature of compact-binary mergers, and the workflow steps (lightcurve-analysis, jet-model GRB fit) would be inapplicable. You want the GRB jet energy E0 itself to constrain the EOS — the article states no significant constraint is imposed by E0 because the ratio ξ between E0 and the disk mass mdisk is treated as a free parameter; the EOS constraint instead flows via inclination and kilonova ejecta masses. The target is a parameter-estimation run for a new astrophysical transient model rather than reusing the existing NMMA inference infrastructure — the article notes reliable interpretation requires advancing the models themselves, not just the parameter-estimation machinery.

skills.name: equilibrium-condensation-simulation
skills.search_text: equilibrium-condensation-simulation Use when you need condensation sequences or 50% condensation temperatures (Tc) of elements/molecules from a stellar abundance pattern, or bulk compositions of rocky planets accreted from a feeding zone, e.g. testing metallicity or C/O sensitivity of Tc. skills.summary: Runs a T-p-dependent chemical equilibrium condensation simulation via Gibbs free energy minimisation using the ECCOplanets Python code, to derive condensation temperatures of planet-building elements and rocky planet bulk compositions from a given stellar elemental abundance pattern.

skills.name: equilibrium-photoionization-solver-execution
skills.search_text: equilibrium-photoionization-solver-execution Use when you need equilibrium ionization/temperature solutions for hydrogen and helium gas in a spherical geometry with a central point source, and when agreement with a Cloudy reference profile (e.g. Cloudy 13.03) must be quantified radius by radius. The problem requires metal line cooling — rabacus does not yet include metal line cooling (planned future improvement). Non-equilibrium (time-dependent) ionization evolution is needed — rabacus provides only equilibrium solvers; non-equilibrium solvers are planned future work. The geometry is not one of rabacus's supported cases (semi-infinite slab with isotropic background, spherical gas with central point source, spherical gas with isotropic background). Executes the rabacus equilibrium photoionization solver (Fortran 90 core wrapped in Python via f2py) to compute coupled H/He ionization fractions and temperatures, and validates the radial profiles against Cloudy 13.03 reference solutions such as the Friedrich et al. (2012) helium sphere test. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.004

(2012) helium sphere test.

skills.description: Use when comparing template-matching RV precision against DRS CCF uncertainties for ESPRESSO M-type spectra, or when validating an S-BART RV run against the paper's ~15 cm/s median uncertainty claim.
skills.name: espresso-ccf-rv-comparison
skills.search_text: espresso-ccf-rv-comparison Use when comparing template-matching RV precision against DRS CCF uncertainties for ESPRESSO M-type spectra, or when validating an S-BART RV run against the paper's ~15 cm/s median uncertainty claim. The goal is analyzing planetary or activity signals in the RV time-series — the paper explicitly leaves 'a full analysis of the planetary and activity signals present in the considered datasets for future work'. skills.search_text: fits-to-hdf5-data-model-mapping Use when converting FITS files (or MeasurementSets) into HDF5 while preserving the FITS data model of HDUs, header cards, image datasets, and binary-table columns. The target software stack only supports FITS — HDF5 is not well supported by data reduction software packages and image viewers; use this skill only when downstream tools can read HDF5 or you plan round-trip conversion back to FITS. You need features with no HDFITS equivalent yet, such as the FITS subtractive dithering technique, a specification for uncertainties, or columns of data with masked values. The data are arbitrary Python objects rather than FITS/MS scientific data — use hickle (HDF5-based pickle replacement) instead. Ports FITS files into the HDFITS HDF5 format using fits2hdf, preserving the FITS data model (HDUs, header cards as attributes, image and binary-table datasets) via CLASS attributes. Enables faster reads, better compression, and round-trip conversion back to FITS. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.05.001
skills.summary: Ports FITS files into the HDFITS HDF5 format using fits2hdf, preserving the FITS data model (HDUs, header cards as attributes, image and binary-table datasets) via CLASS attributes. Enables faster reads, better compression, and round-trip conversion back to FITS.

skills.description: Use when a ForeCAT terminal CME state (final latitude, longitude, tilt, coronal speed) must be propagated interplanetary space and the analysis needs internal flux rope properties (B, temperature) and expansion/deformation profiles, not just arrival time.
skills.name: flux-rope-internal-property-evolution
skills.search_text: flux-rope-internal-property-evolution Use when a ForeCAT terminal CME state (final latitude, longitude, tilt, coronal speed) must be propagated interplanetary space and the analysis needs internal flux rope properties (B, temperature) and expansion/deformation profiles, not just arrival time. The goal is coronal deflection/rotation from the solar surface — ForeCAT handles that regime; ANTEATR starts from the far corona (FCrmax) and needs an already-evolved terminal state. The CME is treated as a hydrodynamic pressure pulse with no internal magnetic structure — the internal thermal and magnetic evolution machinery would be moot. Only a single foreCAT-FIDO in situ profile at 1 AU is needed without propagation/expansion modeling — run FIDO directly rather than re-propagating. Runs the ANTEATR-PARADE component of OSPREI (fully contained in PARADE.py) to propagate a far-corona flux rope CME to the satellite distance while computing the evolution of its internal thermal and magnetic properties via conservation laws. This supplies arrival time plus expansion/deformation physics that simple drag-only arrival models omit. astronomy/v1 10.1029/2021sw002914

skills.description: Use when benchmarking long-range self-gravity for large particle systems, or when verifying that an FMM implementation scales linearly with particle count and quantifying its sensitivity to the MAC angle against a quadratic exact N-body baseline.
skills.name: fmm-gravity-force-computation
skills.search_text: fmm-gravity-force-computation Use when benchmarking long-range self-gravity for large particle systems, or when verifying that an FMM implementation scales linearly with particle count and quantifying its sensitivity to the MAC angle against a quadratic exact N-body baseline. Particle counts are small enough that exact N-body (quadratic) summation is affordable and maximum force accuracy is required. The analysis targets hydrodynamics problems without self-gravity (e.g., Sod shock tubes or Sedov blast waves), where FMM gravity is not exercised. The target runtime requires non-MPI backends (Legion or Kokkos node-level parallelism), which the current FleCSPH version does not support. Benchmark FleCSPH's fast multipole method (FMM) gravity against an exact N-body reference to demonstrate linear (or sublinear) versus quadratic scaling with particle count, and to characterize the strong dependence of FMM timing on the MAC angle. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.softx.2020.100602

skills.name: force-solver-configuration-treepm-fmm
skills.search_text: force-solver-configuration-treepm-fmm Use when validating two cosmological N-body codes (e.g. CONCEPT 1.0 vs gadget-4) against each other on the same initial conditions, or when diagnosing a scale- or time-dependent power discrepancy attributable to the gravitational force solver configuration. You need to compare performance/runtime rather than power-spectrum accuracy — CONCEPT is only several times faster than GADGET-2 for low to medium resolutions (k_Nyquist < 5 Mpc/h) and slower at higher resolution, so timing claims need the separate benchmarking protocol. The runs were not started from identical initial conditions or do not share box size/resolution — relative ratios then mix differences in ICs and sampling with solver differences. A simple additive formulation without interaction terms is used — the article states tests without interactions are 'inadequate in capturing the complexity of the data' The target variable is not strictly positive/continuous — the gamma family with log (or inverse power) link assumes this distributional form A k-fold cross-validation analysis of photo-z under/over-estimation is required — the authors state this is out of scope for this method http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Fit a gamma-family Generalized Linear Model with a log link to predict photometric redshifts from PCA-reduced galaxy magnitudes, using a factorial formula with interaction (crossing) terms so the model captures non-linear structure in the photometry. Delivers catastrophic outlier rates as low as ~1–2% within seconds on a desktop machine. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.002
skills.summary: Fit a gamma-family Generalized Linear Model with a log link to predict photometric redshifts from PCA-reduced galaxy magnitudes, using a factorial formula with interaction (crossing) terms so the model captures non-linear structure in the photometry. Delivers catastrophic outlier rates as low as ~1–2% within seconds on a desktop machine.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A simple additive formulation without interaction terms is used — the article states tests without interactions are 'inadequate in capturing the complexity of the data' The target variable is not strictly positive/continuous — the gamma family with log (or inverse power) link assumes this distributional form A k-fold cross-validation analysis of photo-z under/over-estimation is required — the authors state this is out of scope for this method

skills.name: gamma-ray-spectral-fitting
skills.search_text: gamma-ray-spectral-fitting Use when re-analyzing binned Fermi-LAT gamma-ray spectra of a blazar or AGN (e.g. NGC 1275) to search for ALP-induced spectral oscillations via an irregularity statistic rather than ALP model fitting. When the goal is to directly fit the observed spectrum with ALP models to obtain conversion-probability likelihoods — the paper explicitly adopts the irregularity method instead of that approach When the ALP-photon conversion probability itself must be computed (use the alpconv tool for that calculation, not this residual-scatter skill) http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Method for quantifying the irregularity of a gamma-ray spectrum (e.g. the Fermi-LAT observation of NGC 1275) by fitting a null-oscillation model and measuring the scatter of fit residuals, instead of directly fitting the spectrum with axion-like particle (ALP) models. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.physletb.2021.136611
skills.summary: Method for quantifying the irregularity of a gamma-ray spectrum (e.g. the Fermi-LAT observation of NGC 1275) by fitting a null-oscillation model and measuring the scatter of fit residuals, instead of directly fitting the spectrum with axion-like particle (ALP) models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to directly fit the observed spectrum with ALP models to obtain conversion-probability likelihoods — the paper explicitly adopts the irregularity method instead of that approach When the ALP-photon conversion probability itself must be computed (use the alpconv tool for that calculation, not this residual-scatter skill)

skills.search_text: gamma-ray-spectral-null-baseline-comparison Use when re-analyzing Fermi-LAT (or similar) blazar spectra for ALP-photon conversion effects with an irregularity method, where a no-oscillation reference spectrum must be built instead of fitting ALP models to the observed spectrum. skills.description: Use when you have radial/annular X-ray surface-brightness profiles (e.g. extracted with pyproffit) and need to deproject them into electron-density and thermodynamic profiles as input to hydrostatic mass reconstruction from X-ray and/or SZ data.
skills.name: gas-density-profile-reconstruction
skills.search_text: gas-density-profile-reconstruction Use when you have radial/annular X-ray surface-brightness profiles (e.g. extracted with pyproffit) and need to deproject them into electron-density and thermodynamic profiles as input to hydrostatic mass reconstruction from X-ray and/or SZ data. Input is already a deprojected 3D density/temperature profile — deprojection would be redundant; use hydromass mass-model fitting directly instead. No X-ray surface-brightness or SZ data are available (e.g. only weak-lensing shear catalogs) — the deprojection is defined for X-ray and/or Sunyaev-Zeldovich observations. You need purely 2D image analysis without annular binning — the skill requires radial annular profiles as extracted by pyproffit. Deprojects annular X-ray surface-brightness profiles (and optionally SZ pressure and spectroscopic temperature) into electron-density and thermodynamic gas profiles using the hydromass package's global Bayesian framework, including PSF deconvolution. This deprojection step supplies the density input needed for hydrostatic mass-profile reconstruction of galaxy clusters. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202142507
skills.summary: Deprojects annular X-ray surface-brightness profiles (and optionally SZ pressure and spectroscopic temperature) into electron-density and thermodynamic gas profiles using the hydromass package's global Bayesian framework, including PSF deconvolution. This deprojection step supplies the density input needed for hydrostatic mass-profile reconstruction of galaxy clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a deprojected 3D density/temperature profile — deprojection would be redundant; use hydromass mass-model fitting directly instead. No X-ray surface-brightness or SZ data are available (e.g. only weak-lensing shear catalogs) — the deprojection is defined for X-ray and/or Sunyaev-Zeldovich observations. You need purely 2D image analysis without annular binning — the skill requires radial annular profiles as extracted by pyproffit.

skills.name: gas-giant-atmospheric-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: gas-giant-atmospheric-composition-analysis Use when you need to map a giant planet's formation history (core mass, initial orbital distance, planetesimal ratio, dust grain fraction) to its final atmospheric C/O ratio and [(X/H)_planet]/[(X/H)_sun] metallicity. You need a self-consistent, physically detailed planet formation model with disk evolution and accretion physics — SimAb is explicitly a basic, fast, simplified model focused on atmosphere accretion of gas giants. The target is a terrestrial/icy planet rather than a gas giant: SimAb focuses on atmosphere accretion of gas giant planets. You only have the mature planet's observed atmosphere and want inversion of formation parameters — this skill runs the forward model; inversion (e.g., bounding initial orbital distance from C/O and metallicity) requires the paper's multi-run comparison workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Runs SimAb's single-simulation mode (Srun.py) to predict the final atmospheric composition (C/O ratio and metallicity) of a gas giant given specified formation initial conditions, and reads the resulting run_sum(n).txt composition summary. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202141455
skills.summary: Runs SimAb's single-simulation mode (Srun.py) to predict the final atmospheric composition (C/O ratio and metallicity) of a gas giant given specified formation initial conditions, and reads the resulting run_sum(n).txt composition summary.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a self-consistent, physically detailed planet formation model with disk evolution and accretion physics — SimAb is explicitly a basic, fast, simplified model focused on atmosphere accretion of gas giants. The target is a terrestrial/icy planet rather than a gas giant: SimAb focuses on atmosphere accretion of gas giant planets. You only have the mature planet's observed atmosphere and want inversion of formation parameters — this skill runs the forward model; inversion (e.g., bounding initial orbital distance from C/O and metallicity) requires the paper's multi-run comparison workflow.

skills.description: Use when a central point source ionizes a spherical hydrogen cloud and the analysis requires the effect of diffuse recombination photons rather than the on-the-spot approximation, e.g. reproducing the Raičević et al. (2014) Test 1 sphere.
skills.name: gauss-legendre-angular-quadrature-transfer
skills.search_text: gauss-legendre-angular-quadrature-transfer Use when a central point source ionizes a spherical hydrogen cloud and the analysis requires the effect of diffuse recombination photons rather than the on-the-spot approximation, e.g. reproducing the Raičević et al. (2014) Test 1 sphere. The problem geometry is a semi-infinite slab or a spherical gas in an isotropic background rather than a spherical gas with a central point source, since rabacus treats these as distinct problems Non-equilibrium ionization or metal line cooling is required — the paper states these are future improvements not yet included Only the on-the-spot approximation is needed, in which case the case B solver alone suffices without the N_mu=32 quadrature transport Solve equilibrium hydrogen ionization in a spherically symmetric, uniform-density Strömgren sphere with full transfer of isotropic recombination radiation, using rabacus with N_mu=32 Gauss-Legendre angle quadrature points, and benchmark against case A and on-the-spot (case B) solutions. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.004
skills.summary: Solve equilibrium hydrogen ionization in a spherically symmetric, uniform-density Strömgren sphere with full transfer of isotropic recombination radiation, using rabacus with N_mu=32 Gauss-Legendre angle quadrature points, and benchmark against case A and on-the-spot (case B) solutions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The problem geometry is a semi-infinite slab or a spherical gas in an isotropic background rather than a spherical gas with a central point source, since rabacus treats these as distinct problems Non-equilibrium ionization or metal line cooling is required — the paper states these are future improvements not yet included Only the on-the-spot approximation is needed, in which case the case B solver alone suffices without the N_mu=32 quadrature transport

skills.description: Use when simulating an astronomical image that needs realistic pixel-level noise after drawing a galaxy convolved with a PSF, e.g. reproducing demo1-style GalSim outputs with a fixed random seed.
skills.name: gaussian-noise-addition-to-fits-images
skills.search_text: gaussian-noise-addition-to-fits-images Use when simulating an astronomical image that needs realistic pixel-level noise after drawing a galaxy convolved with a PSF, e.g. reproducing demo1-style GalSim outputs with a fixed random seed. The image already contains noise, e.g. RealGalaxy images from the COSMOS catalog, where a noise-whitening procedure rather than fresh Gaussian noise is required. Correlated noise is needed, where whitening or symmetrizing an existing noise field is the correct operation instead of adding white Gaussian noise. The simulation is driven by a config file run through the galsim executable and noise should be specified declaratively rather than via the Python API. http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Adds Gaussian (white) noise to a GalSim-drawn galaxy image using image.addNoise with a galsim.GaussianNoise object at a specified sigma, then writes the result to a FITS file, replicating the deterministic demo1.py workflow. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.02.002
skills.summary: Adds Gaussian (white) noise to a GalSim-drawn galaxy image using image.addNoise with a galsim.GaussianNoise object at a specified sigma, then writes the result to a FITS file, replicating the deterministic demo1.py workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The image already contains noise, e.g. RealGalaxy images from the COSMOS catalog, where a noise-whitening procedure rather than fresh Gaussian noise is required. Correlated noise is needed, where whitening or symmetrizing an existing noise field is the correct operation instead of adding white Gaussian noise. The simulation is driven by a config file run through the galsim executable and noise should be specified declaratively rather than via the Python API.

skills.name: gaussian-prior-specification-cosmological-parameters
skills.search_text: gaussian-prior-specification-cosmological-parameters Use when running an MCMC posterior analysis of Big Bang Nucleosynthesis abundances where neutron lifetime and baryon density must be Gaussian-constrained and nuclear-rate uncertainties propagated log-normally. Uncertainties on tau_n, Omega_B h^2, or nuclear rates follow non-Gaussian/non-log-normal shapes that would require custom likelihood definitions rather than the reported prior choices. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Specifies the Gaussian priors on tau_n and Omega_B h^2 and log-normal priors on the 63 nuclear-rate nuisance parameters used to sample the BBN light-element abundance posterior in PRyMordial, enabling PRIMAT-vs-NACRE II uncertainty propagation. astronomy/v1 10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-12442-0

skills.search_text: gaussian-process-kernel-structure-learning Use when a time series (e.g., astronomical light curves of stellar variability or exoplanet transits) must be modelled with a Gaussian Process but no covariance function can be justified a priori, and accurate uncertainty estimation is required. When a physically motivated covariance function is already known and fixed-kernel GP regression suffices — structure learning is aimed at inferring the covariance structure from the series itself When the dataset is very large: the paper explicitly flags scalability to larger datasets (e.g., for missions such as PLATO) as future algorithmic work, not a current capability When the workflow requires non-JAX environments or Python < 3.10, since gallifrey depends on jax (>=0.5.0,<0.6.0) and Python 3.10+ http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Bayesian GP kernel structure learning in which the covariance function is inferred from the time series instead of specified explicitly: a prior is placed over kernel structures and hyperparameters, and the GP posterior is sampled with Sequential Monte Carlo whose transitions use a novel involutive MCMC procedure, implemented in gallifrey on JAX. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202554518

skills.description: Use when fitting RV timeseries (e.g. Barnard's star/GJ 699, HARPS-type instruments) where stellar activity or correlated noise may mimic planetary signals and competing noise models (jitter, moving-average, GP) must be compared by Evidence (ln Z).
skills.name: gaussian-process-noise-modelling
skills.search_text: gaussian-process-noise-modelling Use when fitting RV timeseries (e.g. Barnard's star/GJ 699, HARPS-type instruments) where stellar activity or correlated noise may mimic planetary signals and competing noise models (jitter, moving-average, GP) must be compared by Evidence (ln Z). The data show no evidence of correlated/stellar-activity noise and a simple jitter term suffices — adding a GP risks absorbing genuine Keplerian signals. The dataset is a single-planet, high-SNR signal with clean white noise (e.g. the 51 Peg test case), where noise-model competition adds complexity without benefit. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Model stellar-activity and instrumental correlated noise in radial velocity timeseries with a Gaussian Process (RotationTerm kernel via celerite2) alongside jitter and moving-average alternatives, so EMPEROR's Bayesian model comparison can select the optimal noise treatment. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202554336
skills.summary: Model stellar-activity and instrumental correlated noise in radial velocity timeseries with a Gaussian Process (RotationTerm kernel via celerite2) alongside jitter and moving-average alternatives, so EMPEROR's Bayesian model comparison can select the optimal noise treatment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data show no evidence of correlated/stellar-activity noise and a simple jitter term suffices — adding a GP risks absorbing genuine Keplerian signals. The dataset is a single-planet, high-SNR signal with clean white noise (e.g. the 51 Peg test case), where noise-model competition adds complexity without benefit.

skills.description: Use when 38-point-class HARPS RV time series show correlated stellar activity noise that a plain Keplerian fit cannot absorb, and joint modelling with TESS sectors plus ground-based transits (PEST, TRAPPIST-South) is needed to separate planetary signal from activity jitter.
skills.name: gaussian-process-stellar-activity-modelling
skills.search_text: gaussian-process-stellar-activity-modelling Use when 38-point-class HARPS RV time series show correlated stellar activity noise that a plain Keplerian fit cannot absorb, and joint modelling with TESS sectors plus ground-based transits (PEST, TRAPPIST-South) is needed to separate planetary signal from activity jitter. When the suspected signal origin is dilution by nearby contaminant stars rather than stellar activity — use the TESS-cont DILUTION analysis instead. When the target has no RV measurements and only transit photometry is available, so no mass/amplitude signal exists for the GP to disentangle. When a simple Keplerian plus white-noise model already fits the RVs with no correlated residuals, adding a GP over-parameterises the fit and degrades mass precision. A joint Bayesian inference recipe in which Gaussian-process activity terms are fitted simultaneously to HARPS radial velocities and TESS/ground-based transit photometry, with eccentric/circular, long-term-drift, and GP model variants discriminated via Bayesian evidence, to recover an unbiased planet mass and radius (as done for the super-Neptune TOI-5005 b). astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451656
skills.summary: A joint Bayesian inference recipe in which Gaussian-process activity terms are fitted simultaneously to HARPS radial velocities and TESS/ground-based transit photometry, with eccentric/circular, long-term-drift, and GP model variants discriminated via Bayesian evidence, to recover an unbiased planet mass and radius (as done for the super-Neptune TOI-5005 b).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the suspected signal origin is dilution by nearby contaminant stars rather than stellar activity — use the TESS-cont DILUTION analysis instead. When the target has no RV measurements and only transit photometry is available, so no mass/amplitude signal exists for the GP to disentangle. When a simple Keplerian plus white-noise model already fits the RVs with no correlated residuals, adding a GP over-parameterises the fit and degrades mass precision.

skills.description: Use when isothermal GC retention-time data (corrected against a reference such as natural gas) must be converted to vapour pressures, extrapolated below the measured temperature range (e.g. to 20°C from 40–120°C data), or related to molecular descriptors such as MW or intrinsic molar volume.
skills.name: gc-derived-vapour-pressure-data-analysis
skills.search_text: gc-derived-vapour-pressure-data-analysis Use when isothermal GC retention-time data (corrected against a reference such as natural gas) must be converted to vapour pressures, extrapolated below the measured temperature range (e.g. to 20°C from 40–120°C data), or related to molecular descriptors such as MW or intrinsic molar volume. The compounds are solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C): Equation (9) data must additionally be converted to solid vapour pressure using entropy of fusion (ΔSf) and melting point, so the liquid-phase regression is not directly applicable. Target compounds are triorganostannanes or other species with little or highly variable published vapour pressure data — the paper flags that applicability of the MW relationship (Equation 9) to such compounds is uncertain. You need to apply hydrocarbon MW-based relationships directly to organostannanes — the article states such MW relationships cannot be used with tetraorganostannanes, and hydrocarbon estimation methods underestimate tetraalkenylstannanes (e.g. Vi4Sn estimated 0.26/0.25 vs 0.35 kPa experimental). http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 A method for converting isothermal capillary GC retention times into equilibrium vapour pressures (relative to a reference compound such as tetramethylstannane), extrapolating them to 20°C, and regressing lnP against molecular weight or intrinsic molar volume for tetraorganostannanes. astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w
skills.summary: A method for converting isothermal capillary GC retention times into equilibrium vapour pressures (relative to a reference compound such as tetramethylstannane), extrapolating them to 20°C, and regressing lnP against molecular weight or intrinsic molar volume for tetraorganostannanes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The compounds are solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C): Equation (9) data must additionally be converted to solid vapour pressure using entropy of fusion (ΔSf) and melting point, so the liquid-phase regression is not directly applicable. Target compounds are triorganostannanes or other species with little or highly variable published vapour pressure data — the paper flags that applicability of the MW relationship (Equation 9) to such compounds is uncertain. You need to apply hydrocarbon MW-based relationships directly to organostannanes — the article states such MW relationships cannot be used with tetraorganostannanes, and hydrocarbon estimation methods underestimate tetraalkenylstannanes (e.g. Vi4Sn estimated 0.26/0.25 vs 0.35 kPa experimental).

skills.description: Use when a layered planetary interior model (radii, densities, shear moduli, viscosities) must be replaced by an effective homogeneous Voigt rheology for long-term orbital/spin evolution, or when a reduced model over a prescribed frequency range is needed.
skills.name: generalized-voigt-parameter-fitting
skills.search_text: generalized-voigt-parameter-fitting Use when a layered planetary interior model (radii, densities, shear moduli, viscosities) must be replaced by an effective homogeneous Voigt rheology for long-term orbital/spin evolution, or when a reduced model over a prescribed frequency range is needed. skills.summary: Extracts reported GPU-versus-single-CPU-core speedup values for the 13-, 9-, and 3-isotope astrophysical reaction networks (Tesla P100 vs. Power8 core on Summitdev) from a paper figure and serializes them, with scaling-limitation annotations, into a machine-readable CSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw simulation output or timing logs rather than an already-reported figure — re-deriving timings requires running the Maestro/Castro codes on Summitdev, not tabulating published values The target hardware is not the paper's Tesla P100 vs. single Power8 core setup, since the speedup values are hardware-specific and not transferable A single-network analysis is needed — this skill is structured around the three-network (13-, 9-, 3-isotope) comparison

skills.search_text: gradient-based-nuts-mcmc-sampling Use when you need posterior samples from a differentiable CMB power-spectrum likelihood (e.g. candl SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE) and want NUTS sampling driven by exact JAX gradients of the log-likelihood. When you only need parameter constraints and a gradient-free sampler via Cobaya or MontePython suffices, especially if the theory pipeline is not differentiable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Runs gradient-based Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (BlackJAX NUTS) over a JAX-differentiable CMB likelihood (candl) driven by a CosmoPower-JAX emulator, exploiting exact likelihood gradients instead of finite-difference or gradient-free samplers. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202449432
skills.summary: Runs gradient-based Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (BlackJAX NUTS) over a JAX-differentiable CMB likelihood (candl) driven by a CosmoPower-JAX emulator, exploiting exact likelihood gradients instead of finite-difference or gradient-free samplers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the likelihood is not JAX-differentiable (e.g. clik-based Planck likelihoods without clipy/JAX support) — NUTS requires exact gradients that cannot be obtained. When you only need parameter constraints and a gradient-free sampler via Cobaya or MontePython suffices, especially if the theory pipeline is not differentiable.

skills.description: Use when particles in a cosmological N-body snapshot (positions, velocities, masses) must be labelled bound vs unbound using only instantaneous information, without overdensity thresholds or iterative unbinding.
skills.name: gravitational-potential-topology-saddle-point-analysis
skills.search_text: gravitational-potential-topology-saddle-point-analysis Use when particles in a cosmological N-body snapshot (positions, velocities, masses) must be labelled bound vs unbound using only instantaneous information, without overdensity thresholds or iterative unbinding. The analysis requires overdensity-based halo definitions (e.g. FoF or spherical-overdensity thresholds) rather than the boosted-potential binding criterion — strawberry explicitly avoids ad hoc thresholds such as overdensity criteria. Only a subset of particles can be included in the potential calculation — the binding criterion's rationale requires the gravitational effect of all particles. Time-integrated or multi-snapshot orbit information is required — the criterion is deliberately instantaneous-only. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Classifies dark-matter particles as bound or unbound by computing the boosted potential (gravitational potential from an accelerated reference frame), identifying potential minima and the closest saddle points connecting to deeper minima, and comparing each particle's energy to the resulting escape energy — with no ad hoc thresholds such as overdensity criteria. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202556846
skills.summary: Classifies dark-matter particles as bound or unbound by computing the boosted potential (gravitational potential from an accelerated reference frame), identifying potential minima and the closest saddle points connecting to deeper minima, and comparing each particle's energy to the resulting escape energy — with no ad hoc thresholds such as overdensity criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires overdensity-based halo definitions (e.g. FoF or spherical-overdensity thresholds) rather than the boosted-potential binding criterion — strawberry explicitly avoids ad hoc thresholds such as overdensity criteria. Only a subset of particles can be included in the potential calculation — the binding criterion's rationale requires the gravitational effect of all particles. Time-integrated or multi-snapshot orbit information is required — the criterion is deliberately instantaneous-only.

skills.description: Use when you have gravitational-wave strain data plus electromagnetic counterpart observations (kilonova photometry, GRB afterglow light curves) and need joint posterior samples over EOS/ejecta parameters, or when comparing posteriors from nested analyses (e.g. GW+KN-only vs GW+KN+GRB).
skills.name: gravitational-wave-bayesian-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: gravitational-wave-bayesian-parameter-estimation Use when you have gravitational-wave strain data plus electromagnetic counterpart observations (kilonova photometry, GRB afterglow light curves) and need joint posterior samples over EOS/ejecta parameters, or when comparing posteriors from nested analyses (e.g. GW+KN-only vs GW+KN+GRB). The analysis goal is a single-messenger analysis only (e.g. kilonova light-curve fitting without GW data) — then lightcurve-analysis alone suffices and the GW likelihood machinery is unnecessary. You need tight EOS constraints driven by the jet energy: the paper finds 'no significant constraint on the EOS is imposed by the jet energy E0' because the ratio ξ between E0 and disk mass is a free parameter. Kilonova model physics fidelity (not parameter-estimation infrastructure) is the limiting factor — the paper flags limited physics input in kilonova and semi-analytic GRB models as a dominant uncertainty. Joint Bayesian parameter estimation of binary-neutron-merger observables (GW strain, kilonova light curves, GRB afterglow) using NMMA's nmma-analysis/lightcurve-analysis entry points with bilby as backend and dynesty nested sampling, yielding posteriors for ejecta masses, jet energy, inclination, and the neutron-star radius R_1.4. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6
skills.summary: Joint Bayesian parameter estimation of binary-neutron-merger observables (GW strain, kilonova light curves, GRB afterglow) using NMMA's nmma-analysis/lightcurve-analysis entry points with bilby as backend and dynesty nested sampling, yielding posteriors for ejecta masses, jet energy, inclination, and the neutron-star radius R_1.4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a single-messenger analysis only (e.g. kilonova light-curve fitting without GW data) — then lightcurve-analysis alone suffices and the GW likelihood machinery is unnecessary. You need tight EOS constraints driven by the jet energy: the paper finds 'no significant constraint on the EOS is imposed by the jet energy E0' because the ratio ξ between E0 and disk mass is a free parameter. Kilonova model physics fidelity (not parameter-estimation infrastructure) is the limiting factor — the paper flags limited physics input in kilonova and semi-analytic GRB models as a dominant uncertainty.

skills.name: greedy-reduced-basis-construction
skills.search_text: greedy-reduced-basis-construction Use when you have a dense training set of expensive fiducial waveforms (e.g., 501 EOBNRv2 (2,2)-mode waveforms with q in [1,2] generated by the EOB-LAL code) and need a surrogate whose greedy error decays exponentially so m << L basis elements suffice. Data are images or radio interferometric visibilities where bitshuffle is intended (good for radio astronomy data) rather than SDSS-style binary tables Lossy compression is acceptable — the paper explicitly did not compare lossy compression algorithms The file must remain directly readable by legacy FITS-only data reduction software or image viewers, since HDF5 is not well supported by those packages Benchmarks lossless compression of large binary-table FITS files by comparing FITS Rice (FPACK -table) against HDF5 chunked filters (LZF_SS and bitshuffle via fits2hdf), quantifying compression ratio and wall-clock time. It exploits the finding that the FITS data model ports straightforwardly to HDF5 with improved compression and faster reads. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.05.001
skills.summary: Benchmarks lossless compression of large binary-table FITS files by comparing FITS Rice (FPACK -table) against HDF5 chunked filters (LZF_SS and bitshuffle via fits2hdf), quantifying compression ratio and wall-clock time. It exploits the finding that the FITS data model ports straightforwardly to HDF5 with improved compression and faster reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are images or radio interferometric visibilities where bitshuffle is intended (good for radio astronomy data) rather than SDSS-style binary tables Lossy compression is acceptable — the paper explicitly did not compare lossy compression algorithms The file must remain directly readable by legacy FITS-only data reduction software or image viewers, since HDF5 is not well supported by those packages

skills.description: Use when you need to measure the single-core compute throughput of a chunked HDF5-based transform (e.g. rounding precision reduction) without confounding disk I/O, or to validate throughput claims against published MiB/s figures.
skills.name: hdf5-core-driver-in-memory-benchmarking
skills.search_text: hdf5-core-driver-in-memory-benchmarking Use when you need to measure the single-core compute throughput of a chunked HDF5-based transform (e.g. rounding precision reduction) without confounding disk I/O, or to validate throughput claims against published MiB/s figures. You want end-to-end disk I/O performance numbers — the core driver stores data only in memory and will overestimate real-world storage throughput You are benchmarking the full two-step scheme including Bitshuffle lossless compression — this skill isolates the rounding-only ('Rounding') condition with no subsequent lossless compressor The dataset is much larger than available RAM, since the core driver holds the whole file in memory Benchmarks write/read throughput of a data-processing step (e.g. the paper's precision-reduction rounding) by storing visibility data via HDF5's 'core' file driver so I/O is to memory only, isolating compute throughput from disk effects. Used to reproduce the paper's reported ~300 MiB/s single-core precision-reduction throughput. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.07.002
skills.summary: Benchmarks write/read throughput of a data-processing step (e.g. the paper's precision-reduction rounding) by storing visibility data via HDF5's 'core' file driver so I/O is to memory only, isolating compute throughput from disk effects. Used to reproduce the paper's reported ~300 MiB/s single-core precision-reduction throughput.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want end-to-end disk I/O performance numbers — the core driver stores data only in memory and will overestimate real-world storage throughput You are benchmarking the full two-step scheme including Bitshuffle lossless compression — this skill isolates the rounding-only ('Rounding') condition with no subsequent lossless compressor The dataset is much larger than available RAM, since the core driver holds the whole file in memory

skills.name: hdf5-dataset-access
skills.search_text: hdf5-dataset-access Use when opening Starlink HDS/NDF-format data through the HDF5-backed HDSv5 API (e.g. loading a large multi-GB dataset into GAIA) or when benchmarking load time and resident memory with datMap memory mapping enabled vs disabled. Input is a legacy HDS v4 file — migration of HDS v4 files to HDF5 is not addressed and HDSv5 cannot open them directly The goal is writing type-converted data through H5Dwrite directly — HDS string-to-numeric type conversion must happen in datPut before the HDF5 call, so raw H5Dwrite bypasses that behavior The workload relies on unsupported HDF5-native memory mapping of the dataset file (compression filters, type conversion) rather than the anonymous-mmap copy-back scheme Access and load scientific datasets through the HDSv5 layer that re-implements the Starlink Hierarchical Data System (HDS) API on top of HDF5, including evaluation of datMap memory-mapping behavior (anonymous mmap with copy-back on datUnmap) versus direct HDF5 dataset access. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.02.003

skills.description: Use when a user needs to benchmark lossless compression filters — FITS Rice, HDF5 LZF_SS, bitshuffle, GZIP — on synthetic random-integer image grids and reproduce a ratio-vs-time comparison table.
skills.name: hdf5-filter-compression-evaluation
skills.search_text: hdf5-filter-compression-evaluation Use when a user needs to benchmark lossless compression filters — FITS Rice, HDF5 LZF_SS, bitshuffle, GZIP — on synthetic random-integer image grids and reproduce a ratio-vs-time comparison table. The data are real astronomical (correlated) images rather than synthetic random integers — bitshuffle's gains depend on within-block structure and the paper's Table 1 values will not transfer A comparison of lossy compression algorithms is required — the article explicitly states 'we have not compared lossy compression algorithms' The goal is read-throughput benchmarking or data-model conversion (FITS <-> HDFITS) rather than compression ratio/time evaluation A benchmarking method for comparing lossless compression ratios and compression times of FITS Rice (FPACK via CFITSIO) against HDF5 filters (LZF_SS, bitshuffle, GZIP/deflate) on uniformly distributed random-integer images, as done in the HDFITS paper's Table 1. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.05.001
skills.summary: A benchmarking method for comparing lossless compression ratios and compression times of FITS Rice (FPACK via CFITSIO) against HDF5 filters (LZF_SS, bitshuffle, GZIP/deflate) on uniformly distributed random-integer images, as done in the HDFITS paper's Table 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real astronomical (correlated) images rather than synthetic random integers — bitshuffle's gains depend on within-block structure and the paper's Table 1 values will not transfer A comparison of lossy compression algorithms is required — the article explicitly states 'we have not compared lossy compression algorithms' The goal is read-throughput benchmarking or data-model conversion (FITS <-> HDFITS) rather than compression ratio/time evaluation

skills.search_text: hdfits-roundtrip-validation Use when converting FITS or MeasurementSet data into HDF5/HDFITS (or back) and you must verify the converted file is scientifically identical — e.g. before adopting HDF5 storage or benchmarking compression filters against the FITS baseline. The data are already stored as HDFITS and no FITS backwards-compatibility check is needed. You intend to apply genuinely lossy compression and expect bit-identical round-trip output — the paper's round-trip equivalence applies to the lossless HDF5 filter pipeline. Your goal is benchmarking HDF5 lossless filters against FPACK scaled-Rice on floating-point data only; that comparison requires a separate dithering-quantization filter, which the paper notes HDF5 'currently has no equivalent to'. Validate that astronomical data survives a FITS-to-HDFITS (HDF5) round trip by converting with fits2hdf's read_fits/export_hdf and read_hdf/export_fits paths and checking that datasets, headers, and (under lossless compression filters such as lzf, gzip, or bitshuffle) pixel values are reproduced exactly. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.05.001
skills.summary: Validate that astronomical data survives a FITS-to-HDFITS (HDF5) round trip by converting with fits2hdf's read_fits/export_hdf and read_hdf/export_fits paths and checking that datasets, headers, and (under lossless compression filters such as lzf, gzip, or bitshuffle) pixel values are reproduced exactly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already stored as HDFITS and no FITS backwards-compatibility check is needed. You intend to apply genuinely lossy compression and expect bit-identical round-trip output — the paper's round-trip equivalence applies to the lossless HDF5 filter pipeline. Your goal is benchmarking HDF5 lossless filters against FPACK scaled-Rice on floating-point data only; that comparison requires a separate dithering-quantization filter, which the paper notes HDF5 'currently has no equivalent to'.

skills.description: Use when you must support both legacy HDS v4 files and new HDF5-backed HDS v5 files behind one drop-in HDS API, and need a dispatch mechanism that routes each API call based on the locator's file version.
skills.name: hds-api-dispatch-wrapping
skills.search_text: hds-api-dispatch-wrapping Use when you must support both legacy HDS v4 files and new HDF5-backed HDS v5 files behind one drop-in HDS API, and need a dispatch mechanism that routes each API call based on the locator's file version. When migrating HDSv4 files to HDF5 is the goal — the README states 'I'm not yet worrying about migration of HDS v4 files to HDF5'; a conversion tool is a separate path When you only need to read/write HDF5-backed files directly (use the hds-v5 library itself rather than a dispatch wrapper) When the routines query low-level implementation details — per the article, a handful of such routines were not implemented Wraps the ~150 public HDS API routines so that each call is dispatched at runtime to the correct backend (native HDSv4 or the HDF5-based HDSv5) by inspecting a version integer stored as the first member of the shared HDSLoc locator struct. This lets the Starlink software run unmodified over either file format. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.02.003
skills.summary: Wraps the ~150 public HDS API routines so that each call is dispatched at runtime to the correct backend (native HDSv4 or the HDF5-based HDSv5) by inspecting a version integer stored as the first member of the shared HDSLoc locator struct. This lets the Starlink software run unmodified over either file format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When migrating HDSv4 files to HDF5 is the goal — the README states 'I'm not yet worrying about migration of HDS v4 files to HDF5'; a conversion tool is a separate path When you only need to read/write HDF5-backed files directly (use the hds-v5 library itself rather than a dispatch wrapper) When the routines query low-level implementation details — per the article, a handful of such routines were not implemented
