skills.name: multi-instrument-lightcurve-joint-fitting
skills.search_text: multi-instrument-lightcurve-joint-fitting Use when a planet (or multi-planet system) has transit light curves from more than one instrument (e.g. CHEOPS plus TESS sectors) and you need precise planetary radii and orbital periods before downstream modelling such as internal-structure inference. Only single-instrument photometry is available and no joint constraint across instruments is needed — the discovery-paper values may suffice, but note TESS-only radii for small, low-per-transit-SNR planets with large data gaps can deviate >3σ from the true value. The analysis goal is internal-structure/formation inference rather than radius/period retrieval — use the downstream plaNETic Bayesian internal-structure framework instead, feeding it the radii from this fit. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Jointly model transit photometry from multiple space telescopes — here 9.6 days of CHEOPS observations of HIP 29442 (TOI-469) combined with two TESS sectors — to derive per-planet radii and orbital periods with posterior uncertainties, improving precision over single-instrument fits. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202450472
skills.summary: Jointly model transit photometry from multiple space telescopes — here 9.6 days of CHEOPS observations of HIP 29442 (TOI-469) combined with two TESS sectors — to derive per-planet radii and orbital periods with posterior uncertainties, improving precision over single-instrument fits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only single-instrument photometry is available and no joint constraint across instruments is needed — the discovery-paper values may suffice, but note TESS-only radii for small, low-per-transit-SNR planets with large data gaps can deviate >3σ from the true value. The analysis goal is internal-structure/formation inference rather than radius/period retrieval — use the downstream plaNETic Bayesian internal-structure framework instead, feeding it the radii from this fit.

skills.description: Use when you have N transit light curves of the same planet observed under different conditions (instrument, filter, weather, cadence) and need joint system-parameter estimates with per-transit Tmid values and robust uncertainty comparison versus single-curve fits.
skills.name: multi-light-curve-simultaneous-transit-fitting
skills.search_text: multi-light-curve-simultaneous-transit-fitting Use when you have N transit light curves of the same planet observed under different conditions (instrument, filter, weather, cadence) and need joint system-parameter estimates with per-transit Tmid values and robust uncertainty comparison versus single-curve fits. You only have a single transit light curve — use TAP's single-curve mode instead of the multicurve locked-parameter mechanism You need to combine light curves by phase folding and rebinning — TAP is explicitly designed to avoid this, and folding would discard per-transit Tmid information The light curves require a transit model other than the Mandel and Agol (2002)/EXOFAST analytic form that TAP implements http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Simultaneously fit multiple transit light curves (e.g., long-cadence Kepler photometry) with TAP's MCMC engine, locking shared system parameters (P, a/Rs, Rp/Rs, i, Tmid) across curves while letting limb-darkening, wavelet-noise, and trend parameters evolve independently per curve, without phase folding or rebinning. astronomy/v1 10.1155/2012/697967
skills.summary: Simultaneously fit multiple transit light curves (e.g., long-cadence Kepler photometry) with TAP's MCMC engine, locking shared system parameters (P, a/Rs, Rp/Rs, i, Tmid) across curves while letting limb-darkening, wavelet-noise, and trend parameters evolve independently per curve, without phase folding or rebinning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single transit light curve — use TAP's single-curve mode instead of the multicurve locked-parameter mechanism You need to combine light curves by phase folding and rebinning — TAP is explicitly designed to avoid this, and folding would discard per-transit Tmid information The light curves require a transit model other than the Mandel and Agol (2002)/EXOFAST analytic form that TAP implements

skills.description: Use when a paper reports a parameter estimate (e.g., R_1.4) with asymmetric credible bounds from a joint analysis and you must verify a claimed precision improvement against Table 1-style literature baselines.
skills.name: multi-messenger-inference-uncertainty-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-messenger-inference-uncertainty-comparison Use when a paper reports a parameter estimate (e.g., R_1.4) with asymmetric credible bounds from a joint analysis and you must verify a claimed precision improvement against Table 1-style literature baselines. The parameter of interest has symmetric errors or no reported credible bounds, so upper-minus-lower width cannot be defined consistently across entries Baselines come from fundamentally different analyses (e.g., isolated NS X-ray measurements vs merger inference) whose credible intervals are not defined on comparable posterior assumptions The goal is point-estimate accuracy rather than precision comparison — width comparison says nothing about which central value is correct http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 A tabular comparison procedure for quantifying how much a joint multi-messenger Bayesian analysis (NMMA on GW170817 + AT2017gfo + GRB170817A) narrows the credible interval of a derived parameter — here the 1.4 solar-mass neutron-star radius R = 11.98 (+0.35/−0.40) km — relative to prior single- or partial-messenger literature baselines. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6
skills.summary: A tabular comparison procedure for quantifying how much a joint multi-messenger Bayesian analysis (NMMA on GW170817 + AT2017gfo + GRB170817A) narrows the credible interval of a derived parameter — here the 1.4 solar-mass neutron-star radius R = 11.98 (+0.35/−0.40) km — relative to prior single- or partial-messenger literature baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The parameter of interest has symmetric errors or no reported credible bounds, so upper-minus-lower width cannot be defined consistently across entries Baselines come from fundamentally different analyses (e.g., isolated NS X-ray measurements vs merger inference) whose credible intervals are not defined on comparable posterior assumptions The goal is point-estimate accuracy rather than precision comparison — width comparison says nothing about which central value is correct

skills.name: multi-sample-photo-z-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-sample-photo-z-comparison-analysis Use when benchmarking a photo-z method's catastrophic outlier rates (O(a): |zphot-zspec|>0.10; O(b): |zphot-zspec|/(1+zspec)>0.10) against published codes across simulated (PHAT0) and real (SDSS DR10) samples. The goal is to re-run the GLM photo-z fit itself rather than tabulate/compare already-reported metrics — use the CosmoPhotoz fitting workflow instead The comparison targets metrics not tabulated in the article (e.g., k-fold cross-validated under/over-estimation of photo-z), which the authors explicitly declare out of scope Only one sample and one method are involved, so a multi-sample, multi-code merged comparison table adds no value http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Assembles a merged comparison table of photometric-redshift quality metrics (bias, rms, catastrophic outlier rates) for the gamma-family GLM method versus published baseline photo-z codes (Le PHARE, BPZ, ANNz, TPZ, BMA), tabulated per sample (PHAT0, SDSS) and per number of retained PCs. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.002
skills.summary: Assembles a merged comparison table of photometric-redshift quality metrics (bias, rms, catastrophic outlier rates) for the gamma-family GLM method versus published baseline photo-z codes (Le PHARE, BPZ, ANNz, TPZ, BMA), tabulated per sample (PHAT0, SDSS) and per number of retained PCs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to re-run the GLM photo-z fit itself rather than tabulate/compare already-reported metrics — use the CosmoPhotoz fitting workflow instead The comparison targets metrics not tabulated in the article (e.g., k-fold cross-validated under/over-estimation of photo-z), which the authors explicitly declare out of scope Only one sample and one method are involved, so a multi-sample, multi-code merged comparison table adds no value

skills.description: Use when single-source ALP constraints from Fermi-LAT spectra exist for two or more blazars and the goal is a joint 95% CL exclusion region in the (gaγ, ma) plane that strictly enlarges each individual contour.
skills.name: multi-source-constraint-combination
skills.search_text: multi-source-constraint-combination Use when single-source ALP constraints from Fermi-LAT spectra exist for two or more blazars and the goal is a joint 95% CL exclusion region in the (gaγ, ma) plane that strictly enlarges each individual contour. Only one source observation is available — the irregularity method applied to a single source (e.g. NGC 1275 alone) is the appropriate single-source skill, not the combination procedure. The goal is model-fitting of the observed spectrum with ALP models rather than the irregularity-based statistical combination — the paper explicitly adopts the irregularity method 'instead of fitting the observed spectrum with ALP models'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Combines ALP exclusion regions from multiple Fermi-LAT source observations (e.g. NGC 1275 and PKS 2155-304) by merging their spectrum-irregularity statistics into a joint statistic, yielding a combined gaγ–ma exclusion contour stronger than either single source. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.physletb.2021.136611
skills.summary: Combines ALP exclusion regions from multiple Fermi-LAT source observations (e.g. NGC 1275 and PKS 2155-304) by merging their spectrum-irregularity statistics into a joint statistic, yielding a combined gaγ–ma exclusion contour stronger than either single source.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one source observation is available — the irregularity method applied to a single source (e.g. NGC 1275 alone) is the appropriate single-source skill, not the combination procedure. The goal is model-fitting of the observed spectrum with ALP models rather than the irregularity-based statistical combination — the paper explicitly adopts the irregularity method 'instead of fitting the observed spectrum with ALP models'.

skills.search_text: multi-step-flag-preservation-in-uv-data Use when reducing e-MERLIN interferometric visibility data where Lovell phase-calibrator stationary scans must be flagged after RFI and dropout flagging, with prior flags preserved. Input is a raw, unflagged uv dataset that has not yet been through SumThreshold RFI flagging and antenna zero-amplitude dropout flagging — this step is an additional, later stage in the SERPent sequence Data are from an array without Lovell telescope phase calibrator stationary scans, or are non-interferometric; SERPent targets radio interferometric array data and its Lovell-specific filter is e-MERLIN inherent behavior Goal is calibration or imaging rather than RFI/stationary-scan flagging of visibilities A discrete filtering step in the SERPent pipeline that flags Lovell telescope phase calibrator stationary scans — inherent to the e-MERLIN system — on top of SumThreshold RFI flagging and antenna zero-amplitude dropout flagging, without disturbing the existing flag table entries. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.09.001
skills.summary: A discrete filtering step in the SERPent pipeline that flags Lovell telescope phase calibrator stationary scans — inherent to the e-MERLIN system — on top of SumThreshold RFI flagging and antenna zero-amplitude dropout flagging, without disturbing the existing flag table entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw, unflagged uv dataset that has not yet been through SumThreshold RFI flagging and antenna zero-amplitude dropout flagging — this step is an additional, later stage in the SERPent sequence Data are from an array without Lovell telescope phase calibrator stationary scans, or are non-interferometric; SERPent targets radio interferometric array data and its Lovell-specific filter is e-MERLIN inherent behavior Goal is calibration or imaging rather than RFI/stationary-scan flagging of visibilities

skills.name: multi-transit-simultaneous-fitting-with-locked-parameters
skills.search_text: multi-transit-simultaneous-fitting-with-locked-parameters Use when several transit light curves observed under different conditions (instrument, filter, weather) must be fit at once with shared system parameters but free per-transit mid-transit times. The orbit is genuinely eccentric and must be fitted — this configuration locks e=0 and omega=0, so eccentric solutions cannot be recovered You plan to phase fold or rebin the light curves — TAP was developed for simultaneous analysis with no need to phase fold and rebin, and this skill follows that configuration Only one light curve with no parameters to share is available — the skill's rationale is uniform simultaneous fitting across multiple transits observed under different conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Fit multiple transit light curves simultaneously in TAP with a shared set of system parameters (e=0, omega=0 locked) while leaving per-transit mid-transit times, wavelet noise parameters, and airmass extinction trends free, validated against published parameter sets such as Winn et al. (2009) WASP-4b. astronomy/v1 10.1155/2012/697967

(2009) WASP-4b.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The orbit is genuinely eccentric and must be fitted — this configuration locks e=0 and omega=0, so eccentric solutions cannot be recovered You plan to phase fold or rebin the light curves — TAP was developed for simultaneous analysis with no need to phase fold and rebin, and this skill follows that configuration Only one light curve with no parameters to share is available — the skill's rationale is uniform simultaneous fitting across multiple transits observed under different conditions

skills.description: Use when a synthetic (or real) multi-angle image series of a body must be turned into a 3-D model, and the reconstructed model must be validated against a reference shape model via point-deviation statistics.
skills.name: multi-view-stereo-mesh-reconstruction
skills.search_text: multi-view-stereo-mesh-reconstruction Use when a synthetic (or real) multi-angle image series of a body must be turned into a 3-D model, and the reconstructed model must be validated against a reference shape model via point-deviation statistics. Input is a single image or too few images — structure-from-motion/multi-view stereo requires multiple overlapping views from different angles; the paper's minimum validated sets are 25 (fly-by) and 53 (orbiting) images The goal is photorealistic image generation rather than 3-D model recovery — use SISPO's rendering capability alone without the OpenMVG/OpenMVS reconstruction chain Comet coma/dust-gas environment visualization is needed — that is ComaCreator's plugin role, not the reconstruction pipeline Reconstructs a dense 3-D mesh of a small solar system body from rendered pinhole-camera image series by running OpenMVG incremental structure-from-motion followed by OpenMVS multi-view stereo densification, then quantifying reconstruction error against the input shape model. This is the 3-D reconstruction case study enabled by SISPO's physically based image simulation pipeline. astronomy/v1 10.1371/journal.pone.0263882
skills.summary: Reconstructs a dense 3-D mesh of a small solar system body from rendered pinhole-camera image series by running OpenMVG incremental structure-from-motion followed by OpenMVS multi-view stereo densification, then quantifying reconstruction error against the input shape model. This is the 3-D reconstruction case study enabled by SISPO's physically based image simulation pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single image or too few images — structure-from-motion/multi-view stereo requires multiple overlapping views from different angles; the paper's minimum validated sets are 25 (fly-by) and 53 (orbiting) images The goal is photorealistic image generation rather than 3-D model recovery — use SISPO's rendering capability alone without the OpenMVG/OpenMVS reconstruction chain Comet coma/dust-gas environment visualization is needed — that is ComaCreator's plugin role, not the reconstruction pipeline

skills.description: Use when derived per-pixel scientific data (vector fields, height maps, normal components) must be packaged for streaming visualization via IIPImage-style tiled servers, or when full 32-bit floating point precision must survive channel mixing and compression.
skills.name: multichannel-tiff-encoding
skills.search_text: multichannel-tiff-encoding Use when derived per-pixel scientific data (vector fields, height maps, normal components) must be packaged for streaming visualization via IIPImage-style tiled servers, or when full 32-bit floating point precision must survive channel mixing and compression. Input imagery is display-oriented 8-bit RGB already gamma-encoded for browsers — the browser engines display gamma-encoded 8-bit images, so no scientific re-encoding value is added The goal is passive visualization of a static image; storing data as static 8-bit compressed images limits interaction to passive visualization, but there is no dynamic channel (normals/heights) to encode The source raster has no elevation or surface-gradient semantics — Horn (1981) gradient estimation and normal packing would be meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3372 Encodes derived scientific channels (e.g. per-pixel surface normals and heights for hillshading) into standard, tileable multi-resolution 32-bit TIFFs — normal XYZ vectors packed into a 3-channel 'color' TIFF and height into a separate 1-channel monochrome TIFF — so an IIPImage server can stream them to lightweight web clients. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2014.12.006
skills.summary: Encodes derived scientific channels (e.g. per-pixel surface normals and heights for hillshading) into standard, tileable multi-resolution 32-bit TIFFs — normal XYZ vectors packed into a 3-channel 'color' TIFF and height into a separate 1-channel monochrome TIFF — so an IIPImage server can stream them to lightweight web clients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input imagery is display-oriented 8-bit RGB already gamma-encoded for browsers — the browser engines display gamma-encoded 8-bit images, so no scientific re-encoding value is added The goal is passive visualization of a static image; storing data as static 8-bit compressed images limits interaction to passive visualization, but there is no dynamic channel (normals/heights) to encode The source raster has no elevation or surface-gradient semantics — Horn (1981) gradient estimation and normal packing would be meaningless

skills.description: Use when strong-scaling curves from AMReX-based simulations (Maestro/Castro) flatten or show non-monotonic upturns, and the goal is to attribute the behavior to the multigrid nodal solver or to hybrid MPI/OpenMP NUMA placement changes.
skills.name: multigrid-solver-scaling-limit-analysis
skills.search_text: multigrid-solver-scaling-limit-analysis Use when strong-scaling curves from AMReX-based simulations (Maestro/Castro) flatten or show non-monotonic upturns, and the goal is to attribute the behavior to the multigrid nodal solver or to hybrid MPI/OpenMP NUMA placement changes. The simulation is highly compressible and should run with Castro rather than Maestro, which is tuned for subsonic convective flows The scaling data are weak-scaling or per-node throughput curves with no MPI/OpenMP thread-configuration change to attribute artifacts to The goal is GPU- or many-core portability assessment of AMReX rather than MPI/NUMA strong-scaling analysis of the nodal multigrid solver Diagnoses the scaling ceiling of AMReX-based codes (e.g., Maestro on the 3-d X-ray burst problem) by isolating the multigrid nodal-projection solver as the dominant bottleneck at O(10^4) processors and attributing curve artifacts to MPI/OpenMP thread-configuration switches on NUMA nodes. astronomy/v1 10.1088/1742-6596/1031/1/012024
skills.summary: Diagnoses the scaling ceiling of AMReX-based codes (e.g., Maestro on the 3-d X-ray burst problem) by isolating the multigrid nodal-projection solver as the dominant bottleneck at O(10^4) processors and attributing curve artifacts to MPI/OpenMP thread-configuration switches on NUMA nodes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The simulation is highly compressible and should run with Castro rather than Maestro, which is tuned for subsonic convective flows The scaling data are weak-scaling or per-node throughput curves with no MPI/OpenMP thread-configuration change to attribute artifacts to The goal is GPU- or many-core portability assessment of AMReX rather than MPI/NUMA strong-scaling analysis of the nodal multigrid solver

skills.name: multivariate-target-density-simulation
skills.search_text: multivariate-target-density-simulation Use when benchmarking a multi-chain MCMC sampler (e.g. DE-MC) against a reference sampler on target distributions of known density, so that percentile-estimate MSE and sampling efficiency can be computed exactly. The target distribution is unknown (a real Bayesian posterior) — efficiency vs optimal-normal-jump RWM cannot be validated against known percentile values The parameter space is not real-valued continuous (e.g. discrete or one-dimensional updates) — outside the DE-MC real parameter space scope, where WinBUGS-style one-dimensional updates apply http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Constructs multivariate Normal and Student t3 target densities with unit variances and pairwise correlations of 0.5 (d = 5, 50, 100) as known-shape benchmark distributions for validating MCMC samplers such as DE-MC against single-chain random walk Metropolis. astronomy/v1 10.1007/s11222-006-8769-1
skills.summary: Constructs multivariate Normal and Student t3 target densities with unit variances and pairwise correlations of 0.5 (d = 5, 50, 100) as known-shape benchmark distributions for validating MCMC samplers such as DE-MC against single-chain random walk Metropolis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target distribution is unknown (a real Bayesian posterior) — efficiency vs optimal-normal-jump RWM cannot be validated against known percentile values The parameter space is not real-valued continuous (e.g. discrete or one-dimensional updates) — outside the DE-MC real parameter space scope, where WinBUGS-style one-dimensional updates apply

skills.description: Use when building an ultraviolet-to-millimetre photometric data table for galaxies whose SEDs will be fitted with radiative transfer models, and when mid-IR spectra (e.g. Spitzer) must be included at matched spectral resolution.
skills.name: multiwavelength-photometry-assembly
skills.search_text: multiwavelength-photometry-assembly Use when building an ultraviolet-to-millimetre photometric data table for galaxies whose SEDs will be fitted with radiative transfer models, and when mid-IR spectra (e.g. Spitzer) must be included at matched spectral resolution. The analysis goal is SED fitting with flexible energy-balance templates rather than exclusive radiative transfer model libraries — SMART was benchmarked as comparable in runtime to energy balance methods but fits exclusively with radiative transfer models. No pre-computed radiative transfer library exists at a resolution matching the available spectroscopy, so spectra cannot be resampled for joint fitting. Only spectroscopic data are available without the ultraviolet-to-millimetre photometry that defines the fitting basis. Assemble ultraviolet-to-millimetre multiwavelength photometry for galaxies (demonstrated on the 42 local ULIRGs of the HERUS sample) and optionally include mid-infrared spectroscopy, such as Spitzer spectra, resampled to the spectral resolution of pre-computed radiative transfer model libraries, so the combined data can be fitted with SMART's Bayesian MCMC SED-fitting code. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stae1141
skills.summary: Assemble ultraviolet-to-millimetre multiwavelength photometry for galaxies (demonstrated on the 42 local ULIRGs of the HERUS sample) and optionally include mid-infrared spectroscopy, such as Spitzer spectra, resampled to the spectral resolution of pre-computed radiative transfer model libraries, so the combined data can be fitted with SMART's Bayesian MCMC SED-fitting code.

No pre-computed radiative transfer library exists at a resolution matching the available spectroscopy, so spectra cannot be resampled for joint fitting. Only spectroscopic data are available without the ultraviolet-to-millimetre photometry that defines the fitting basis.

skills.name: multiwavelength-photometry-band-subset-degradation-analysis
skills.search_text: multiwavelength-photometry-band-subset-degradation-analysis Use when planning or interpreting radio galaxy surveys with poorer multi-wavelength coverage than LOFAR Deep Fields, and you need to know which photometric bands (especially far-infrared and radio) the classifier depends on. skills.search_text: neural-cde-training Use when training a model on irregularly or continuously indexed time-series data (e.g. 2D spiral classification, BIDMC vital-sign regression) where a CDE hidden state driven by an interpolated path is the target architecture. When the data is not a time series / control path (e.g. static feature tables) — a CDE has no continuous driving path to interpolate When natural cubic splines are the only interpolation available and top accuracy is required — the thesis reports neural CDEs using natural cubic splines produce slightly worse results than other interpolation schemes When you need logsignature preprocessing in JAX — at the time of writing there does not exist a JAX library for computing logsignatures; use the PyTorch/torchcde route instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains neural controlled differential equations (neural CDEs) on time-series tasks by interpolating irregularly sampled data into a continuous control path (Hermite cubic splines with backward differences, or log-signature preprocessing) and solving the CDE by reduction to an ODE with an adaptive-step solver. astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2202.02435
skills.summary: Trains neural controlled differential equations (neural CDEs) on time-series tasks by interpolating irregularly sampled data into a continuous control path (Hermite cubic splines with backward differences, or log-signature preprocessing) and solving the CDE by reduction to an ODE with an adaptive-step solver.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data is not a time series / control path (e.g. static feature tables) — a CDE has no continuous driving path to interpolate When natural cubic splines are the only interpolation available and top accuracy is required — the thesis reports neural CDEs using natural cubic splines produce slightly worse results than other interpolation schemes When you need logsignature preprocessing in JAX — at the time of writing there does not exist a JAX library for computing logsignatures; use the PyTorch/torchcde route instead

skills.search_text: neural-network-continuum-prediction Use when a headerless two-column spectrum (wavelengths in angstroms, flux) of an O–G type star needs an automated pseudo-continuum prediction before dividing out the continuum or applying spline corrections. Input wavelengths are in nanometers without changing --sampling from the default 0.05 to 0.005 Objects showing wide emission lines without switching to --weights emission Goal is manual inspection/correction of an already-normalised spectrum — use SUPPNET --path, which does not load SUPPNet Predict a pseudo-continuum for order-merged stellar spectra using SUPPNet, a fully convolutional neural network that is the core of the SUPPNet normalisation pipeline, prior to any smoothing-spline post-processing. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202141480
skills.summary: Predict a pseudo-continuum for order-merged stellar spectra using SUPPNet, a fully convolutional neural network that is the core of the SUPPNet normalisation pipeline, prior to any smoothing-spline post-processing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input wavelengths are in nanometers without changing --sampling from the default 0.05 to 0.005 Objects showing wide emission lines without switching to --weights emission Goal is manual inspection/correction of an already-normalised spectrum — use SUPPNET --path, which does not load SUPPNet

skills.description: Use when you need a parameters-to-log-likelihood function for CMB power-spectrum analyses (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE) that is end-to-end differentiable with JAX, avoiding slow Boltzmann solvers via a trained emulator.
skills.name: neural-network-emulator-likelihood-pipelining
skills.search_text: neural-network-emulator-likelihood-pipelining Use when you need a parameters-to-log-likelihood function for CMB power-spectrum analyses (e.g. SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE) that is end-to-end differentiable with JAX, avoiding slow Boltzmann solvers via a trained emulator. When the theory model cannot be emulated accurately by a trained neural-network emulator (no validated CosmoPower-JAX models for the parameter space) — use a Boltzmann solver interface such as candl.interface.get_CAMB_pars_to_theory_specs_func instead When the analysis requires exact Boltzmann-solver spectra rather than emulator-approximated C_l, since emulator truncation errors propagate into the likelihood http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Chains a differentiable neural-network emulator (CosmoPower-JAX) into a differentiable CMB likelihood (candl) so that a single JAX-differentiable function maps cosmological parameters to a log-likelihood, enabling Hessian-based Fisher forecasts and gradient-based sampling. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202449432
skills.summary: Chains a differentiable neural-network emulator (CosmoPower-JAX) into a differentiable CMB likelihood (candl) so that a single JAX-differentiable function maps cosmological parameters to a log-likelihood, enabling Hessian-based Fisher forecasts and gradient-based sampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the theory model cannot be emulated accurately by a trained neural-network emulator (no validated CosmoPower-JAX models for the parameter space) — use a Boltzmann solver interface such as candl.interface.get_CAMB_pars_to_theory_specs_func instead When the analysis requires exact Boltzmann-solver spectra rather than emulator-approximated C_l, since emulator truncation errors propagate into the likelihood

skills.description: Use when sampling or differentiating through a CMB likelihood requires fast, JAX-native theory spectra (e.g. gradient-based NUTS with BlackJAX) and a trained CosmoPower emulator for the target data set exists.
skills.name: neural-network-emulator-theory-spectra-prediction
skills.search_text: neural-network-emulator-theory-spectra-prediction Use when sampling or differentiating through a CMB likelihood requires fast, JAX-native theory spectra (e.g. gradient-based NUTS with BlackJAX) and a trained CosmoPower emulator for the target data set exists. The target parameter space or survey configuration has no pre-trained CosmoPower emulator — training a new emulator is a separate task Accurate Boltzmann-level spectra (e.g. via CAMB with candl.interface.get_CAMB_pars_to_theory_specs_func) are required and emulator accuracy is not acceptable The analysis pipeline is not JAX-based and CPU/GPU autodiff is unnecessary — a standard sampler with a non-differentiable theory code suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Replace an expensive Boltzmann-solver call with a pre-trained neural-network emulator (CosmoPower TT NN, TE PCAplusNN, EE NN) evaluated in JAX via CosmoPower-JAX, and wire it into candl's likelihood through candl.interface.get_CosmoPowerJAX_pars_to_theory_specs_func so cosmological parameters map directly to differentiable CMB power spectra. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202449432
skills.summary: Replace an expensive Boltzmann-solver call with a pre-trained neural-network emulator (CosmoPower TT NN, TE PCAplusNN, EE NN) evaluated in JAX via CosmoPower-JAX, and wire it into candl's likelihood through candl.interface.get_CosmoPowerJAX_pars_to_theory_specs_func so cosmological parameters map directly to differentiable CMB power spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target parameter space or survey configuration has no pre-trained CosmoPower emulator — training a new emulator is a separate task Accurate Boltzmann-level spectra (e.g. via CAMB with candl.interface.get_CAMB_pars_to_theory_specs_func) are required and emulator accuracy is not acceptable The analysis pipeline is not JAX-based and CPU/GPU autodiff is unnecessary — a standard sampler with a non-differentiable theory code suffices

skills.description: Use when a study needs to quantify computational cost of power-spectrum evaluation — e.g. justifying an analytic emulator for MCMC or large surveys by timing it against CAMB and BACCO on the same grid.
skills.name: neural-network-emulator-timing-comparison
skills.search_text: neural-network-emulator-timing-comparison Use when a study needs to quantify computational cost of power-spectrum evaluation — e.g. justifying an analytic emulator for MCMC or large surveys by timing it against CAMB and BACCO on the same grid. The goal is accuracy assessment rather than speed — use the paper's RMS fractional error analysis (0.2% over k = 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc) instead of timing benchmarks. The target is the nonlinear power spectrum or extended cosmologies (neutrino masses, w0, wa), which are covered by separate emulators (halofit_example.py, syren_new_example.ipynb) not by the linear LCDM timing comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Benchmarks the evaluation speed of the symbolic analytic linear power spectrum emulator (plin_emulated from symbolic_pofk) against the Boltzmann code CAMB and the neural-network-based emulator BACCO on a common cosmology/k grid, quantifying the reported ~950x and ~36x speedups. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202348811
skills.summary: Benchmarks the evaluation speed of the symbolic analytic linear power spectrum emulator (plin_emulated from symbolic_pofk) against the Boltzmann code CAMB and the neural-network-based emulator BACCO on a common cosmology/k grid, quantifying the reported ~950x and ~36x speedups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy assessment rather than speed — use the paper's RMS fractional error analysis (0.2% over k = 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc) instead of timing benchmarks. The target is the nonlinear power spectrum or extended cosmologies (neutrino masses, w0, wa), which are covered by separate emulators (halofit_example.py, syren_new_example.ipynb) not by the linear LCDM timing comparison.

skills.description: Use when you have observed stellar and planetary parameters (e.g. CHEOPS/TESS radii plus ESPRESSO/HIRES RVs) for planets of 0.5–15 M⊕ and need internal-structure posteriors without running the full BICEPS interior model directly.

skills.search_text: neural-network-surrogate-sampling Use when you have observed stellar and planetary parameters (e.g. CHEOPS/TESS radii plus ESPRESSO/HIRES RVs) for planets of 0.5–15 M⊕ and need internal-structure posteriors without running the full BICEPS interior model directly. skills.when_to_use_negative: Planet masses fall outside the validated 0.5–15 Earth-mass range of the trained BICEPS-surrogate networks You need physical forward-model outputs (e.g. detailed composition profiles) rather than fast posterior sampling — run BICEPS directly instead No GPU is available and computation time cannot be tolerated: CPU-only runs 'drastically increase the computation time and is not recommended'

skills.search_text: neural-ode-conditioning-parameter-encoding Use when building a neural ODE surrogate for PDR chemistry and you must decide which quantities (e.g. Av, G0, cosmic-ray rate, density vs abundances, temperature) are injected as conditioning parameters versus evolved as ODE features. When the emulator input is already fully encoded (e.g. a trained checkpoint being loaded for inference with src/neuralpdr/inference.py) — re-encoding is unnecessary When the target model is not an augmented/latent neural ODE surrogate for 3D-PDR chemistry (e.g. a purely feed-forward emulator with a flat input vector) When the dataset is the raw Zenodo download (v1/3pdr_dataset_8192.h5, v2/simulations.tgz) rather than a processed HDF5 file in data/processed/ http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encodes physical/chemical inputs for a NeuralPDR surrogate by splitting visual extinction, radiation field, cosmic ray ionisation rate and density as additional conditioning parameters of the Latent Augmented Neural ODE, while chemical abundances and temperature are passed as ordinary features. skills.description: Use when irregularly-sampled time series must be modelled with a latent ODE and the goal is to generate or forecast samples beyond the training time window (e.g. training on [0,3], testing on [0,12]).
skills.name: neural-ode-solver-configuration-jax
skills.search_text: neural-ode-solver-configuration-jax Use when irregularly-sampled time series must be modelled with a latent ODE and the goal is to generate or forecast samples beyond the training time window (e.g. training on [0,3], testing on [0,12]). The data is a fixed, regularly sampled grid with no irregular observation times and no need for extrapolation beyond the training window — a standard sequence model suffices The system of interest is a controlled/stochastic process best expressed as a neural CDE or neural SDE (the thesis treats these separately, e.g. neural SDEs solved with the reversible Heun method) Natural cubic spline interpolation is required for measurability — the thesis reports neural CDEs using natural cubic splines 'produce slightly worse results than those using other interpolation schemes' http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Configure and train a latent ODE in JAX/Diffrax (GRU encoder, neural ODE latent dynamics via diffeqsolve with Tsit5, Gaussian decoder) and validate its extrapolation to horizons longer than the training interval, e.g. decaying-oscillator series trained on [0,3] and sampled on [0,12]. astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2202.02435
skills.summary: Configure and train a latent ODE in JAX/Diffrax (GRU encoder, neural ODE latent dynamics via diffeqsolve with Tsit5, Gaussian decoder) and validate its extrapolation to horizons longer than the training interval, e.g. decaying-oscillator series trained on [0,3] and sampled on [0,12].
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is a fixed, regularly sampled grid with no irregular observation times and no need for extrapolation beyond the training window — a standard sequence model suffices The system of interest is a controlled/stochastic process best expressed as a neural CDE or neural SDE (the thesis treats these separately, e.g. neural SDEs solved with the reversible Heun method) Natural cubic spline interpolation is required for measurability — the thesis reports neural CDEs using natural cubic splines 'produce slightly worse results than those using other interpolation schemes'

skills.description: Use when you have a raw 3D-PDR dataset (HDF5 or simulations.tgz) from one of the v1/v2/v3 Zenodo deposits and need to train an emulator that reproduces chemical abundances, temperatures, and column density maps faster than the chemical solver.
skills.name: neural-ode-surrogate-training
skills.search_text: neural-ode-surrogate-training Use when you have a raw 3D-PDR dataset (HDF5 or simulations.tgz) from one of the v1/v2/v3 Zenodo deposits and need to train an emulator that reproduces chemical abundances, temperatures, and column density maps faster than the chemical solver. You only need inference or evaluation with an already-trained surrogate — use the inference workflow (inference.py with --dataset_path, --model_dir, --weights_file) instead of retraining Your chemistry model is not 3D-PDR photodissociation-region chemistry (densities, cosmic ray ionisation rates, Av, radiation field as parameters) — the LANODE was trained specifically on 3D-PDR output You want full end-to-end dataset preparation of all versions at once — scripts/data/workflow_setup_all.sh covers all three datasets rather than a per-version training run http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains Latent Augmented Neural ODE surrogate models to emulate the 3D-PDR photodissociation-region chemistry on three datasets of increasing complexity (v1 uniform 1D clouds, v2 varying-density clouds, v3 3D giant molecular cloud), producing checkpoints that enable fast GPU inference of chemical abundances and temperatures. astronomy/v1 10.1088/2632-2153/ade4ee
skills.summary: Trains Latent Augmented Neural ODE surrogate models to emulate the 3D-PDR photodissociation-region chemistry on three datasets of increasing complexity (v1 uniform 1D clouds, v2 varying-density clouds, v3 3D giant molecular cloud), producing checkpoints that enable fast GPU inference of chemical abundances and temperatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need inference or evaluation with an already-trained surrogate — use the inference workflow (inference.py with --dataset_path, --model_dir, --weights_file) instead of retraining Your chemistry model is not 3D-PDR photodissociation-region chemistry (densities, cosmic ray ionisation rates, Av, radiation field as parameters) — the LANODE was trained specifically on 3D-PDR output You want full end-to-end dataset preparation of all versions at once — scripts/data/workflow_setup_all.sh covers all three datasets rather than a per-version training run

skills.description: Use when irregularly sampled, long time series (e.g. BIDMC respiratory rate, heart rate, SpO2) must be modelled by a differential-equation-based regressor while taking integration steps much larger than the data sampling rate without discarding sub-step information.
skills.name: neural-rde-model-training
skills.search_text: neural-rde-model-training Use when irregularly sampled, long time series (e.g. BIDMC respiratory rate, heart rate, SpO2) must be modelled by a differential-equation-based regressor while taking integration steps much larger than the data sampling rate without discarding sub-step information. Data are short or densely and regularly sampled, so large integration steps are unnecessary and a standard neural CDE suffices The task requires an interpolation scheme with better measurability properties, e.g. rectilinear interpolation, rather than logsignature preprocessing Working in JAX: at the time of writing there does not exist a JAX library for computing logsignatures, so the PyTorch/torchcde route does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a neural RDE driven by a log-ODE preprocessed path (logsignatures of depth 2-3 over large integration steps) and benchmarks it against neural CDE and ODE-RNN baselines on the three BIDMC vital-sign regression datasets, targeting the reported ~10x wall-clock training speed-up. astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2202.02435
skills.summary: Trains a neural RDE driven by a log-ODE preprocessed path (logsignatures of depth 2-3 over large integration steps) and benchmarks it against neural CDE and ODE-RNN baselines on the three BIDMC vital-sign regression datasets, targeting the reported ~10x wall-clock training speed-up.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are short or densely and regularly sampled, so large integration steps are unnecessary and a standard neural CDE suffices The task requires an interpolation scheme with better measurability properties, e.g. rectilinear interpolation, rather than logsignature preprocessing Working in JAX: at the time of writing there does not exist a JAX library for computing logsignatures, so the PyTorch/torchcde route does not apply

skills.description: Use when the goal is to generate synthetic stochastic time series (e.g. Brownian-motion paths) whose distribution — including initial condition — matches a set of observed (t, y) trajectories, via adversarial training of a neural SDE generator.
skills.name: neural-sde-generative-adversarial-training
skills.search_text: neural-sde-generative-adversarial-training Use when the goal is to generate synthetic stochastic time series (e.g. Brownian-motion paths) whose distribution — including initial condition — matches a set of observed (t, y) trajectories, via adversarial training of a neural SDE generator. The target data is deterministic (noise-free ODE trajectories) where a plain neural ODE fit suffices rather than a stochastic generator The task is time-series prediction/forecasting rather than distribution matching — a neural CDE alone (without adversarial training) is the appropriate model http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a small SDE-GAN — a neural SDE generator driven by a Brownian control against a neural CDE discriminator with Lipschitz-constrained weights — to match the distribution of Brownian-motion time series including their initial condition, using Diffrax/JAX/Equinox. astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2202.02435
skills.summary: Train a small SDE-GAN — a neural SDE generator driven by a Brownian control against a neural CDE discriminator with Lipschitz-constrained weights — to match the distribution of Brownian-motion time series including their initial condition, using Diffrax/JAX/Equinox.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target data is deterministic (noise-free ODE trajectories) where a plain neural ODE fit suffices rather than a stochastic generator The task is time-series prediction/forecasting rather than distribution matching — a neural CDE alone (without adversarial training) is the appropriate model

skills.name: neutrino-decoupling-temperature-tracking
skills.search_text: neutrino-decoupling-temperature-tracking Use when a cosmology analysis requires a first-principles SM thermodynamic background (N_eff, neutrino energy density, thermal history) rather than assuming instantaneous neutrino decoupling or hardcoded N_eff values. When the analysis needs BBN light-element abundances (Yp, D/H) rather than the thermal background itself — that is a separate PRyMordial computation. When exploring beyond-the-SM scenarios with new decoupling physics — the default SM parameter set will not capture the New Physics sector. When a precomputed cosmoMC table suffices (e.g. PRyM_Yp_DH_cosmoMC_2023.dat) rather than a fresh integration of the coupled Boltzmann system. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Compute the Standard Model thermal background by solving the coupled Boltzmann equations for photon temperature T_gamma(t), neutrino temperature T_nu(t), and scale factor a(T_gamma) through the BBN epoch, yielding N_eff^SM = 3.044 and Omega_nu(rel) h^2 = 5.70e-6 with non-instantaneous neutrino decoupling included. astronomy/v1 10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-12442-0

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis needs BBN light-element abundances (Yp, D/H) rather than the thermal background itself — that is a separate PRyMordial computation. When exploring beyond-the-SM scenarios with new decoupling physics — the default SM parameter set will not capture the New Physics sector. When a precomputed cosmoMC table suffices (e.g. PRyM_Yp_DH_cosmoMC_2023.dat) rather than a fresh integration of the coupled Boltzmann system.

The Askaryan radio emission at the vertex has not yet been modelled — propagation follows, not replaces, the emission stage of the NuRadioMC chain You need detector response or trigger simulation — that stage is handled by NuRadioReco, which is used by NuRadioMC for detector and trigger simulation Radio emission from cosmic-ray air showers rather than in-ice neutrino vertex-to-antenna propagation is the goal Ray-trace every neutrino interaction vertex to every detector antenna in the ice using the NuRadioMC signal-propagation module, enumerating all valid ray-path solutions under the medium's refractive-index profile. skills.description: Use when a paper reports a 1.4M⊙ neutron-star radius with asymmetric credible intervals (e.g., R = 11.98 +0.35/−0.40 km) and you must benchmark it against prior literature values to verify a claimed precision improvement.
skills.name: neutron-star-radius-measurement-extraction
skills.search_text: neutron-star-radius-measurement-extraction Use when a paper reports a 1.4M⊙ neutron-star radius with asymmetric credible intervals (e.g., R = 11.98 +0.35/−0.40 km) and you must benchmark it against prior literature values to verify a claimed precision improvement. The paper reports only a single radius point estimate with symmetric errors and no credible-interval table — there is nothing to cross-compare widths against. The target is measuring a radius from raw GW/kilonova/GRB data with NMMA itself (run nmma-generation/nmma-analysis) rather than extracting and benchmarking already-published values. The quantity is not R_1.4 — e.g., tidal deformability, EOS constraints, or the Hubble constant — since Table 1 entries and widths are defined specifically for the 1.4M⊙ radius. http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Extracts and cross-compares credible-interval estimates of the 1.4 solar-mass neutron-star radius from Table 1 of the Pang et al. 2023 Nature Communications NMMA paper and prior literature, quantifying how joint GW (GW170817), kilonova (AT2017gfo), and GRB afterglow (GRB170817A) analysis narrows the R_1.4 constraint. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6
skills.summary: Extracts and cross-compares credible-interval estimates of the 1.4 solar-mass neutron-star radius from Table 1 of the Pang et al. 2023 Nature Communications NMMA paper and prior literature, quantifying how joint GW (GW170817), kilonova (AT2017gfo), and GRB afterglow (GRB170817A) analysis narrows the R_1.4 constraint.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The paper reports only a single radius point estimate with symmetric errors and no credible-interval table — there is nothing to cross-compare widths against. The target is measuring a radius from raw GW/kilonova/GRB data with NMMA itself (run nmma-generation/nmma-analysis) rather than extracting and benchmarking already-published values. The quantity is not R_1.4 — e.g., tidal deformability, EOS constraints, or the Hubble constant — since Table 1 entries and widths are defined specifically for the 1.4M⊙ radius.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to constrain fractional NP modifications of BBN-era weak n↔p conversion rates from percent-level PDG measurements of primordial helium-4 and deuterium, using PRyMordial predictions sampled with emcee.
skills.name: neutron-to-proton-born-rate-constraint-analysis
skills.search_text: neutron-to-proton-born-rate-constraint-analysis Use when the goal is to constrain fractional NP modifications of BBN-era weak n↔p conversion rates from percent-level PDG measurements of primordial helium-4 and deuterium, using PRyMordial predictions sampled with emcee. When the target is NP affecting thermonuclear reaction rates or the thermal history (e.g. N_eff, decoupling) rather than the weak n↔p Born conversion rates — the skill's parameter space and likelihood are specific to NP_delta_nTOp. When the analysis goal is a forward prediction of BBN abundances within the Standard Model (e.g. via the PRyMdemoSM notebook) rather than a Bayesian constraint on a BSM parameter. When the observational inputs are not percent-level primordial D/H and Y_p measurements with CMB-informed Omega_B h^2 priors — the few-percent bound is only meaningful against PDG-level precision data. A Bayesian workflow that uses PRyMordial's n↔p weak-conversion pipeline to place credible upper bounds on New Physics (NP) shifts of the Born neutron-to-proton rates by fitting primordial helium-4 (Y_p) and deuterium (D/H) abundances with emcee, reproducing the few-percent bound reported in the PRyMordial paper. astronomy/v1 10.1140/epjc/s10052-024-12442-0
skills.summary: A Bayesian workflow that uses PRyMordial's n↔p weak-conversion pipeline to place credible upper bounds on New Physics (NP) shifts of the Born neutron-to-proton rates by fitting primordial helium-4 (Y_p) and deuterium (D/H) abundances with emcee, reproducing the few-percent bound reported in the PRyMordial paper.

skills.description: Use when you have per-spectrum radial velocities (with uncertainties, drift and secular-acceleration columns) from a spectrograph's pipeline and need to quantify the instrument's night-to-night zero-point stability as an upper limit on RV precision.
skills.name: nightly-zero-point-estimation
skills.search_text: nightly-zero-point-estimation Use when you have per-spectrum radial velocities (with uncertainties, drift and secular-acceleration columns) from a spectrograph's pipeline and need to quantify the instrument's night-to-night zero-point stability as an upper limit on RV precision. When the goal is to detect or characterize planetary or stellar activity signals in the RV time series — the paper explicitly leaves a full analysis of the planetary and activity signals present in the considered datasets for future work, and the NZP scatter is only an upper-limit diagnostic. When RVs come from a pipeline whose output lacks the DRIFT and SA columns (e.g., non-SBART CCF or SERVAL outputs), since drift and secular-acceleration corrections are essential to the per-night offset computation. Estimates the nightly zero point (NZP) of an echelle spectrograph (ESPRESSO) from S-BART radial-velocity time series of 33 GTO targets by grouping drift-corrected, secular-acceleration-subtracted RVs per night and computing the inverse-variance-weighted scatter of the per-night offsets. The resulting weighted NZP scatter (~0.7 m/s here) serves as an upper limit on the instrument's attainable RV precision. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202142262
skills.summary: Estimates the nightly zero point (NZP) of an echelle spectrograph (ESPRESSO) from S-BART radial-velocity time series of 33 GTO targets by grouping drift-corrected, secular-acceleration-subtracted RVs per night and computing the inverse-variance-weighted scatter of the per-night offsets. The resulting weighted NZP scatter (~0.7 m/s here) serves as an upper limit on the instrument's attainable RV precision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to detect or characterize planetary or stellar activity signals in the RV time series — the paper explicitly leaves a full analysis of the planetary and activity signals present in the considered datasets for future work, and the NZP scatter is only an upper-limit diagnostic. skills.description: Use when a nonlinear PDE (e.g. nonlinear Schrodinger equation with a bright soliton) must be evolved on a graph of coupled 1D segments and you need to observe scattering at vertices and spreading across the full network over time.
skills.name: nls-network-simulation
skills.search_text: nls-network-simulation Use when a nonlinear PDE (e.g. nonlinear Schrodinger equation with a bright soliton) must be evolved on a graph of coupled 1D segments and you need to observe scattering at vertices and spreading across the full network over time. The problem is an eigenvalue calculation (e.g. Mathieu, Rayleigh-Benard growth rates, pipe-flow eigenvalues) — use Dedalus's solve_dense/solve_sparse paths rather than SBDF2 initial-value integration. The PDE is linear and single-domain, so no vertex continuity/Kirchhoff-flux coupling or nonlinear term is needed. You only need a steady spectral solve with no time evolution of a traveling excitation. Simulates nonlinear Schrodinger dynamics on a graph network by time-integrating a bright soliton placed on one edge with Dedalus's SBDF2 semi-implicit stepper, reproducing the paper's Fig. 10 vertex-scattering behavior where the excitation disperses into all network segments. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.023068
skills.summary: Simulates nonlinear Schrodinger dynamics on a graph network by time-integrating a bright soliton placed on one edge with Dedalus's SBDF2 semi-implicit stepper, reproducing the paper's Fig. 10 vertex-scattering behavior where the excitation disperses into all network segments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The problem is an eigenvalue calculation (e.g. Mathieu, Rayleigh-Benard growth rates, pipe-flow eigenvalues) — use Dedalus's solve_dense/solve_sparse paths rather than SBDF2 initial-value integration. skills.search_text: orbital-close-approach-time-series-computation Use when you need the finite, positive collision time between two bodies on intersecting Kepler orbits from their orbital elements, or when simulating a Keplerian system where collisions are rare and per-pair analytic collision times enable jumping from event to event. Interactions are not Keplerian two-body encounters: the article notes gravitational interactions between particles can only be treated as gravitational scattering or secular perturbation, at the cost of reduced time-step or accuracy Systems where collisions are frequent rather than rare — the event-jumping algorithm is motivated by systems like the Solar System where collisions are rare Full force-integration between particles is required, since the propagator jumps collision to collision rather than integrating gravitational interactions continuously http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Computes analytic collision/close-approach times between bodies on intersecting Kepler orbits by reducing the problem to finding the grid point between two parallel lines closest to the origin, solved via the continued fraction of the orbital-period ratio, enabling large time jumps in N-body Keplerian simulations. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202243754

skills.description: Use when integrating a second-order ODE with a high or rapidly varying oscillation frequency w(t) (e.g. Airy-type w(t)=sqrt(t) on t in [1,100]) where a plain Runge-Kutta solver would need prohibitively small steps to resolve each period.
skills.name: oscillatory-ode-adaptive-stepping
skills.search_text: oscillatory-ode-adaptive-stepping Use when integrating a second-order ODE with a high or rapidly varying oscillation frequency w(t) (e.g. Airy-type w(t)=sqrt(t) on t in [1,100]) where a plain Runge-Kutta solver would need prohibitively small steps to resolve each period. The ODE is not of the oscillatory form x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0, or w(t) varies rapidly relative to the integration timescale everywhere, so the WKB approximation is never valid and plain Runge-Kutta is the right choice The problem is a first-order or non-oscillatory ODE where standard integrators (e.g. scipy solve_ivp) already step efficiently Runs the oscode/pyoscode hybrid stepper, which dynamically alternates between Runge-Kutta steps and an embedded WKB approximation to integrate highly oscillatory ODEs like x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0, taking single steps that span many oscillation periods. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.013030
skills.summary: Runs the oscode/pyoscode hybrid stepper, which dynamically alternates between Runge-Kutta steps and an embedded WKB approximation to integrate highly oscillatory ODEs like x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0, taking single steps that span many oscillation periods.

skills.description: Use when numerically solving a second-order ODE with an oscillatory solution whose frequency w(t) varies slowly relative to the timescale of integration over at least part of the range (e.g. Airy, burst equation, or cosmological perturbation modes).
skills.name: oscillatory-ode-numerical-integration
skills.search_text: oscillatory-ode-numerical-integration Use when numerically solving a second-order ODE with an oscillatory solution whose frequency w(t) varies slowly relative to the timescale of integration over at least part of the range (e.g. Airy, burst equation, or cosmological perturbation modes). The frequency does not vary slowly relative to the integration timescale over any part of the range — the WKB approximation underlying the speedup is then invalid The ODE is not of the supported second-order oscillatory form x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 with scalar w(t) and g(t) A first-order multistep solver such as scipy.integrate would suffice because oscillations are cheap to resolve — oscode's benefit is skipping periods of high-frequency oscillation http://edamontology.org/topic_3369 Integrate second-order oscillatory ODEs of the form x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 with oscode/pyoscode, which dynamically switches between Runge-Kutta steps and a WKB approximation to skip many oscillation periods in one step. Validated against analytic references such as the Airy equation Ai(-t) and the burst equation cos(100*arctan(t)) at rtol=1e-4. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.013030
skills.summary: Integrate second-order oscillatory ODEs of the form x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 with oscode/pyoscode, which dynamically switches between Runge-Kutta steps and a WKB approximation to skip many oscillation periods in one step. Validated against analytic references such as the Airy equation Ai(-t) and the burst equation cos(100*arctan(t)) at rtol=1e-4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The frequency does not vary slowly relative to the integration timescale over any part of the range — the WKB approximation underlying the speedup is then invalid The ODE is not of the supported second-order oscillatory form x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 with scalar w(t) and g(t) A first-order multistep solver such as scipy.integrate would suffice because oscillations are cheap to resolve — oscode's benefit is skipping periods of high-frequency oscillation

skills.search_text: per-order-rv-weighted-average-combination Use when deriving an RV time series from echelle spectra (e.g., HARPS S2D) with the classical template-matching formulation, or when establishing a per-order baseline to diagnose whether a semi-Bayesian approach is needed. When the goal is the statistically principled semi-Bayesian posterior — S-BART marginalizes over the continuum and enforces a single common RV shift across all orders, and on Barnard's star it yields smaller RV scatter than the per-order weighted-average pipelines (HARPS-TERRA, SERVAL) When an order shows an anomalously small uncertainty in RV_orderwise_errors.png — the weighted average can then be dominated by an unreliable order Classical template-matching baseline for stellar radial velocities: estimate an RV shift independently for each spectral order against the stellar template, then combine the order-wise RVs into a single spectrum-level value through a weighted average. Serves as the reference point against which the semi-Bayesian (S-BART) single-common-RV-shift formulation is validated. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202142262
skills.summary: Classical template-matching baseline for stellar radial velocities: estimate an RV shift independently for each spectral order against the stellar template, then combine the order-wise RVs into a single spectrum-level value through a weighted average. Serves as the reference point against which the semi-Bayesian (S-BART) single-common-RV-shift formulation is validated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is the statistically principled semi-Bayesian posterior — S-BART marginalizes over the continuum and enforces a single common RV shift across all orders, and on Barnard's star it yields smaller RV scatter than the per-order weighted-average pipelines (HARPS-TERRA, SERVAL) When an order shows an anomalously small uncertainty in RV_orderwise_errors.png — the weighted average can then be dominated by an unreliable order

skills.description: Use when implementing or verifying the short-range pair traversal of a P3M-style N-body solver in a periodic box: you need a tiling scheme that guarantees completeness for all pairs within the cut-off x_r.
skills.name: periodic-box-domain-decomposition
skills.search_text: periodic-box-domain-decomposition Use when implementing or verifying the short-range pair traversal of a P3M-style N-body solver in a periodic box: you need a tiling scheme that guarantees completeness for all pairs within the cut-off x_r. The solver has no short-range cut-off component (e.g. pure long-range PM or particle-mesh-only computation) — tiling for x_r completeness is pointless Boundary conditions are non-periodic, so minimum-image distances used in the Cython traversal kernel are invalid Input positions are already partitioned or paired by another method (e.g. a tree code) and re-tiling would be redundant Decomposes a periodic simulation box into spatial domains, tiles, and subtiles — with tile extents of at least the short-range cut-off x_r in every dimension — so that the P3M short-range force computation visits every particle pair with separation <= x_r while early-rejecting non-interacting candidates. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stac568
skills.summary: Decomposes a periodic simulation box into spatial domains, tiles, and subtiles — with tile extents of at least the short-range cut-off x_r in every dimension — so that the P3M short-range force computation visits every particle pair with separation <= x_r while early-rejecting non-interacting candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The solver has no short-range cut-off component (e.g. pure long-range PM or particle-mesh-only computation) — tiling for x_r completeness is pointless Boundary conditions are non-periodic, so minimum-image distances used in the Cython traversal kernel are invalid Input positions are already partitioned or paired by another method (e.g. a tree code) and re-tiling would be redundant

skills.name: phase-space-density-thresholding
skills.search_text: phase-space-density-thresholding Use when an Eulerian Vlasov or hybrid-Vlasov solver's full 3D–3V velocity grid is prohibitively large (e.g. ~10^18 cells / 4 EiB) and only a small region of velocity space carries non-negligible phase-space density. The distribution function fills velocity space nearly uniformly, so sparsity savings are negligible and full-grid storage is simpler The solver already uses a particle/trajectory-based (PIC) representation rather than an Eulerian velocity grid Physical processes depend sensitively on tail cells below the f_min cutoff that the buffer layer cannot capture (e.g. very low-density beams far from the core population) http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Sparse velocity-space representation used by Vlasiator: the distribution function is stored and propagated only where phase-space density is non-negligible (above an f_min threshold, with a buffer layer of marginally populated cells), reducing memory from ~4 EiB for a full 3D–3V Eulerian grid by factors of 10^2–10^3. astronomy/v1 10.1007/s41115-018-0003-2

The planet's radius and mass are not yet constrained by a joint fit (e.g. candidate with no RV mass), so no reliable irradiation/escape calculation can be anchored The goal is flux-contamination assessment of TESS photometry rather than atmospheric escape — TESS-cont addresses crowding metrics (CROWDSAP, FLFRCSAP), not mass loss Estimates the present-day atmospheric mass-loss rate of a confirmed transiting planet by running two independent photoevaporation models on the same set of planet (Rp, Mp, ρp) and host-star irradiation parameters, then contrasting the predictions to expose model-choice dependence. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451656
skills.summary: Estimates the present-day atmospheric mass-loss rate of a confirmed transiting planet by running two independent photoevaporation models on the same set of planet (Rp, Mp, ρp) and host-star irradiation parameters, then contrasting the predictions to expose model-choice dependence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The planet's radius and mass are not yet constrained by a joint fit (e.g. candidate with no RV mass), so no reliable irradiation/escape calculation can be anchored The goal is flux-contamination assessment of TESS photometry rather than atmospheric escape — TESS-cont addresses crowding metrics (CROWDSAP, FLFRCSAP), not mass loss

skills.description: Use when you have observed planetary parameters (radii ~3.41, 1.55, 1.54 R_earth; periods 13.6, 3.5, 6.4 days for HIP 29442) plus plaNETic posterior samples and need to infer formation pathways by scanning a Bern-model synthetic population for system analogues.
skills.name: planetary-system-analogue-identification
skills.search_text: planetary-system-analogue-identification Use when you have observed planetary parameters (radii ~3.41, 1.55, 1.54 R_earth; periods 13.6, 3.5, 6.4 days for HIP 29442) plus plaNETic posterior samples and need to infer formation pathways by scanning a Bern-model synthetic population for system analogues. Planets are outside plaNETic's validated mass range of 0.5–15 Earth masses, so internal-structure posteriors feeding the analogue matching cannot be trusted. The goal is internal-structure inference itself rather than formation-pathway interpretation — use the plaNETic grid accept-reject sampling skill directly. No synthetic population or formation model output is available, so matched analogues cannot provide iceline or disk-solid-mass diagnostics. Identifies planetary system analogues in a Bern-model synthetic planet-formation population by matching observed planet masses, radii, and periods (from plaNETic/CHEOPS analysis of HIP 29442, TOI-469), then extracting formation diagnostics such as formation location relative to the water iceline and initial disk solid mass. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202450472
skills.summary: Identifies planetary system analogues in a Bern-model synthetic planet-formation population by matching observed planet masses, radii, and periods (from plaNETic/CHEOPS analysis of HIP 29442, TOI-469), then extracting formation diagnostics such as formation location relative to the water iceline and initial disk solid mass.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Planets are outside plaNETic's validated mass range of 0.5–15 Earth masses, so internal-structure posteriors feeding the analogue matching cannot be trusted. The goal is internal-structure inference itself rather than formation-pathway interpretation — use the plaNETic grid accept-reject sampling skill directly. No synthetic population or formation model output is available, so matched analogues cannot provide iceline or disk-solid-mass diagnostics.

skills.description: Use when a new multi-planet system with published radii (e.g. from CHEOPS+TESS joint modelling) and RVs (e.g. ESPRESSO/HIRES) must be set up as input for plaNETic internal-structure posterior runs.
skills.name: planetary-system-parameter-file-preparation
skills.search_text: planetary-system-parameter-file-preparation Use when a new multi-planet system with published radii (e.g. from CHEOPS+TESS joint modelling) and RVs (e.g. ESPRESSO/HIRES) must be set up as input for plaNETic internal-structure posterior runs. The planets fall outside plaNETic's validated mass range of 0.5–15 Mearth Only TESS photometry with low per-transit SNR and large gaps is available for small planets — the paper shows planet d's radius deviated by >3σ from the discovery paper, so radii should come from CHEOPS+TESS joint modelling instead The goal is forward-modelling planet formation rather than Bayesian internal-structure inference from observed parameters http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Prepare a plaNETic 'run_grid' subfolder for a new planetary system (here HIP 29442 / TOI-469) by writing a 'stellar_planetary_parameters.csv' with observed host-star and planet properties from CHEOPS+TESS radius fits and ESPRESSO/HIRES RVs, plus an adapted 'run_grid_xxx.py' executable cloned from the 'TOI-469_Egger+' template. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202450472
skills.summary: Prepare a plaNETic 'run_grid' subfolder for a new planetary system (here HIP 29442 / TOI-469) by writing a 'stellar_planetary_parameters.csv' with observed host-star and planet properties from CHEOPS+TESS radius fits and ESPRESSO/HIRES RVs, plus an adapted 'run_grid_xxx.py' executable cloned from the 'TOI-469_Egger+' template.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The planets fall outside plaNETic's validated mass range of 0.5–15 Mearth Only TESS photometry with low per-transit SNR and large gaps is available for small planets — the paper shows planet d's radius deviated by >3σ from the discovery paper, so radii should come from CHEOPS+TESS joint modelling instead The goal is forward-modelling planet formation rather than Bayesian internal-structure inference from observed parameters

skills.name: plot-file-verification
