skills.description: Use when building a cosmological (or any) MCMC likelihood pipeline on CosmoHammer and you need to plug in, order, and initialise custom core/likelihood modules with parameter-bound enforcement before sampling.
skills.name: plugin-module-registration-pattern
skills.search_text: plugin-module-registration-pattern Use when building a cosmological (or any) MCMC likelihood pipeline on CosmoHammer and you need to plug in, order, and initialise custom core/likelihood modules with parameter-bound enforcement before sampling. When the likelihood/theory code cannot be wrapped as a Python module — CosmoHammer's plug-in architecture requires Python modules containing further likelihood functions or theory prediction codes When you need a monolithic sampler that bundles its own Boltzmann code and likelihood (e.g. CosmoMC) rather than composing standalone modules When sampling parameters should be allowed outside the physical min/max bounds supplied at chain construction Extends the CosmoHammer MCMC framework by registering self-contained core and likelihood modules (e.g. CambCoreModule and WmapLikelihoodModule) into a LikelihoodComputationChain, which stores them, initialises them in order via setup(), and shuttles data between them through a shared chain context (ctx). astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.06.003
skills.summary: Extends the CosmoHammer MCMC framework by registering self-contained core and likelihood modules (e.g. CambCoreModule and WmapLikelihoodModule) into a LikelihoodComputationChain, which stores them, initialises them in order via setup(), and shuttles data between them through a shared chain context (ctx).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the likelihood/theory code cannot be wrapped as a Python module — CosmoHammer's plug-in architecture requires Python modules containing further likelihood functions or theory prediction codes When you need a monolithic sampler that bundles its own Boltzmann code and likelihood (e.g. CosmoMC) rather than composing standalone modules When sampling parameters should be allowed outside the physical min/max bounds supplied at chain construction

skills.description: Use when a reconstructed 3-D model (e.g., an OpenMVS dense point cloud from SfM imagery) must be validated against a known reference surface, and error must be reported as Gaussian mean/std deviation statistics.
skills.name: point-cloud-deviation-statistics
skills.search_text: point-cloud-deviation-statistics Use when a reconstructed 3-D model (e.g., an OpenMVS dense point cloud from SfM imagery) must be validated against a known reference surface, and error must be reported as Gaussian mean/std deviation statistics. No ground-truth reference surface exists (e.g., target body is unknown before close encounter), so point-to-mesh comparison cannot be anchored. The reconstruction was not produced from the same reference geometry or registered into a common frame — distances would be dominated by misalignment, not reconstruction error. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Quantify the accuracy of a 3-D reconstruction against a reference shape model by computing point-to-mesh Gaussian distances in CloudCompare and summarizing them as Gaussian mean and standard deviation statistics. In the SISPO SSSB fly-by case this yields a mean error of 14.7 m and standard deviation of 63.9 m. astronomy/v1 10.1371/journal.pone.0263882
skills.summary: Quantify the accuracy of a 3-D reconstruction against a reference shape model by computing point-to-mesh Gaussian distances in CloudCompare and summarizing them as Gaussian mean and standard deviation statistics. In the SISPO SSSB fly-by case this yields a mean error of 14.7 m and standard deviation of 63.9 m.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth reference surface exists (e.g., target body is unknown before close encounter), so point-to-mesh comparison cannot be anchored. The reconstruction was not produced from the same reference geometry or registered into a common frame — distances would be dominated by misalignment, not reconstruction error.

skills.description: Use when an integrated flux density for a compact, bright point source must be measured from HEALPix I/Q/U map products (e.g., the B-Machine 37.5 GHz destriped maps) and compared to a reference instrument such as WMAP Q-band.
skills.name: point-source-aperture-photometry
skills.search_text: point-source-aperture-photometry Use when an integrated flux density for a compact, bright point source must be measured from HEALPix I/Q/U map products (e.g., the B-Machine 37.5 GHz destriped maps) and compared to a reference instrument such as WMAP Q-band. The target's polarized emission in U is too faint to be detected (e.g., Tau A), so aperture photometry on the U map would not yield a usable flux The data are still raw timestreams rather than destriped maps — destriping must be done first (dst pipeline), since correlated-noise baselines bias map-domain fluxes The source is extended diffuse emission rather than a compact point source suitable for aperture photometry on a 5-degree patch Measures the integrated flux density of a compact source (here Tau A / Crab Nebula) from destriped B-Machine Nside 512 HEALPix I, Q, U maps via aperture photometry on gnomonic patches, and validates the result against the WMAP 7-year Q-band reference flux in intensity and polarization. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Measures the integrated flux density of a compact source (here Tau A / Crab Nebula) from destriped B-Machine Nside 512 HEALPix I, Q, U maps via aperture photometry on gnomonic patches, and validates the result against the WMAP 7-year Q-band reference flux in intensity and polarization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target's polarized emission in U is too faint to be detected (e.g., Tau A), so aperture photometry on the U map would not yield a usable flux The data are still raw timestreams rather than destriped maps — destriping must be done first (dst pipeline), since correlated-noise baselines bias map-domain fluxes The source is extended diffuse emission rather than a compact point source suitable for aperture photometry on a 5-degree patch

skills.description: Use when a newly destriped low-frequency microwave sky map needs absolute calibration validation against a known bright point source, or when reproducing the B-Machine '20% in I, 6% in Q' Tau A agreement check.
skills.name: point-source-calibration-validation
skills.search_text: point-source-calibration-validation Use when a newly destriped low-frequency microwave sky map needs absolute calibration validation against a known bright point source, or when reproducing the B-Machine '20% in I, 6% in Q' Tau A agreement check. Tau A emission in the U Stokes parameter is too faint to be detected, so this skill must not be used to calibrate U The maps have not been destriped (low-frequency correlated noise not removed), since correlated-noise residuals would bias the aperture photometry The target source is extended diffuse foreground emission rather than a compact point source matching the 40-arcmin gaussian-smoothed point-source maps http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Validates the absolute polarization/temperature calibration of a ground-based CMB polarimeter (B-Machine, 37.5 GHz) by measuring the integrated flux density of the bright point source Tau A (Crab Nebula) on destriped HEALPix maps and comparing it to the WMAP 7-year Q-band reference flux. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Validates the absolute polarization/temperature calibration of a ground-based CMB polarimeter (B-Machine, 37.5 GHz) by measuring the integrated flux density of the bright point source Tau A (Crab Nebula) on destriped HEALPix maps and comparing it to the WMAP 7-year Q-band reference flux.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tau A emission in the U Stokes parameter is too faint to be detected, so this skill must not be used to calibrate U The maps have not been destriped (low-frequency correlated noise not removed), since correlated-noise residuals would bias the aperture photometry The target source is extended diffuse foreground emission rather than a compact point source matching the 40-arcmin gaussian-smoothed point-source maps

skills.description: Use when preprocessing an HSC catalog extract for transient host-galaxy association and you need to retain only extended (galaxy) sources, discarding point-like (star) sources via the extended flag.
skills.name: point-source-extended-source-discrimination
skills.search_text: point-source-extended-source-discrimination Use when preprocessing an HSC catalog extract for transient host-galaxy association and you need to retain only extended (galaxy) sources, discarding point-like (star) sources via the extended flag. Input catalog is Pan-STARRS — stars must be discarded using colour criteria rather than an extended flag Input catalog is AllWISE or GLADE, which follow different galaxy-identification strategies than HSC's extended flag Point-like transient sources (not galaxies) are the objects of interest, e.g. pure star-catalog work http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 A star/galaxy separation step used by galclaim to keep only galaxies from an input catalog before chance-alignment probability computation; for HSC this is done by filtering rows on the catalog-provided extended flag. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.softx.2023.101582
skills.summary: A star/galaxy separation step used by galclaim to keep only galaxies from an input catalog before chance-alignment probability computation; for HSC this is done by filtering rows on the catalog-provided extended flag.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input catalog is Pan-STARRS — stars must be discarded using colour criteria rather than an extended flag Input catalog is AllWISE or GLADE, which follow different galaxy-identification strategies than HSC's extended flag Point-like transient sources (not galaxies) are the objects of interest, e.g. pure star-catalog work

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify the accuracy of a transient spectrum extractor (e.g. HyperGal vs. pysedm) on IFS cubes by injecting sources of known contrast and spectrum, then measuring recovery error per contrast bin.
skills.name: point-source-injection-simulation
skills.search_text: point-source-injection-simulation Use when you need to quantify the accuracy of a transient spectrum extractor (e.g. HyperGal vs. pysedm) on IFS cubes by injecting sources of known contrast and spectrum, then measuring recovery error per contrast bin. The goal is classification/typing performance rather than extraction accuracy — use SNID classification with rlap_min = 6 and the 50% top-10 model agreement criterion instead The transient is treated as an isolated point source with no structured host background — the standard PSF extraction path (e.g. pysedm) applies, and injection-based scene-modeling validation is unnecessary No pre-transient photometric host reference is available to build the hyperspectral galaxy model required as the injection scene http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Validation-by-injection scheme for scene-modeling spectrum extraction: inject a point source with a known input spectrum into a synthetic SEDm data cube at a controlled SN/host contrast c, run the extraction pipeline, and quantify recovered-spectrum fidelity via continuum-divided spectral relative RMS. It isolates extraction accuracy from classifier behavior by comparing extracted vs. injected spectra. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202244740
skills.summary: Validation-by-injection scheme for scene-modeling spectrum extraction: inject a point source with a known input spectrum into a synthetic SEDm data cube at a controlled SN/host contrast c, run the extraction pipeline, and quantify recovered-spectrum fidelity via continuum-divided spectral relative RMS. It isolates extraction accuracy from classifier behavior by comparing extracted vs. injected spectra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classification/typing performance rather than extraction accuracy — use SNID classification with rlap_min = 6 and the 50% top-10 model agreement criterion instead The transient is treated as an isolated point source with no structured host background — the standard PSF extraction path (e.g. pysedm) applies, and injection-based scene-modeling validation is unnecessary No pre-transient photometric host reference is available to build the hyperspectral galaxy model required as the injection scene

skills.description: Use when generating mock observational galaxy images from radiative-transfer data cubes and need survey-realistic PSF blurring, filter throughput application, and sky background noise injection per band.
skills.name: point-spread-function-convolution-mock-imaging
skills.search_text: point-spread-function-convolution-mock-imaging Use when generating mock observational galaxy images from radiative-transfer data cubes and need survey-realistic PSF blurring, filter throughput application, and sky background noise injection per band. The input is raw simulation particle data that still needs SKIRT radiative transfer — apply the PreProcess and DataGeneration stages first Euclid mock imaging requiring a convolved PSF — only filters are uploaded since the Euclid PSF files cannot be accessed The goal is pure radiative-transfer SED modelling without observation simulation — the PSF/instrumental/noise postprocessing is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Convolve ideal IFU-like SKIRT data cubes with per-survey point spread functions (stored as numpy arrays in Data/PSFs/(survey)) while applying filter throughputs, instrumental effects, and sky background noise, to produce realistic mock bandpass images for surveys such as CSST, Euclid, HST, JWST, Roman, and HSC from IllustrisTNG and EAGLE simulations. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202554287
skills.summary: Convolve ideal IFU-like SKIRT data cubes with per-survey point spread functions (stored as numpy arrays in Data/PSFs/(survey)) while applying filter throughputs, instrumental effects, and sky background noise, to produce realistic mock bandpass images for surveys such as CSST, Euclid, HST, JWST, Roman, and HSC from IllustrisTNG and EAGLE simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw simulation particle data that still needs SKIRT radiative transfer — apply the PreProcess and DataGeneration stages first Euclid mock imaging requiring a convolved PSF — only filters are uploaded since the Euclid PSF files cannot be accessed The goal is pure radiative-transfer SED modelling without observation simulation — the PSF/instrumental/noise postprocessing is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when you need to map polarimeter timeline samples (PHI, THETA, PSI angles) onto a HEALPix grid to build the binning operator B or the destriping operator for CMB map-making.
skills.name: pointing-matrix-construction-healpix
skills.search_text: pointing-matrix-construction-healpix Use when you need to map polarimeter timeline samples (PHI, THETA, PSI angles) onto a HEALPix grid to build the binning operator B or the destriping operator for CMB map-making. The timeline contains systematic effects such as thermally induced gain variations near sunrise/sunset — these must be masked or handled before map-making, since destriping only removes low-frequency correlated noise in the timestream The scanning strategy lacks frequent crossing points, which the paper states destriping requires to be effective The input is not a single HDF5 file with the required columns (TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, TEMP, Q, U) and you do not intend to modify dst_io.read_data to support another format http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Constructs the pointing matrix P that maps each polarimeter timestream sample (defined by its PHI, THETA, PSI angles) onto a HEALPix Nside 256 sky pixel. P underpins both the binning operator B and the destriping operator R^T (I - P B^T P^T) R, which are applied via matrix-vector products rather than any dense matrix. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Constructs the pointing matrix P that maps each polarimeter timestream sample (defined by its PHI, THETA, PSI angles) onto a HEALPix Nside 256 sky pixel. P underpins both the binning operator B and the destriping operator R^T (I - P B^T P^T) R, which are applied via matrix-vector products rather than any dense matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The timeline contains systematic effects such as thermally induced gain variations near sunrise/sunset — these must be masked or handled before map-making, since destriping only removes low-frequency correlated noise in the timestream The scanning strategy lacks frequent crossing points, which the paper states destriping requires to be effective The input is not a single HDF5 file with the required columns (TIME, PHI, THETA, PSI, FLAG, TEMP, Q, U) and you do not intend to modify dst_io.read_data to support another format

skills.description: Use when fitting X-ray spectra (OGIP PHA/ARF/RMF, e.g. XMM-Newton or Hitomi observations) where counts are low and chi-square fitting would bias parameter estimates, or when a differentiable likelihood is needed for Bayesian inference.
skills.name: poisson-likelihood-cstat-spectral-modeling
skills.search_text: poisson-likelihood-cstat-spectral-modeling Use when fitting X-ray spectra (OGIP PHA/ARF/RMF, e.g. XMM-Newton or Hitomi observations) where counts are low and chi-square fitting would bias parameter estimates, or when a differentiable likelihood is needed for Bayesian inference. When input spectra are already binned/processed such that a chi-square fit on Gaussian errors is standard practice and counts are high — the article's rationale for C-stat targets low-count Poisson data When a comprehensive error budget is required and the only available background option is SubtractedBackground, which does not propagate dispersion When a non-Python HEASoft/XSPEC-dependent pipeline must be preserved — jaxspec is pure Python with no HEASoft dependency and is still in early release with expected API changes http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Fits X-ray spectra under a Poisson likelihood (C-statistic) rather than chi-square, so parameter estimates remain unbiased at low counts; in jaxspec this likelihood is differentiable and JAX-compilable, enabling Bayesian sampling (NUTS) or GPU variational inference. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451736
skills.summary: Fits X-ray spectra under a Poisson likelihood (C-statistic) rather than chi-square, so parameter estimates remain unbiased at low counts; in jaxspec this likelihood is differentiable and JAX-compilable, enabling Bayesian sampling (NUTS) or GPU variational inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When input spectra are already binned/processed such that a chi-square fit on Gaussian errors is standard practice and counts are high — the article's rationale for C-stat targets low-count Poisson data When a comprehensive error budget is required and the only available background option is SubtractedBackground, which does not propagate dispersion When a non-Python HEASoft/XSPEC-dependent pipeline must be preserved — jaxspec is pure Python with no HEASoft dependency and is still in early release with expected API changes

skills.description: Use when fitting physical component models to X-ray/IFU data cubes whose noise is Poisson-distributed (photon counts), and you need differentiable likelihood terms for a PALM-style optimization with explicit step sizes.
skills.name: poisson-likelihood-gradient-and-hessian-computation
skills.search_text: poisson-likelihood-gradient-and-hessian-computation Use when fitting physical component models to X-ray/IFU data cubes whose noise is Poisson-distributed (photon counts), and you need differentiable likelihood terms for a PALM-style optimization with explicit step sizes. Data whose noise is not Poisson-distributed (e.g. Gaussian-noise calibration or non-count data) — the likelihood, gradient, and Hessian diagonal forms would be wrong The spectral model is not differentiable with respect to its parameters (no ∂M/∂θ available via auto-differentiation) A per-pixel 1D fit suffices and no spatial coupling of parameters is desired — the classic per-pixel approach is the appropriate baseline Computes the gradients and per-pixel Hessian diagonal of the negative Poisson log-likelihood used inside SUSHI's PALM loop, driving the gradient-descent updates of the IAE spectral parameter maps θ_c and the amplitude maps A_c for hyperspectral (IFU) data cubes with photon-counting noise. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202347518
skills.summary: Computes the gradients and per-pixel Hessian diagonal of the negative Poisson log-likelihood used inside SUSHI's PALM loop, driving the gradient-descent updates of the IAE spectral parameter maps θ_c and the amplitude maps A_c for hyperspectral (IFU) data cubes with photon-counting noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data whose noise is not Poisson-distributed (e.g. Gaussian-noise calibration or non-count data) — the likelihood, gradient, and Hessian diagonal forms would be wrong The spectral model is not differentiable with respect to its parameters (no ∂M/∂θ available via auto-differentiation) A per-pixel 1D fit suffices and no spatial coupling of parameters is desired — the classic per-pixel approach is the appropriate baseline

skills.description: Use when fitting photon-counting (Poisson-noise) hyperspectral X-ray data cubes with fixed, learned per-component spectral models (e.g. IAE decoders) and you need pixel-wise amplitude maps and spatially regularized spectral parameters.
skills.name: poisson-likelihood-optimization
skills.search_text: poisson-likelihood-optimization Use when fitting photon-counting (Poisson-noise) hyperspectral X-ray data cubes with fixed, learned per-component spectral models (e.g. IAE decoders) and you need pixel-wise amplitude maps and spatially regularized spectral parameters. Data with Gaussian (non-counting) noise statistics, where a Poisson log-likelihood is mismatched to the measurement process Problems where a fixed number of physical components cannot be assumed or no spectral model (analytical or learned IAE) is available for a component Cases where a component is very weak relative to another (e.g. synchrotron under bright thermal emission) and spatial regularization patches were too large to recover it — SUSHI's known failure mode Alternating proximal optimization (PALM, Bolte et al. 2014) of per-component amplitudes and latent spectral parameters under a negative Poisson log-likelihood, as implemented in SUSHI's non-stationary unmixing of X-ray hyperspectral cubes with IAE spectral models. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202347518
skills.summary: Alternating proximal optimization (PALM, Bolte et al. 2014) of per-component amplitudes and latent spectral parameters under a negative Poisson log-likelihood, as implemented in SUSHI's non-stationary unmixing of X-ray hyperspectral cubes with IAE spectral models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data with Gaussian (non-counting) noise statistics, where a Poisson log-likelihood is mismatched to the measurement process Problems where a fixed number of physical components cannot be assumed or no spectral model (analytical or learned IAE) is available for a component Cases where a component is very weak relative to another (e.g. synchrotron under bright thermal emission) and spatial regularization patches were too large to recover it — SUSHI's known failure mode

skills.description: Use when the input is a photon-counting X-ray hyperspectral cube (e.g. Chandra ACIS-S, 375 channels from 3 keV to 8.48 keV) whose counts follow Poisson statistics, and you need per-pixel physical parameters (temperature, redshift, photon index) or unmixed component maps.
skills.name: poisson-likelihood-spectral-fitting
skills.search_text: poisson-likelihood-spectral-fitting Use when the input is a photon-counting X-ray hyperspectral cube (e.g. Chandra ACIS-S, 375 channels from 3 keV to 8.48 keV) whose counts follow Poisson statistics, and you need per-pixel physical parameters (temperature, redshift, photon index) or unmixed component maps. When SUSHI's final output would be mistaken for physical parameters directly — it returns fitted unmixed spectra and does not directly provide physical parameters When the synchrotron (or any) component is weak relative to the thermal component and patches are large enough that spatial regularization cannot compensate — SUSHI failed to reconstruct the synchrotron component in this regime When no spectral model is available for the assumed physical components — SUSHI requires a fixed number of components, each with a (possibly non-analytical) spectral model Fits X-ray hyperspectral (IFU) cubes by minimizing the Poisson negative log-likelihood over spectral-parameter and amplitude maps, as implemented in the SUSHI algorithm (Lascar, Bobin & Acero 2024), using PALM optimization with starlet-wavelet sparsity and non-negativity proximal steps. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202347518
skills.summary: Fits X-ray hyperspectral (IFU) cubes by minimizing the Poisson negative log-likelihood over spectral-parameter and amplitude maps, as implemented in the SUSHI algorithm (Lascar, Bobin & Acero 2024), using PALM optimization with starlet-wavelet sparsity and non-negativity proximal steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When SUSHI's final output would be mistaken for physical parameters directly — it returns fitted unmixed spectra and does not directly provide physical parameters When the synchrotron (or any) component is weak relative to the thermal component and patches are large enough that spatial regularization cannot compensate — SUSHI failed to reconstruct the synchrotron component in this regime When no spectral model is available for the assumed physical components — SUSHI requires a fixed number of components, each with a (possibly non-analytical) spectral model

skills.description: Use when validating or reproducing Marz-style spectral smoothing: you need a noisy exponential-decay test signal with known ground truth to show that the exponential decay filter preserves peak locations better than a moving-average (boxcar) smoother.
skills.name: poisson-noise-signal-synthesis

skills.name: polychromatic-versus-grey-background-ionization-comparison
skills.search_text: polychromatic-versus-grey-background-ionization-comparison Use when comparing ionization/temperature solutions of a Lyman-limit slab exposed to an isotropic background where spectral shape matters — i.e. testing grey vs. polychromatic (HM12) treatment of the meta-galactic background. The problem geometry is a point source or a spherical cloud rather than a semi-infinite slab in an isotropic background — rabacus provides separate solvers for those cases. Only an order-of-magnitude column-density estimate is needed and spectral shape, helium, and temperature treatment can all be treated approximately. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Quantifies how the spectral shape of an ionizing background (polychromatic HM12 vs. a grey/hardening spectrum) alters equilibrium column densities and temperatures in a semi-infinite slab, using rabacus's grey_fixT_B and hm12_fixT_B case-B slab solvers. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.004

skills.when_to_use_negative: The problem geometry is a point source or a spherical cloud rather than a semi-infinite slab in an isotropic background — rabacus provides separate solvers for those cases. skills.description: Use when sampling from a high-dimensional real-parameter posterior (e.g. Bayesian analysis) where choosing scale/orientation for a jumping distribution is hard, or WinBUGS one-dimensional updates are insufficient.
skills.name: population-based-multi-chain-mcmc
skills.search_text: population-based-multi-chain-mcmc Use when sampling from a high-dimensional real-parameter posterior (e.g. Bayesian analysis) where choosing scale/orientation for a jumping distribution is hard, or WinBUGS one-dimensional updates are insufficient. When a closed-form Gibbs step exists — e.g. the conditional distribution needed for Gibbs sampling of a parameter is available in closed form and easy to sample directly When the initial population covers only a single modal region, since distant modes cannot be reached by the sampler When greedy, fast-converging optimization-like sampling is required, since DE-MC is not a greedy algorithm and large populations need more computer time to converge http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implements DE-MC, a population-based Metropolis sampler in which each of N parallel chains proposes jumps as gamma*(x_R1 - x_R2) differences drawn from the other N-1 chains, so jump scale and orientation adapt automatically to the target's variance-covariance matrix. astronomy/v1 10.1007/s11222-006-8769-1
skills.summary: Implements DE-MC, a population-based Metropolis sampler in which each of N parallel chains proposes jumps as gamma*(x_R1 - x_R2) differences drawn from the other N-1 chains, so jump scale and orientation adapt automatically to the target's variance-covariance matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a closed-form Gibbs step exists — e.g. the conditional distribution needed for Gibbs sampling of a parameter is available in closed form and easy to sample directly When the initial population covers only a single modal region, since distant modes cannot be reached by the sampler When greedy, fast-converging optimization-like sampling is required, since DE-MC is not a greedy algorithm and large populations need more computer time to converge

skills.name: positional-data-file-diff-verification
skills.search_text: positional-data-file-diff-verification Use when validating that galkin_data.py reproduces its published positional data output for a specific Galactic parameter condition (e.g. R0=8.5 kpc) before trusting regenerated rotation-curve data in downstream analyses. skills.summary: Regenerate the galkin positional data output (output/posdata.dat) for a chosen Galactic parameter set (e.g. R0=8.5 kpc) and verify it row by row against a deposited sample reference file (posdata_R85.dat) as a reproducibility check of galkin_data.py.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to inspect raw published measurements: use output/rawdata.dat or galkin/data/data_*.dat instead — the README warns these are 'given as in the original reference and thus not normalised to the selected input parameters' and should not be used unless fully aware of each reference's assumptions When the target parameter set has no deposited reference sample file (only baseline, R85, and R75 reference samples are shipped) — no acceptance benchmark exists for other conditions When running galkin repeatedly on the fly for parameter scanning — use galkin_data_fast.py in-memory mode rather than file-based diff verification

skills.description: Use when a CME case run in OSPREI requires an initial flux-rope magnetic field strength (FRB/beta_M) that must be justified from observations rather than assumed, and post-eruption arcades are visible in AIA 193/304 Å data for the event.
skills.name: post-eruption-arcade-reconnected-flux-estimation
skills.search_text: post-eruption-arcade-reconnected-flux-estimation Use when a CME case run in OSPREI requires an initial flux-rope magnetic field strength (FRB/beta_M) that must be justified from observations rather than assumed, and post-eruption arcades are visible in AIA 193/304 Å data for the event. No post-eruption arcade is observable in AIA 193/304 Å for the event (e.g., far-side or poorly observed eruptions), so no reconnected flux can be measured The goal is a fine-tuned best-fit simulation rather than a forecasting proof-of-concept with observationally justifiable inputs Only arrival time/speed matters and the CME is treated as a hydrodynamic pressure pulse without an internal magnetic structure — FRB/beta_M scaling is then irrelevant Estimates an observationally grounded CME flux-rope magnetic field scaling (beta_M) by tracking post-eruption arcade (PEA) area evolution in SDO/AIA 193 and 304 Å imagery and computing reconnected magnetic flux via the Gopalswamy et al. (2017) Flux Rope from Eruption Data method, then feeds the derived value into the OSPREI chain in place of hand-picked FRB scalings. astronomy/v1 10.1029/2021sw002914
skills.summary: Estimates an observationally grounded CME flux-rope magnetic field scaling (beta_M) by tracking post-eruption arcade (PEA) area evolution in SDO/AIA 193 and 304 Å imagery and computing reconnected magnetic flux via the Gopalswamy et al. (2017) Flux Rope from Eruption Data method, then feeds the derived value into the OSPREI chain in place of hand-picked FRB scalings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No post-eruption arcade is observable in AIA 193/304 Å for the event (e.g., far-side or poorly observed eruptions), so no reconnected flux can be measured The goal is a fine-tuned best-fit simulation rather than a forecasting proof-of-concept with observationally justifiable inputs Only arrival time/speed matters and the CME is treated as a hydrodynamic pressure pulse without an internal magnetic structure — FRB/beta_M scaling is then irrelevant

skills.search_text: post-newtonian-inspired-amplitude-phase-modeling Use when building a reduced-basis/empirical-interpolant surrogate for a waveform family and you need cheap parametric fits of amplitude and phase at each empirical time node across a mass-ratio training interval (e.g., q = 1 to 10). The goal is evaluating an already-built surrogate (e.g., via gwsurrogate.LoadSurrogate) rather than constructing the parametric fits themselves The waveform parameter space includes precession or spins, since the fits here are one-dimensional functions of mass ratio for nonspinning BBHs with q = 1 to 10 Empirical time nodes have not yet been selected (the fits are defined pointwise at the m nodes of the empirical interpolant) http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Fits the waveform amplitude and phase, evaluated at each of the m greedy-selected empirical time nodes, as functions of mass ratio using either polynomial least-squares (Eq. 25) or a post-Newtonian-inspired ansatz (Eqs. 28-29) combining polynomial terms with inverse powers of the symmetric mass ratio, selecting the better family per node for a compact surrogate model. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevx.4.031006

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is evaluating an already-built surrogate (e.g., via gwsurrogate.LoadSurrogate) rather than constructing the parametric fits themselves The waveform parameter space includes precession or spins, since the fits here are one-dimensional functions of mass ratio for nonspinning BBHs with q = 1 to 10 Empirical time nodes have not yet been selected (the fits are defined pointwise at the m nodes of the empirical interpolant)

skills.summary: Extracts per-parameter marginal constraints (mean and standard deviation) from gradient-based MCMC posterior chains produced with BlackJAX NUTS on a candl JAX likelihood, by denormalising Fisher-normalised draws back into physical parameter units.

skills.search_text: posterior-comparison-across-samplers Use when an MCMC fit (e.g. vis-r on ALMA visibility data such as hr4796.selfcal.npy) must be validated against an alternative sampler, or when an emcee posterior has insufficient independent samples and HMC convergence must be demonstrated. (2018) for measuring parameter estimation errors of a single run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw live-point-only output without born iso-likelihood contour information (e.g. PolyChord <1.14 with 'write_dead' disabled), since the thread division algorithm requires born contours to split the run Input is posterior samples from an MCMC sampler rather than nested sampling dead points — nestcheck is designed for analysing samples produced by nested sampling You need parameter estimation errors from many independent nested sampling runs averaged together instead of from a single run; this skill addresses the single-run case, where the paper finds no prior method could measure errors accurately

skills.description: Use when validating or tuning a DE-MC / differential-evolution MCMC implementation on a known target where the true posterior mean is computable, especially the bimodal normal mixture that defeats random walk Metropolis.
skills.name: posterior-mean-rmse-estimation
skills.search_text: posterior-mean-rmse-estimation Use when validating or tuning a DE-MC / differential-evolution MCMC implementation on a known target where the true posterior mean is computable, especially the bimodal normal mixture that defeats random walk Metropolis. The target has only a single modal region and the population starts there — the benchmark's failure mode (unreachable distant modes) does not apply, and simpler unimodal diagnostics suffice The true posterior mean is not analytically known, so RMSE against 1.667 cannot be computed as a correctness check The task is one-dimensional updating in the generalized linear model context, where WinBUGS-style per-dimension Gibbs/Metropolis updates are the established choice http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark a population MCMC sampler (DE-MC) on the two-component Normal mixture target (1/3)N_d(-5,I)+(2/3)N_d(5,I) by measuring RMSE of the posterior mean estimate against the known expected value 1.667, together with the acceptance fraction, for d = 5 and d = 10. astronomy/v1 10.1007/s11222-006-8769-1

skills.description: Use when you have retained posterior samples from an MCMC run (e.g. CosmoHammer/emcee over WMAP 7 Lambda-CDM parameters) and need means, marginal standard deviations, and a within-tolerance comparison to a reference sampler.
skills.name: posterior-summary-statistics-computation
skills.search_text: posterior-summary-statistics-computation Use when you have retained posterior samples from an MCMC run (e.g. CosmoHammer/emcee over WMAP 7 Lambda-CDM parameters) and need means, marginal standard deviations, and a within-tolerance comparison to a reference sampler. You only need a single best-fit point before sampling (the article instead uses particle swarm optimization via ParticleSwarmOptimizer for that purpose), not a posterior distribution over samples. The chain has not yet converged or burn-in has not been run/determined — summarising unconverged samples would violate the ~3.4%-of-sigma agreement criterion. You only have single likelihood evaluations (e.g. the WMAP 3/5/7/9-year likelihood print placeholders) rather than an ensemble of posterior samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Discard burn-in from an MCMC chain and compute per-parameter posterior means and marginal standard deviations (here for the seven Lambda-CDM parameters fitted to WMAP 7-year data with CosmoHammer/emcee), then validate the estimates against a reference chain such as CosmoMC within the expected statistical-error tolerance of about 3.4% of sigma. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.06.003
skills.summary: Discard burn-in from an MCMC chain and compute per-parameter posterior means and marginal standard deviations (here for the seven Lambda-CDM parameters fitted to WMAP 7-year data with CosmoHammer/emcee), then validate the estimates against a reference chain such as CosmoMC within the expected statistical-error tolerance of about 3.4% of sigma.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single best-fit point before sampling (the article instead uses particle swarm optimization via ParticleSwarmOptimizer for that purpose), not a posterior distribution over samples. The chain has not yet converged or burn-in has not been run/determined — summarising unconverged samples would violate the ~3.4%-of-sigma agreement criterion. You only have single likelihood evaluations (e.g. the WMAP 3/5/7/9-year likelihood print placeholders) rather than an ensemble of posterior samples.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how wall time of a parallelised sampler (e.g. CosmoHammer with emcee on EC2 or a grid) scales with core count, and you need a fitted power-law exponent alpha to quantify scaling overhead.
skills.name: power-law-walltime-regression
skills.search_text: power-law-walltime-regression Use when benchmarking how wall time of a parallelised sampler (e.g. CosmoHammer with emcee on EC2 or a grid) scales with core count, and you need a fitted power-law exponent alpha to quantify scaling overhead. The core count exceeds the number of walkers (here >300 for a 6-parameter run with walkers ratio 50): extra processes idle and wall-time scaling saturates, so a log-log fit over the saturated region would misrepresent the exponent. The sampling method is Metropolis–Hastings, which the paper reports is dominated by overheads in parallelised MCMC sampling rather than benefiting from ensemble parallelism. The goal is sampling accuracy or posterior quality rather than computational scaling; this skill only characterises wall-time behaviour, and no numeric likelihood or posterior results are reported in the article. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Benchmark wall time of a parallelised MCMC sampling run across a sweep of core counts and fit log(T) vs log(N) by least squares to recover the power-law scaling exponent alpha, following the CosmoHammer EC2 analysis that yielded alpha = 0.89 (11% overhead per doubling of cores). astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.06.003
skills.summary: Benchmark wall time of a parallelised MCMC sampling run across a sweep of core counts and fit log(T) vs log(N) by least squares to recover the power-law scaling exponent alpha, following the CosmoHammer EC2 analysis that yielded alpha = 0.89 (11% overhead per doubling of cores).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The core count exceeds the number of walkers (here >300 for a 6-parameter run with walkers ratio 50): extra processes idle and wall-time scaling saturates, so a log-log fit over the saturated region would misrepresent the exponent. The sampling method is Metropolis–Hastings, which the paper reports is dominated by overheads in parallelised MCMC sampling rather than benefiting from ensemble parallelism. The goal is sampling accuracy or posterior quality rather than computational scaling; this skill only characterises wall-time behaviour, and no numeric likelihood or posterior results are reported in the article.

skills.description: Use when compressing correlated integer visibility/correlator data (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder HDF5 visibilities) and you need to quantize values to a power-of-two grid without meaningfully raising thermal noise.
skills.name: power-of-two-rounding-granularity-derivation
skills.search_text: power-of-two-rounding-granularity-derivation Use when compressing correlated integer visibility/correlator data (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder HDF5 visibilities) and you need to quantize values to a power-of-two grid without meaningfully raising thermal noise. Data are floating-point or already low-entropy, so the rounding step offers no entropy reduction and only destroys precision Correlations between adjacent elements are weak, so precision reduction will not improve downstream lossless compression ratios enough to justify the noise increase You cannot estimate thermal noise per element (no calibration-independent radiometer-equation covariance available), making the sigma_r^2 < f*s^2 constraint inapplicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Derives the largest power-of-two rounding granularity g for integer radio data such that the induced rounding noise variance stays below a chosen fraction f of the element-wise thermal noise estimated from a calibration-independent radiometer equation (Eqs. 14-16), enabling nearly lossless precision reduction before lossless compression. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.07.002
skills.summary: Derives the largest power-of-two rounding granularity g for integer radio data such that the induced rounding noise variance stays below a chosen fraction f of the element-wise thermal noise estimated from a calibration-independent radiometer equation (Eqs. 14-16), enabling nearly lossless precision reduction before lossless compression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are floating-point or already low-entropy, so the rounding step offers no entropy reduction and only destroys precision Correlations between adjacent elements are weak, so precision reduction will not improve downstream lossless compression ratios enough to justify the noise increase You cannot estimate thermal noise per element (no calibration-independent radiometer-equation covariance available), making the sigma_r^2 < f*s^2 constraint inapplicable

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify the wall-clock evaluation cost of an analytic power-spectrum emulator relative to Boltzmann-solver (CAMB) or neural-network emulator (BACCO) references, using identical cosmologies and wavenumbers across k = 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc.
skills.name: power-spectrum-emulator-benchmarking
skills.search_text: power-spectrum-emulator-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify the wall-clock evaluation cost of an analytic power-spectrum emulator relative to Boltzmann-solver (CAMB) or neural-network emulator (BACCO) references, using identical cosmologies and wavenumbers across k = 9e-3 to 9 h/Mpc. The goal is to validate emulator accuracy (RMS fractional error ~0.2%) rather than timing — accuracy validation requires comparing against Boltzmann-equation solutions, not stopwatch benchmarks. The comparison target is the nonlinear (halofit) or extended-cosmology (neutrino masses, w0, wa) emulators, whose benchmark numbers differ from the linear ΛCDM emulator reported here. http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Benchmark the evaluation speed of the symbolic_pofk analytic linear power spectrum emulator (plin_emulated()) against CAMB and the BACCO neural-network emulator on a common cosmology/k grid, quantifying the reported speedups of ~950x versus CAMB and ~36x versus BACCO. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202348811
skills.summary: Benchmark the evaluation speed of the symbolic_pofk analytic linear power spectrum emulator (plin_emulated()) against CAMB and the BACCO neural-network emulator on a common cosmology/k grid, quantifying the reported speedups of ~950x versus CAMB and ~36x versus BACCO.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to validate emulator accuracy (RMS fractional error ~0.2%) rather than timing — accuracy validation requires comparing against Boltzmann-equation solutions, not stopwatch benchmarks. skills.search_text: precision-reduction-rounding Use when processing integrated, post-correlation radio data (e.g. CHIME Pathfinder correlator frames stored as 32-bit integers) where controlled precision reduction relative to thermal noise is needed to improve subsequent Bitshuffle/LZ77 compression ratios. skills.name: predictive-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: predictive-accuracy-evaluation Use when comparing a learned GP covariance structure against a fixed-kernel GP baseline on time series (e.g. synthetic series with known ground-truth kernel labels), and you need both point-prediction accuracy (RMSE) and uncertainty-calibration (interval coverage) metrics. The covariance structure is already known and fixed — gallifrey exists precisely for cases where the covariance function cannot be specified explicitly, so a learned-structure benchmark adds cost without information. No held-out data or ground-truth kernel labels exist, so RMSE and coverage against known structure cannot be computed and the paper's validation criterion cannot be evaluated. Datasets are large: the paper flags scalability to larger datasets (e.g. PLATO-scale) as future algorithmic work, so extrapolating the benchmark result to very large series is out of scope. Benchmark protocol for evaluating GP structure learning (gallifrey's SMC with involutive MCMC) against traditional fixed-kernel GP baselines using predictive RMSE and prediction-interval coverage, aggregated into a per-method comparison table. It operationalizes the paper's claim that structure learning has advantages in accuracy and uncertainty estimation. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202554518

The task is to run the full SMART Bayesian MCMC fit on observational data (e.g. Spitzer spectroscopy of HERUS ULIRGs) rather than to reimplement how its model space is assembled The input is photometric or spectroscopic galaxy data needing an SED fit, not the pre-computed radiative transfer library templates themselves A non-radiative-transfer model space (e.g. popular energy balance SED methods) is what must be reproduced Implement a Python 3.10 scientific module that reproduces a component of the SMART SED-fitting pipeline: loading the four pre-computed radiative transfer libraries (starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, polar dust) and combining scaled templates into a composite ultraviolet-to-millimetre galaxy SED. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stae1141

skills.description: Use when a task requires running a documented Python program (e.g. PyExoCross) over large spectroscopic line-list data (ExoMol, HITRAN, HITEMP formats) by configuring an input file and validating its generated output tables.
skills.name: python-scientific-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: python-scientific-workflow-execution Use when a task requires running a documented Python program (e.g. PyExoCross) over large spectroscopic line-list data (ExoMol, HITRAN, HITEMP formats) by configuring an input file and validating its generated output tables. The goal is spectral synthesis (stick spectra or cross-sections with Doppler/Gaussian/Lorentzian/Voigt profiles) rather than scalar property computation — enable the spectra/cross-section functions instead of lifetimes. The data are in HITRAN/HITEMP format and only format conversion between ExoMol and HITRAN is needed — use the Conversion function, not the lifetimes module. Line-list files are not present locally and must be fetched — use PyExoCross's batch-download code for ExoMol files before running post-processing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Executes a configured Python scientific post-processing program (PyExoCross) over a molecular line list by writing a structured input file, running `python run.py`, and validating the tabular outputs. The workflow covers directory layout, function flags, parallelism settings, and output checks for tasks such as computing radiative lifetimes from the 24Mg-1H Yadin ExoMol line list. astronomy/v1 10.1093/rasti/rzae016
skills.summary: Executes a configured Python scientific post-processing program (PyExoCross) over a molecular line list by writing a structured input file, running `python run.py`, and validating the tabular outputs. The workflow covers directory layout, function flags, parallelism settings, and output checks for tasks such as computing radiative lifetimes from the 24Mg-1H Yadin ExoMol line list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is spectral synthesis (stick spectra or cross-sections with Doppler/Gaussian/Lorentzian/Voigt profiles) rather than scalar property computation — enable the spectra/cross-section functions instead of lifetimes. The data are in HITRAN/HITEMP format and only format conversion between ExoMol and HITRAN is needed — use the Conversion function, not the lifetimes module. Line-list files are not present locally and must be fetched — use PyExoCross's batch-download code for ExoMol files before running post-processing.

skills.description: Use when a Python (Larch) XAFS workflow has produced chi(k) from autobk background subtraction and you must compute and persist the chi(R) Fourier-transform spectrum plus its window parameters as a reusable CSV artifact.
skills.name: python-spectroscopy-data-export
skills.search_text: python-spectroscopy-data-export Use when a Python (Larch) XAFS workflow has produced chi(k) from autobk background subtraction and you must compute and persist the chi(R) Fourier-transform spectrum plus its window parameters as a reusable CSV artifact. The goal is EXAFS path fitting rather than spectrum export — use feffit with a feffit_transform (kmin=3, kmax=12, kweight=2, dk=4, kaiser window, rmin=1.0, rmax=3.0) instead of a standalone xftf export. The input is raw mu(E) data not yet background-subtracted — xftf requires chi(k) from autobk as input, so run the autobk step first. A back-transform from R-space to k-space is needed — use larch's xftr (e.g. rmin=1, rmax=3.3, dr=0.2, window='hanning') rather than xftf. Exports derived spectroscopy products — here the chi(R) spectrum produced by Larch's Fourier-transform stage of XAFS analysis — from Python into a plain CSV file together with the processing parameters (FT window type, kmin, kmax, dk, kweight) needed to reproduce it. astronomy/v1 10.1088/1742-6596/430/1/012007
skills.summary: Exports derived spectroscopy products — here the chi(R) spectrum produced by Larch's Fourier-transform stage of XAFS analysis — from Python into a plain CSV file together with the processing parameters (FT window type, kmin, kmax, dk, kweight) needed to reproduce it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is EXAFS path fitting rather than spectrum export — use feffit with a feffit_transform (kmin=3, kmax=12, kweight=2, dk=4, kaiser window, rmin=1.0, rmax=3.0) instead of a standalone xftf export. The input is raw mu(E) data not yet background-subtracted — xftf requires chi(k) from autobk as input, so run the autobk step first. A back-transform from R-space to k-space is needed — use larch's xftr (e.g. rmin=1, rmax=3.3, dr=0.2, window='hanning') rather than xftf.

skills.description: Use when a websocket-based web application must execute user-submitted tasks such that variables defined in an earlier task remain in memory for later tasks on the same connection, but each session's state must be isolated from other sessions and from the web server process.
skills.name: python-subprocess-orchestration
skills.search_text: python-subprocess-orchestration Use when a websocket-based web application must execute user-submitted tasks such that variables defined in an earlier task remain in memory for later tasks on the same connection, but each session's state must be isolated from other sessions and from the web server process. Tasks are independent one-shot jobs whose state need not persist across requests — the original per-job subprocess (destroyed on completion) is sufficient The analysis runs entirely client-side; Toyz exists so users can interact with data stored on a remote server without installing local software, so local-only analysis gains nothing from this session layer The task module is not granted permission for the user or does not end in tasks.py — the dispatch path must refuse it rather than spawn/route it http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Reconstructs a workspace-as-process layer in which each client session (browser window/tab) runs as a dedicated Python subprocess on the server, persisting the user's in-memory variables across sequential tasks while remaining isolated from the Tornado web application layer, as implemented in the Toyz framework. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.10.001
skills.summary: Reconstructs a workspace-as-process layer in which each client session (browser window/tab) runs as a dedicated Python subprocess on the server, persisting the user's in-memory variables across sequential tasks while remaining isolated from the Tornado web application layer, as implemented in the Toyz framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tasks are independent one-shot jobs whose state need not persist across requests — the original per-job subprocess (destroyed on completion) is sufficient The analysis runs entirely client-side; Toyz exists so users can interact with data stored on a remote server without installing local software, so local-only analysis gains nothing from this session layer The task module is not granted permission for the user or does not end in tasks.py — the dispatch path must refuse it rather than spawn/route it

skills.search_text: pytorch-module-construction Use when a training pipeline must accept a user-configurable neural backbone, e.g. when input images are small/low-resolution and the full ResNet18 (layer1–layer4) is too deep, or the backbone must be chosen from a config file. Input images are large/high-resolution and benefit from the full four-stage ResNet18 receptive field — keep the default (no last_layer). The goal is a ready-made backbone without custom depth control — the package's built-in AstroMorphologyModel or the streamlined training script already suffices. The task needs a non-ResNet architecture family; this skill only implements truncation of ResNet18's four convolutional stages.

skills.description: Use when you have a small (n≈7–13) compound set with measured or extrapolated vapour pressures plus a molecular descriptor (MW or intrinsic molar volume) and need to fit and validate a linear lnP–descriptor relationship.
skills.name: qspr-property-relationship-fitting
skills.search_text: qspr-property-relationship-fitting Use when you have a small (n≈7–13) compound set with measured or extrapolated vapour pressures plus a molecular descriptor (MW or intrinsic molar volume) and need to fit and validate a linear lnP–descriptor relationship. The target property involves triorganostannanes — published vapour pressure values vary considerably and applicability of Equation (9) to triorganostannanes is uncertain The compounds are solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) — Equation (9) data need conversion to solid vapour pressure using entropy of fusion (ΔSf) and melting point, an extra required input You need an MW-based relationship transferable between hydrocarbons and tetraorganostannanes — existing MW relationships for hydrocarbons cannot be used with tetraorganostannanes http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 Fits ordinary least-squares QSPR regressions of lnP (kPa) against molecular weight and intrinsic molar volume for tetraorganostannanes plus hydrocarbons, reproducing Hawker (1992) Equations 8 and 9 from GC-derived vapour pressure data. astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w
skills.summary: Fits ordinary least-squares QSPR regressions of lnP (kPa) against molecular weight and intrinsic molar volume for tetraorganostannanes plus hydrocarbons, reproducing Hawker (1992) Equations 8 and 9 from GC-derived vapour pressure data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target property involves triorganostannanes — published vapour pressure values vary considerably and applicability of Equation (9) to triorganostannanes is uncertain The compounds are solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) — Equation (9) data need conversion to solid vapour pressure using entropy of fusion (ΔSf) and melting point, an extra required input You need an MW-based relationship transferable between hydrocarbons and tetraorganostannanes — existing MW relationships for hydrocarbons cannot be used with tetraorganostannanes

skills.description: Use when experimental property data exist for organometallic compounds (e.g. tetraorganostannane vapour pressures) and you must decide whether hydrocarbon-derived estimation methods are adequate, or when extrapolating GC-measured vapour pressures below the measured range.
skills.name: qspr-transferability-assessment-hydrocarbons-to-organostannanes
skills.search_text: qspr-transferability-assessment-hydrocarbons-to-organostannanes Use when experimental property data exist for organometallic compounds (e.g. tetraorganostannane vapour pressures) and you must decide whether hydrocarbon-derived estimation methods are adequate, or when extrapolating GC-measured vapour pressures below the measured range. When no appropriate boiling point data exist for the compound or its hydrocarbon analogue — the paper notes adequacy for other tetraalkyl/alkenylstannanes is uncertain 'because of lack of appropriate boiling point data' When the relationship of interest depends on molecular weight — the article states existing MW-based hydrocarbon relationships 'can not be used with tetraorganostannanes' For solid tetraorganostannanes (MP > 25°C) without conversion, since Equation (9) data must be transformed to solid vapour pressure using entropy of fusion and melting point A method for testing whether QSPR/estimation relationships calibrated on hydrocarbons can predict physicochemical properties (here, 20°C vapour pressures) of organometallic analogues (tetraorganostannanes) by substituting carbon for the central Sn atom and applying hydrocarbon-based estimators (Antoine equation, Modified Watson correlation). astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w
skills.summary: A method for testing whether QSPR/estimation relationships calibrated on hydrocarbons can predict physicochemical properties (here, 20°C vapour pressures) of organometallic analogues (tetraorganostannanes) by substituting carbon for the central Sn atom and applying hydrocarbon-based estimators (Antoine equation, Modified Watson correlation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no appropriate boiling point data exist for the compound or its hydrocarbon analogue — the paper notes adequacy for other tetraalkyl/alkenylstannanes is uncertain 'because of lack of appropriate boiling point data' When the relationship of interest depends on molecular weight — the article states existing MW-based hydrocarbon relationships 'can not be used with tetraorganostannanes' For solid tetraorganostannanes (MP > 25°C) without conversion, since Equation (9) data must be transformed to solid vapour pressure using entropy of fusion and melting point

The spectrum has not been cross-correlated against templates yet — there are no correlation peaks to interpolate around The analysis goal is interactive, human-guided redshifting (manual template comparison or feature marking), where automatic peak ranking and refinement are not the primary mechanism http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Refinement step in Marz's autoz cross-correlation pipeline: after ranking all template correlation peaks together, a quadratic fit is applied around each of the ten highest correlation peaks to determine local maxima at sub-pixel precision, yielding more accurate redshift candidates. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2016.03.001

skills.search_text: quantum-scattering-output-validation Use when a MOLSCAT calculation delegates potential terms to a user VSTAR routine via negative NTERM entries, and you must verify that the printed POTENL expansion matches the expected radial coefficients before accepting the run. skills.when_to_use_negative: Potential terms are supplied entirely by input data (positive NTERM/NPOWER/A in &POTL) with no VSTAR plug-in — there is no user routine to validate The calculation uses a special-purpose potential data file variant (e.g. molscat-Mg_NH or molscat-H2_H2 executables with data/ files) rather than the general-purpose POTENL with user VSTAR terms The goal is validating scattering observables (S matrices, cross sections, scattering lengths) rather than the potential expansion itself

skills.description: Use when input is generic FITS spectra (e.g. from AAOmega or any spectrograph following the Marz format) that need automatic redshifts and correlation peaks, particularly for quasars or mixed stellar/galaxy target types, including low signal-to-noise data.
skills.name: quasar-spectrum-template-matching
skills.search_text: quasar-spectrum-template-matching Use when input is generic FITS spectra (e.g. from AAOmega or any spectrograph following the Marz format) that need automatic redshifts and correlation peaks, particularly for quasars or mixed stellar/galaxy target types, including low signal-to-noise data. Input spectra are not in the well-defined Marz FITS input format and cannot be converted — Marz 'has since been generalised to take spectra from any spectrograph, given it follows a well defined input format' Redshifts must be derived from emission-line catalogues alone rather than full-spectrum template cross-correlation (use feature-marking/manual approaches instead) The task requires nonlinear spectral fitting or PCA-based redshifting of photometric data — this skill is strictly a Fourier-space template cross-correlation method An automatic spectroscopic redshift pipeline (Marz) that preprocesses FITS spectra along dual general/quasar paths and matches them against twelve stellar and galaxy templates using a modified autoz cross-correlation algorithm, ranking peaks and refining redshifts. It replaced runz, raising automatic matching performance on OzDES spectra from 54% to 91%. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2016.03.001
skills.summary: An automatic spectroscopic redshift pipeline (Marz) that preprocesses FITS spectra along dual general/quasar paths and matches them against twelve stellar and galaxy templates using a modified autoz cross-correlation algorithm, ranking peaks and refining redshifts. It replaced runz, raising automatic matching performance on OzDES spectra from 54% to 91%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input spectra are not in the well-defined Marz FITS input format and cannot be converted — Marz 'has since been generalised to take spectra from any spectrograph, given it follows a well defined input format' Redshifts must be derived from emission-line catalogues alone rather than full-spectrum template cross-correlation (use feature-marking/manual approaches instead) The task requires nonlinear spectral fitting or PCA-based redshifting of photometric data — this skill is strictly a Fourier-space template cross-correlation method

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending the 3D quasigeostrophic baroclinic instability example, or when studying the statistically saturated state of a sea of compact eddies that form, merge, and break up over several dynamical times.
skills.name: quasigeostrophic-flow-simulation
skills.search_text: quasigeostrophic-flow-simulation Use when reproducing or extending the 3D quasigeostrophic baroclinic instability example, or when studying the statistically saturated state of a sea of compact eddies that form, merge, and break up over several dynamical times. When the target is a linear/eigenvalue problem (e.g. Rayleigh-Benard growth rates or pipe flow eigenvalues) rather than nonlinear time integration of quasigeostrophic dynamics When the flow has not been integrated long enough to saturate — before t=200 the solution does not yet exhibit the compact-eddy statistically saturated state When working with non-spectral discretizations or non-Dedalus PDE frameworks, since the example relies on Dedalus's symbolic equation entry and compiled sparse solvers Reproduce the Dedalus 3D quasigeostrophic baroclinic instability example by spectrally evolving the potential vorticity (p) and buoyancy (w) fields on a 256x128x32-mode domain with Ekman pumping boundary conditions and depth-dependent stratification, integrating to t=200 to reach the statistically saturated state. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.023068
skills.summary: Reproduce the Dedalus 3D quasigeostrophic baroclinic instability example by spectrally evolving the potential vorticity (p) and buoyancy (w) fields on a 256x128x32-mode domain with Ekman pumping boundary conditions and depth-dependent stratification, integrating to t=200 to reach the statistically saturated state.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target is a linear/eigenvalue problem (e.g. Rayleigh-Benard growth rates or pipe flow eigenvalues) rather than nonlinear time integration of quasigeostrophic dynamics When the flow has not been integrated long enough to saturate — before t=200 the solution does not yet exhibit the compact-eddy statistically saturated state When working with non-spectral discretizations or non-Dedalus PDE frameworks, since the example relies on Dedalus's symbolic equation entry and compiled sparse solvers

skills.description: Use when implementing or exporting a Bayesian MCMC sampler as a reusable R function module, specifically a Differential Evolution Markov Chain (DE-MC) sampler for real parameter spaces.
skills.name: r-function-module-development
skills.search_text: r-function-module-development Use when implementing or exporting a Bayesian MCMC sampler as a reusable R function module, specifically a Differential Evolution Markov Chain (DE-MC) sampler for real parameter spaces. skills.summary: Implements the Marz Figure of Merit (FOM) quality classifier that converts the two highest cross-correlation peak strengths (v1, v2) from the modified autoz matcher into a suggested Quality of Match (QOP 1-6) grade for automatic redshifts, using the paper's FOM thresholds (alpha=2.5, beta=0.75).

skills.description: Use when you have simulated SEDm cubes with known input host redshifts and want to verify that a redshift measured from the HyperGal-isolated host component is consistent with simulation truth.
skills.name: redshift-residual-validation-against-simulation-truth
skills.search_text: redshift-residual-validation-against-simulation-truth Use when you have simulated SEDm cubes with known input host redshifts and want to verify that a redshift measured from the HyperGal-isolated host component is consistent with simulation truth. Real (non-simulated) observations: there is no z_input truth value, so residual validation against simulation truth cannot be performed Hosts that already have an external spectroscopic redshift (e.g. from SDSS, precision sigma_z ~ 1e-5): the pipeline-internal redshift at sigma_z ~ 5e-3 offers no advantage Hosts whose emission lines (e.g. Halpha) fall outside the [4000,8000] Å SEDm wavelength domain at the redshift of interest Validates an in-pipeline host redshift estimate — obtained from the host component isolated by HyperGal's fitted scene model — by comparing it to the known simulation input redshift within the SNID precision sigma_z ~ 5e-3. This operationalizes the paper's sanctioned future-work extension that replaces HyperGal's external-redshift input. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202244740
skills.summary: Validates an in-pipeline host redshift estimate — obtained from the host component isolated by HyperGal's fitted scene model — by comparing it to the known simulation input redshift within the SNID precision sigma_z ~ 5e-3. This operationalizes the paper's sanctioned future-work extension that replaces HyperGal's external-redshift input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real (non-simulated) observations: there is no z_input truth value, so residual validation against simulation truth cannot be performed Hosts that already have an external spectroscopic redshift (e.g. from SDSS, precision sigma_z ~ 1e-5): the pipeline-internal redshift at sigma_z ~ 5e-3 offers no advantage Hosts whose emission lines (e.g. Halpha) fall outside the [4000,8000] Å SEDm wavelength domain at the redshift of interest

skills.description: Use when reconstructing a model redshift-space 2PCF ξ(s) from a power spectrum with RSD, de-wiggled BAO wiggles, and Gaussian redshift errors, e.g. for BAO fitting with CosmoBolognaLib.
skills.name: redshift-space-power-spectrum-modelling
skills.search_text: redshift-space-power-spectrum-modelling Use when reconstructing a model redshift-space 2PCF ξ(s) from a power spectrum with RSD, de-wiggled BAO wiggles, and Gaussian redshift errors, e.g. for BAO fitting with CosmoBolognaLib. The task is measuring ξ(s) from an observed galaxy catalogue (pair counting with the chain-mesh algorithm), not constructing a model power-spectrum-based 2PCF Only real-space clustering is required — the µ-dependent RSD terms and redshift-error damping σ are not needed The Python wrapper is required for the specific modelling function, since only a subset of CBL functions currently has a Python wrapper Model the angle-averaged two-point correlation function of cosmic tracers in redshift space by constructing the redshift-space power spectrum P(k,µ) (Eq. 16) with the linear growth rate f and Gaussian redshift-error damping σ, applying the de-wiggled BAO prescription (Eq. 23, Sigma_NL), and Fourier anti-transforming the µ-integrated multipoles (Eqs. 20–22) using CosmoBolognaLib modelling classes. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2016.01.005
skills.summary: Model the angle-averaged two-point correlation function of cosmic tracers in redshift space by constructing the redshift-space power spectrum P(k,µ) (Eq. 16) with the linear growth rate f and Gaussian redshift-error damping σ, applying the de-wiggled BAO prescription (Eq. 23, Sigma_NL), and Fourier anti-transforming the µ-integrated multipoles (Eqs. 20–22) using CosmoBolognaLib modelling classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is measuring ξ(s) from an observed galaxy catalogue (pair counting with the chain-mesh algorithm), not constructing a model power-spectrum-based 2PCF Only real-space clustering is required — the µ-dependent RSD terms and redshift-error damping σ are not needed The Python wrapper is required for the specific modelling function, since only a subset of CBL functions currently has a Python wrapper

skills.description: Use when measuring higher-order clustering of a simulated or observed galaxy/halo catalogue, specifically when ζ and the reduced 3PCF Q are needed as functions of triangle opening angle θ at fixed sides r12, r13.
skills.name: reduced-3pcf-normalization
skills.search_text: reduced-3pcf-normalization Use when measuring higher-order clustering of a simulated or observed galaxy/halo catalogue, specifically when ζ and the reduced 3PCF Q are needed as functions of triangle opening angle θ at fixed sides r12, r13. The analysis only requires two-point statistics — CBL's optimised 2PCF chain-mesh pair-counting pipeline is the appropriate path, not the 3PCF estimator The catalogue cannot be accompanied by a random catalogue, since the Szapudi-Szalay estimator requires DDD, DDR, DRR and RRR triplet counts Full Python-wrapper coverage of a specific CBL function is assumed — only a subset of CBL has a Python wrapper, so a C++ implementation may be required Measure the connected three-point correlation function ζ(r12, r23, r31) of a galaxy or halo catalogue with the Szapudi-Szalay (1998) estimator implemented in CosmoBolognaLib, then normalize it into the reduced 3PCF Q = ζ/(ξ12ξ23 + ξ23ξ31 + ξ31ξ12), fixing two triangle sides and binning in the opening angle θ. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2016.01.005
skills.summary: Measure the connected three-point correlation function ζ(r12, r23, r31) of a galaxy or halo catalogue with the Szapudi-Szalay (1998) estimator implemented in CosmoBolognaLib, then normalize it into the reduced 3PCF Q = ζ/(ξ12ξ23 + ξ23ξ31 + ξ31ξ12), fixing two triangle sides and binning in the opening angle θ.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only requires two-point statistics — CBL's optimised 2PCF chain-mesh pair-counting pipeline is the appropriate path, not the 3PCF estimator The catalogue cannot be accompanied by a random catalogue, since the Szapudi-Szalay estimator requires DDD, DDR, DRR and RRR triplet counts Full Python-wrapper coverage of a specific CBL function is assumed — only a subset of CBL has a Python wrapper, so a C++ implementation may be required

skills.description: Use when you need a goodness-of-fit metric proving that a timestream filtering step (e.g. destriping with 60-second baselines) removed low-frequency correlated noise without biasing the signal, given HEALPix residual maps for I/Q.
skills.name: reduced-chi2-map-goodness-of-fit
skills.search_text: reduced-chi2-map-goodness-of-fit Use when you need a goodness-of-fit metric proving that a timestream filtering step (e.g. destriping with 60-second baselines) removed low-frequency correlated noise without biasing the signal, given HEALPix residual maps for I/Q. Systematic effects such as thermally induced gain variations (e.g. sections near sunrise/sunset) have not been masked; the paper states such effects must be dealt with before map-making and destriping can be 'ineffective of even harmful' there The noise properties of the timestream are unknown, so no expected white-noise level exists against which the reduced chi2 of the residual map can be normalized Validates a CMB map-making (destriping) pipeline by computing the reduced chi2 of residual maps — the difference between output maps and the input smoothed signal — for I and Q, expecting destriped residuals to fall to the white-noise level (~1.0) while plain binning leaves correlated-noise excess (~1.05). astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.10.002
skills.summary: Validates a CMB map-making (destriping) pipeline by computing the reduced chi2 of residual maps — the difference between output maps and the input smoothed signal — for I and Q, expecting destriped residuals to fall to the white-noise level (~1.0) while plain binning leaves correlated-noise excess (~1.05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Systematic effects such as thermally induced gain variations (e.g. sections near sunrise/sunset) have not been masked; the paper states such effects must be dealt with before map-making and destriping can be 'ineffective of even harmful' there The noise properties of the timestream are unknown, so no expected white-noise level exists against which the reduced chi2 of the residual map can be normalized

skills.description: Use when you have independently derived a rounding granularity g and precision-reduced radio data from Equations 14-16 and must confirm your values match the authors' kiyo-masui/bitshuffle example before trusting downstream compression results.
skills.name: reference-implementation-consistency-check
skills.search_text: reference-implementation-consistency-check Use when you have independently derived a rounding granularity g and precision-reduced radio data from Equations 14-16 and must confirm your values match the authors' kiyo-masui/bitshuffle example before trusting downstream compression results. Data are not radiometer-equation-limited (e.g. post-calibration or systematics-dominated data), since the noise scale s from Equation 14 no longer bounds rounding noise meaningfully. Data are uncorrelated between adjacent elements, where Bitshuffle-style reference tooling gains nothing and the consistency check target codepath does not apply. A quick lossy-compression comparison is needed instead of exact consistency with the paper's nearly-lossless rounding step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Validates a self-implemented controlled precision-reduction (radiometer-relative rounding) procedure by comparing the chosen power-of-two granularity and the rounded integer values against the authors' released example code in the kiyo-masui/bitshuffle repository. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.07.002
skills.summary: Validates a self-implemented controlled precision-reduction (radiometer-relative rounding) procedure by comparing the chosen power-of-two granularity and the rounded integer values against the authors' released example code in the kiyo-masui/bitshuffle repository.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not radiometer-equation-limited (e.g. post-calibration or systematics-dominated data), since the noise scale s from Equation 14 no longer bounds rounding noise meaningfully. Data are uncorrelated between adjacent elements, where Bitshuffle-style reference tooling gains nothing and the consistency check target codepath does not apply. A quick lossy-compression comparison is needed instead of exact consistency with the paper's nearly-lossless rounding step.
