skills.search_text: reference-output-consistency-checking Use when a tool is supposed to reproduce known reference outputs (e.g. after re-running a conversion under new Galactic parameters R0=7.5 or 8.5 kpc) and you must confirm the regenerated files match shipped samples. When validating the raw data files galkin/data/data_*.dat or output/rawdata.dat directly — these are given as in the original references and are deliberately NOT normalised to the selected input parameters, so comparison against converted reference outputs is invalid. skills.search_text: reference-output-diff-comparison Use when a paper prints a human-readable reference listing (e.g. an AST Channel block-structured serialisation) and the goal is to reproduce that exact text with library code and validate it by diff. skills.description: Use when comparing implicit ODE solvers or tolerance settings on a stiff system (e.g. the Einstein-Boltzmann background) and you need a quantitative, solver-independent accuracy metric rather than trusting each solver's own tolerance claims.
skills.name: reference-solution-error-norm-computation
skills.search_text: reference-solution-error-norm-computation Use when comparing implicit ODE solvers or tolerance settings on a stiff system (e.g. the Einstein-Boltzmann background) and you need a quantitative, solver-independent accuracy metric rather than trusting each solver's own tolerance claims. When the goal is agreement of physical spectra (P(k), C_l) with an established code like CLASS at the 0.1% level — that requires spectrum comparison, not time-grid L2 error When only a single production solve is needed and no solver/tolerance selection or benchmarking is intended When the ODE system is non-stiff and explicit methods are appropriate — implicit high-order solvers with sparse Jacobians would be unnecessary overhead Benchmark ODE solver accuracy by solving a system once at very tight tolerances to obtain a reference solution, then quantifying each solver/tolerance configuration by the L2 norm error of its solution interpolated onto the reference time grid. This is the method behind the work-precision diagram comparing Rodas4/4P/5/5P/6P, FBDF and QNDF on SymBoltz's background equations. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202557450
skills.summary: Benchmark ODE solver accuracy by solving a system once at very tight tolerances to obtain a reference solution, then quantifying each solver/tolerance configuration by the L2 norm error of its solution interpolated onto the reference time grid. This is the method behind the work-precision diagram comparing Rodas4/4P/5/5P/6P, FBDF and QNDF on SymBoltz's background equations.

skills.description: Use when simulating in-ice radio-neutrino detection where signal propagation depends on the medium's depth-dependent index-of-refraction profile, e.g. ray-tracing neutrino-interaction vertices to antennas in NuRadioMC.
skills.name: refractive-index-medium-modeling
skills.search_text: refractive-index-medium-modeling Use when simulating in-ice radio-neutrino detection where signal propagation depends on the medium's depth-dependent index-of-refraction profile, e.g. ray-tracing neutrino-interaction vertices to antennas in NuRadioMC. The medium's index-of-refraction profile is arbitrary 3D and you are not prepared to use the RadioPropa numerical ray tracer — the default ray tracer is not built for that case. The task concerns radio-emission modelling or detector/trigger response (handled by NuRadioReco within NuRadioMC), not propagation of the signal through the ice. Birefringence effects in the ice must be modelled — this requires the separate first-principle birefringence calculation added to NuRadioMC by Heyer & Glaser (2023). http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Define and apply the refractive-index (firn/ice) profile of the propagation medium so that NuRadioMC can ray-trace Askaryan radio signals from neutrino-interaction vertices to every antenna, enumerating valid ray-path solutions with their path lengths, arrival times, and amplitude factors. astronomy/v1 10.1140/epjc/s10052-020-7612-8
skills.summary: Define and apply the refractive-index (firn/ice) profile of the propagation medium so that NuRadioMC can ray-trace Askaryan radio signals from neutrino-interaction vertices to every antenna, enumerating valid ray-path solutions with their path lengths, arrival times, and amplitude factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The medium's index-of-refraction profile is arbitrary 3D and you are not prepared to use the RadioPropa numerical ray tracer — the default ray tracer is not built for that case. The task concerns radio-emission modelling or detector/trigger response (handled by NuRadioReco within NuRadioMC), not propagation of the signal through the ice. Birefringence effects in the ice must be modelled — this requires the separate first-principle birefringence calculation added to NuRadioMC by Heyer & Glaser (2023).

skills.description: Use when comparing neural differential equation models on irregularly sampled time-series regression tasks (e.g. BIDMC respiratory rate, heart rate, SpO2) and you must report test-set L2 loss (mean ± std over seeds) plus training time.
skills.name: regression-l2-loss-evaluation
skills.search_text: regression-l2-loss-evaluation Use when comparing neural differential equation models on irregularly sampled time-series regression tasks (e.g. BIDMC respiratory rate, heart rate, SpO2) and you must report test-set L2 loss (mean ± std over seeds) plus training time. The task is classification or probabilistic/generative evaluation rather than regression — L2 loss and this mean ± std protocol are specific to regression error. There is no held-out test split or no multiple seeds available, so the mean ± standard deviation over seeds cannot be computed as the protocol requires. skills.search_text: resolution-dependent-model-agreement-analysis Use when validating a new or faster galactic kinematic modelling tool against an established code, or when you need to know how beam smearing (PSF FWHM relative to R_eff) affects agreement between two mock-observed rotation/dispersion curve predictions. skills.summary: Benchmark a fast parametric rotation-curve forward-modelling code (RotCurves) against an established reference code (dysmalpy) by mock-observing an identical fiducial galaxy mass model at different resolutions and comparing beam-smeared rotation and dispersion curves out to 3R_eff, while recording single-realization runtime ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The galaxy is not an axisymmetric, rotationally supported disk (V/sigma_0 >= 2) with a well-defined kinematic axis and no strong deviations from circular motions The system is unresolved (beam size much larger than the disk effective radius), where beam-smearing corrections break down and discrepancies reach ~15 per cent even between codes You need full 3D data-cube forward modelling rather than 1D rotation-curve comparison, since this benchmark only compares mock-observed 1D rotation and dispersion curves

skills.search_text: retention-ratio-vapour-pressure-analysis Use when isothermal GC retention times (40–120°C, 20°C increments) are available for a homologous compound series plus a reference compound with known ΔHv, and relative vaporization thermodynamics are needed. skills.search_text: reverse-mode-automatic-differentiation Use when a loss depends on the solution of a neural ODE or neural CDE solve in Diffrax/JAX and gradients w.r.t. y0 or parameters are needed, especially when long time series would exhaust memory with discretise-then-optimise. Memory is not a constraint and the solve has few steps: backpropagating through the solver internals (discretise-then-optimise with RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint) differentiates the exact discretisation actually used, with no adjoint-ODE approximation error The vector field or control interpolation is not smooth enough for the adjoint ODE derivation, e.g. unmeasurable controls where even rectilinear interpolation properties are insufficient The task is training rather than verification of the adjoint method itself — use the library's built-in adjoint handling instead of hand-deriving a reverse-mode solver Backpropagates gradients through a numerical ODE/CDE solve either by autodiff through the solver internals (discretise-then-optimise, e.g. Diffrax's RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint) or via a continuous adjoint solved backwards in time (optimise-then-discretise, e.g. Diffrax's BacksolveAdjoint), which is required for constant-memory gradients on long time series. astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2202.02435
skills.summary: Backpropagates gradients through a numerical ODE/CDE solve either by autodiff through the solver internals (discretise-then-optimise, e.g. Diffrax's RecursiveCheckpointAdjoint) or via a continuous adjoint solved backwards in time (optimise-then-discretise, e.g. Diffrax's BacksolveAdjoint), which is required for constant-memory gradients on long time series.

skills.description: Use when a scalar loss function (e.g. weighted χ² over P(k) on a log-spaced k-grid) must be differentiated with respect to many cosmological parameters and forward-mode AD is too slow, i.e. gradient-based MCMC, Fisher forecasting or emulator training in large parameter spaces.
skills.name: reverse-mode-automatic-differentiation-implementation
skills.search_text: reverse-mode-automatic-differentiation-implementation Use when a scalar loss function (e.g. weighted χ² over P(k) on a log-spaced k-grid) must be differentiated with respect to many cosmological parameters and forward-mode AD is too slow, i.e. gradient-based MCMC, Fisher forecasting or emulator training in large parameter spaces. skills.when_to_use_negative: The quantity to differentiate is a vector-valued output (e.g. log power spectra themselves) rather than a scalar loss — ForwardDiff.jacobian on the output is already supported by SymBoltz Only a handful of input parameters are differentiated, so forward-mode AD cost does not dominate and reverse mode offers no advantage The model was not compiled with an analytical sparse Jacobian (jac = true, sparse = true), which the paper identifies as key to differentiable performance

skills.name: rime-per-antenna-coherency-computation
skills.search_text: rime-per-antenna-coherency-computation Use when simulating radio-interferometric visibilities from a sky model of point and Gaussian sources, or when a χ²/likelihood must be computed from model vs observed visibilities for Bayesian inference (BIRO). Data is not fully calibrated: evaluation of the direction-independent gain (G_ps DIE) matrices is not included in Montblanc, and E_ps (DDE) terms are substituted with analytic expressions rather than full matrix evaluation Problem requires multi-GPU or clustered execution: only single GPUs are currently supported Source morphology outside point or Gaussian shapes (e.g. beta profiles) is needed, as other morphologies are only future additions Computes the Radio Interferometer Measurement Equation (RIME) by first evaluating expensive per-antenna terms A[t,p,s,λ] (EK kernel), combining them into per-baseline source coherencies and 3D model visibilities (B Sum kernel), and reducing to a single χ² scalar. This factored decomposition is what makes Montblanc's GPU-accelerated BIRO workflow tractable. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.06.003
skills.summary: Computes the Radio Interferometer Measurement Equation (RIME) by first evaluating expensive per-antenna terms A[t,p,s,λ] (EK kernel), combining them into per-baseline source coherencies and 3D model visibilities (B Sum kernel), and reducing to a single χ² scalar. This factored decomposition is what makes Montblanc's GPU-accelerated BIRO workflow tractable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not fully calibrated: evaluation of the direction-independent gain (G_ps DIE) matrices is not included in Montblanc, and E_ps (DDE) terms are substituted with analytic expressions rather than full matrix evaluation Problem requires multi-GPU or clustered execution: only single GPUs are currently supported Source morphology outside point or Gaussian shapes (e.g. beta profiles) is needed, as other morphologies are only future additions

skills.search_text: robust-pca-dimensionality-reduction Use when correlated multi-band magnitudes (e.g. PHAT0 u'g'r'i'z' or SDSS DR10 photometry) must be compressed into uncorrelated PCs before fitting a gamma GLM with log link for photo-z prediction. When the user's simple formulation without interaction terms is intended — the article notes such tests are inadequate in capturing the complexity of the data, so PCs alone without crossed GLM terms will underperform When exact cross-platform reproducibility of PC scores is required — the R and Python codes solve the SVD matrices slightly differently and this was not fully reconciled http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Robust principal component analysis applied to galaxy photometric magnitudes to produce uncorrelated principal components used as explanatory variables for gamma-family GLM photometric redshift estimation, with the number of PCs selected by a ~99.5% cumulative variance threshold. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.002

skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are clean and approximately Gaussian, so standard PCA via correlation-matrix diagonalization suffices and is cheaper The dataset is not importable as a CSV/TXT table with named columns (e.g., binary or ragged formats) The goal is clustering structure rather than linear dimension reduction — AMADA's hierarchical clustering over correlation matrices (Pearson, Spearman, or MIC) would be the appropriate mode

skills.description: Use when magnitudes fed into a regression (e.g. photometric redshift GLM) are correlated and you need uncorrelated explanatory variables computed robustly on combined training+test data.
skills.name: robust-principal-component-analysis
skills.search_text: robust-principal-component-analysis Use when magnitudes fed into a regression (e.g. photometric redshift GLM) are correlated and you need uncorrelated explanatory variables computed robustly on combined training+test data. When the covariates are already uncorrelated or physically independent inputs — PCA on the complete set would add unnecessary preprocessing and mixing between training and test samples. When the downstream model requires interpretable per-band coefficients — PCs of the magnitude set lose direct magnitude-level interpretation. When the goal is a simple formulation without interaction terms capturing data complexity — the paper notes such simple tests are inadequate, but if a strictly linear, band-wise model is required, PCs may not be the right explanatory variables. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Robust PCA (Candes et al. 2011-style) decorrelates galaxy magnitudes into principal components that serve as explanatory variables for a gamma-family, log-link GLM photo-z estimator. The number of retained components is chosen by a cumulative total-variance threshold of ~99.5%. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.002
skills.summary: Robust PCA (Candes et al. 2011-style) decorrelates galaxy magnitudes into principal components that serve as explanatory variables for a gamma-family, log-link GLM photo-z estimator. The number of retained components is chosen by a cumulative total-variance threshold of ~99.5%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the covariates are already uncorrelated or physically independent inputs — PCA on the complete set would add unnecessary preprocessing and mixing between training and test samples. When the downstream model requires interpretable per-band coefficients — PCs of the magnitude set lose direct magnitude-level interpretation. When the goal is a simple formulation without interaction terms capturing data complexity — the paper notes such simple tests are inadequate, but if a strictly linear, band-wise model is required, PCs may not be the right explanatory variables.

When a validated transfer function file is already supplied and hmf's default k-bounds are used unchanged and no convergence warning is raised — the check is redundant When the power spectrum is normalised via sigma_8 and non-top-hat filters (e.g. WDM-corrected T_WDM(k) and non-sharp-k windows) are the object of study; the 95% rule here is derived specifically for the top-hat window W(x) = 3(sin x - x cos x)/x^3 When the goal is a differential HMF fitting-function comparison (f(sigma) choice) rather than verifying the numerical integrals feeding σ(M) Reconstructs hmf's kR convergence-bound check on the mass-variance (σ(M)) window-function integrals: numerically integrating the unnormalised power spectrum P0(k)=k^n*T^2 against the top-hat window with Romberg integration, then deriving and testing the 95%-integral-fraction rule that yields k_min*R_max < 0.1 and k_max*R_min > 3. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.11.001

skills.description: Use when integrating a second-order linear ODE x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 whose frequency is high or rapidly oscillatory on part of the range but slowly varying elsewhere, and standard RK stepping would be prohibitively expensive.
skills.name: runge-kutta-hybrid-step-switching
skills.search_text: runge-kutta-hybrid-step-switching Use when integrating a second-order linear ODE x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 whose frequency is high or rapidly oscillatory on part of the range but slowly varying elsewhere, and standard RK stepping would be prohibitively expensive. The frequency changes rapidly relative to the timescales of integration over the whole range, violating the WKB validity condition so steps cannot skip oscillations. The problem is not of the oscillatory ODE form x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 that oscode's stepper targets. A non-oscillatory ODE is involved, where a plain Runge-Kutta solver is cheaper and the WKB machinery adds overhead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Implements oscode's hybrid stepping loop, which dynamically alternates between a Runge-Kutta estimate and an embedded WKB (analytic) approximation wherever the frequency w(t) varies slowly, so single steps can span many oscillation periods while staying accurate at high frequencies. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.013030
skills.summary: Implements oscode's hybrid stepping loop, which dynamically alternates between a Runge-Kutta estimate and an embedded WKB (analytic) approximation wherever the frequency w(t) varies slowly, so single steps can span many oscillation periods while staying accurate at high frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The frequency changes rapidly relative to the timescales of integration over the whole range, violating the WKB validity condition so steps cannot skip oscillations. The problem is not of the oscillatory ODE form x'' + g(t)x' + w(t)^2 x = 0 that oscode's stepper targets. A non-oscillatory ODE is involved, where a plain Runge-Kutta solver is cheaper and the WKB machinery adds overhead.

skills.name: runge-kutta-method-of-lines-time-integration
skills.search_text: runge-kutta-method-of-lines-time-integration Use when a conservative hyperbolic system (e.g. 1D SRHD charges q=(D,Sx,τ)) has been discretised in space with a finite-volume update and needs stable, higher-order-in-time evolution with CFL-safe step control. When the spatial discretisation has not been kept in conservative finite-volume form — the paper notes finite volume for the flux is required to avoid violating the entropy and Rankine–Hugoniot jump conditions When a fixed Δt would violate the CFL restriction λΔt/Δx < 1 at the finest resolution, e.g. Δt=0.01 with λΔt/Δx ≥ 1 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Time-integration skill that wraps the PVRS spatial discretisation (HLL fluxes with minmod reconstruction) as a semi-discrete right-hand side L(u) of ∂u/∂t = −L(u) and advances it with a 4th-order Runge-Kutta Method of Lines (MoL-RK4), as implemented in the aztekas solver for 1D relativistic hydrodynamics. astronomy/v1 10.1371/journal.pone.0195494

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the spatial discretisation has not been kept in conservative finite-volume form — the paper notes finite volume for the flux is required to avoid violating the entropy and Rankine–Hugoniot jump conditions When a fixed Δt would violate the CFL restriction λΔt/Δx < 1 at the finest resolution, e.g. Δt=0.01 with λΔt/Δx ≥ 1

skills.description: Use when a new fitting or analysis pipeline's computational cost must be compared against a reference method on a fixed sample, e.g. showing that SMART's radiative-transfer-only fitting of 42 HERUS ULIRG SEDs takes comparable time to popular energy balance methods.
skills.name: runtime-benchmark-measurement
skills.search_text: runtime-benchmark-measurement Use when a new fitting or analysis pipeline's computational cost must be compared against a reference method on a fixed sample, e.g. showing that SMART's radiative-transfer-only fitting of 42 HERUS ULIRG SEDs takes comparable time to popular energy balance methods. The reference method has been re-implemented locally with different settings — re-measure both rather than mixing your own timings with literature-reported values. The analysis goal is fitting accuracy or parameter recovery rather than computational cost — runtime benchmarking alone will not answer that. Method for measuring and comparing the wall-clock execution time of a scientific SED-fitting code (e.g. SMART's Bayesian MCMC fitting of radiative transfer libraries) against an established alternative method (e.g. energy balance fitting) on the same sample, to establish computational comparability. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stae1141
skills.summary: Method for measuring and comparing the wall-clock execution time of a scientific SED-fitting code (e.g. SMART's Bayesian MCMC fitting of radiative transfer libraries) against an established alternative method (e.g. energy balance fitting) on the same sample, to establish computational comparability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference method has been re-implemented locally with different settings — re-measure both rather than mixing your own timings with literature-reported values. The analysis goal is fitting accuracy or parameter recovery rather than computational cost — runtime benchmarking alone will not answer that.

skills.description: Use when you need per-object SALT2 stretch and colour from multi-band SN Ia light curves, or when you must locate the redshift above which survey selection effects bias fitted light-curve parameters.

skills.search_text: salt2-lightcurve-fitting Use when you need per-object SALT2 stretch and colour from multi-band SN Ia light curves, or when you must locate the redshift above which survey selection effects bias fitted light-curve parameters. The light curves are not SN Ia photometry or do not span enough of the rise and decline to constrain SALT2 stretch and colour The goal is raw survey/dataset generation (Target, Survey, DataSet construction) rather than light-curve parameter fitting The sample has already been restricted to a volume- and selection-unbiased regime, so a redshift-dependence study would be redundant Fit the SALT2 light-curve model to simulated or observed SN Ia photometry (g, r, i bands) with sncosmo to recover stretch (x1) and colour (c) per object, then study their redshift dependence. skills.description: Decision support for stopping or comparing MCMC runs: given autocorrelation times, walker counts, burn-in and sample lengths, determine whether the sample has reached a target error regime (e.g. the 10% level) versus a competing sampler's tuning endpoint.
skills.name: sampler-stopping-criterion-computation
skills.search_text: sampler-stopping-criterion-computation Decision support for stopping or comparing MCMC runs: given autocorrelation times, walker counts, burn-in and sample lengths, determine whether the sample has reached a target error regime (e.g. the 10% level) versus a competing sampler's tuning endpoint. When only a single fixed chain with no burn-in/autocorrelation metadata exists and no error target is specified — epsilon is undefined without b, n, L and tau When the goal is proposal tuning of a Metropolis–Hastings sampler (the article's comparison endpoint n = 2000 is specific to the self-tuning CosmoMC benchmark, not general proposal adaptation) Computes the statistical error epsilon of an MCMC ensemble sample from the autocorrelation time tau, burn-in length b, sequential steps n, and walker count L via epsilon = |2*tau/((n-b)*L)|^(1/2), to decide when sampling effort suffices (e.g. epsilon <= 0.1). astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.06.003
skills.summary: Computes the statistical error epsilon of an MCMC ensemble sample from the autocorrelation time tau, burn-in length b, sequential steps n, and walker count L via epsilon = |2*tau/((n-b)*L)|^(1/2), to decide when sampling effort suffices (e.g. epsilon <= 0.1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single fixed chain with no burn-in/autocorrelation metadata exists and no error target is specified — epsilon is undefined without b, n, L and tau When the goal is proposal tuning of a Metropolis–Hastings sampler (the article's comparison endpoint n = 2000 is specific to the self-tuning CosmoMC benchmark, not general proposal adaptation)

The goal is ab-initio neutron-to-proton conversion and light-element abundance (Yp, D/H) computation rather than the pure thermal background — that is a separate PRyMordial pipeline stage. skills.name: schirmer-aperture-mass-filter-convolution
skills.search_text: schirmer-aperture-mass-filter-convolution Use when a galaxy positions+ellipticities shear catalog must be turned into an aperture mass map for cluster detection, and an NFW-motivated radial filter (Schirmer 2007) with exponential cut-offs is appropriate. The analysis goal is the 2-pt angular correlation function — the ccogs angular_correlation package (with a chosen estimator and a flat random galaxy distribution) is the appropriate tool instead. skills.summary: Computes a 2-D aperture mass map from a weak-lensing shear catalog by convolving a Schirmer et al (2007) filter — an NFW profile with exponential cut-offs at zero and large radii — with the tangential shear field, using the GPU-based aperture_mass package of the ccogs suite.

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or decomposing a galaxy SED into starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, and polar dust radiative transfer components, e.g. to reproduce SMART's model space before Bayesian MCMC fitting.
skills.name: sed-component-modeling
skills.search_text: sed-component-modeling Use when reconstructing or decomposing a galaxy SED into starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, and polar dust radiative transfer components, e.g. to reproduce SMART's model space before Bayesian MCMC fitting. The SED fitting should be driven by non-radiative-transfer energy balance methods — SMART's model space is assembled exclusively from radiative transfer libraries, so this composition approach does not apply to purely empirical or parametric energy balance SED codes. The target is an individual library template rather than a multi-component composite SED summing starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, and polar dust contributions. Builds composite galaxy ultraviolet-to-millimetre spectral energy distributions by scaling and summing templates drawn exclusively from four pre-computed radiative transfer model libraries (starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, polar dust), as used in the SMART SED fitting code. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stae1141
skills.summary: Builds composite galaxy ultraviolet-to-millimetre spectral energy distributions by scaling and summing templates drawn exclusively from four pre-computed radiative transfer model libraries (starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, polar dust), as used in the SMART SED fitting code.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SED fitting should be driven by non-radiative-transfer energy balance methods — SMART's model space is assembled exclusively from radiative transfer libraries, so this composition approach does not apply to purely empirical or parametric energy balance SED codes. The target is an individual library template rather than a multi-component composite SED summing starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, and polar dust contributions.

skills.description: Use when SED fitting must combine spectroscopy (e.g. Spitzer IRS spectra) with photometry and radiative transfer model libraries whose wavelength grids are coarser than the observed spectra, requiring convolution/rebinning first.
skills.name: sed-fitting-input-preparation
skills.search_text: sed-fitting-input-preparation Use when SED fitting must combine spectroscopy (e.g. Spitzer IRS spectra) with photometry and radiative transfer model libraries whose wavelength grids are coarser than the observed spectra, requiring convolution/rebinning first. Input data are photometric points only — no spectroscopy needs convolution/rebinning to the model grid resolution. The spectra are already on the same spectral resolution grid as the radiative transfer model libraries and parse correctly in SMART's input reader. Fitting with non-radiative-transfer SED codes (e.g. energy balance methods) that do not use SMART's four pre-computed model libraries. http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Preprocess observational spectroscopy (e.g. Spitzer spectra of the 42 HERUS ULIRGs) to the spectral resolution of SMART's pre-computed radiative transfer model libraries (starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, polar dust) before Bayesian MCMC SED fitting, assembling resolution-matched spectra into a multi-extension FITS file. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stae1141
skills.summary: Preprocess observational spectroscopy (e.g. Spitzer spectra of the 42 HERUS ULIRGs) to the spectral resolution of SMART's pre-computed radiative transfer model libraries (starburst, AGN torus, host galaxy, polar dust) before Bayesian MCMC SED fitting, assembling resolution-matched spectra into a multi-extension FITS file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are photometric points only — no spectroscopy needs convolution/rebinning to the model grid resolution. The spectra are already on the same spectral resolution grid as the radiative transfer model libraries and parse correctly in SMART's input reader. Fitting with non-radiative-transfer SED codes (e.g. energy balance methods) that do not use SMART's four pre-computed model libraries.

skills.description: Use when a reduced SEDm (SEDmachine) IFU data cube of a ZTF transient is contaminated by host-galaxy flux near the host core, and a clean SN spectrum is needed for SNID typing.
skills.name: sedm-ifu-spectrum-extraction
skills.search_text: sedm-ifu-spectrum-extraction Use when a reduced SEDm (SEDmachine) IFU data cube of a ZTF transient is contaminated by host-galaxy flux near the host core, and a clean SN spectrum is needed for SNID typing. The transient is an isolated point source far from its host core — the standard PSF extraction (pysedm) suffices since contamination is not the limiting factor No pre-transient photometric host images are available to build the CIGALE hyperspectral galaxy model No external host redshift exists and in-pipeline redshift estimation is required — the paper notes 'the most limiting constraint from Hyper Gal is the need for an external redshift measurement of the host galaxy' Extracts a clean transient spectrum from SEDm IFU cubes using HyperGal, a fully chromatic scene modeler that fits a CIGALE-based hyperspectral host model plus a point-source SN and diffuse background, mitigating host contamination near the galaxy core. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202244740
skills.summary: Extracts a clean transient spectrum from SEDm IFU cubes using HyperGal, a fully chromatic scene modeler that fits a CIGALE-based hyperspectral host model plus a point-source SN and diffuse background, mitigating host contamination near the galaxy core.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The transient is an isolated point source far from its host core — the standard PSF extraction (pysedm) suffices since contamination is not the limiting factor No pre-transient photometric host images are available to build the CIGALE hyperspectral galaxy model No external host redshift exists and in-pipeline redshift estimation is required — the paper notes 'the most limiting constraint from Hyper Gal is the need for an external redshift measurement of the host galaxy'

skills.name: sedm-spectral-rebinning
skills.search_text: sedm-spectral-rebinning Use when a CIGALE-based hyperspectral host model must be matched to SEDm low-resolution IFS data: the model cube's native spectral grid differs from the SEDm ~26 A/px sampling and [3700, 9300] A domain and must be rebinned before scene-model fitting. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target instrument is not SEDm — the [3700, 9300] A domain and ~26 A/px binning are specific to the SEDm spectro-spatial observation space When no external host redshift is available — HyperGal/CIGALE fitting requires an external redshift measurement as input, and the rebinning step depends on the fitted model When the goal is a posteriori host measurements (e.g. redshift or local Halpha flux) from SEDm residuals — the residual host component cannot support such measurements

skills.description: Use when the task requires evolving 3D hydrodynamic systems with Newtonian self-gravity (e.g., oscillating stars, single/binary stars) via SPH and need reproducible particle evolutions across particle counts.
skills.name: self-gravitating-hydrodynamics-simulation
skills.search_text: self-gravitating-hydrodynamics-simulation Use when the task requires evolving 3D hydrodynamic systems with Newtonian self-gravity (e.g., oscillating stars, single/binary stars) via SPH and need reproducible particle evolutions across particle counts. Problem lacks self-gravity and is covered by pure-hydro examples (Sod shock tube 1D/2D/3D, Noh 2D/3D, Sedov 2D/3D, airfoil) — use the hydro_{1-2-3}d drivers instead of newtonian A non-MPI or task-based runtime (Legion, Kokkos) is required — the current FleCSPH version is limited to only the MPI backend Exact N-body gravitational forces are required — FMM's first-order multipole expansion conserves linear momentum but exact angular momentum only at first order http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Run SPH simulations of self-gravitating astrophysical systems (e.g., oscillating stars) with FleCSPH, using FleCSI's parallel octree and FMM for gravity, from initial-data generation through H5part output of evolution diagnostics. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.softx.2020.100602
skills.summary: Run SPH simulations of self-gravitating astrophysical systems (e.g., oscillating stars) with FleCSPH, using FleCSI's parallel octree and FMM for gravity, from initial-data generation through H5part output of evolution diagnostics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Problem lacks self-gravity and is covered by pure-hydro examples (Sod shock tube 1D/2D/3D, Noh 2D/3D, Sedov 2D/3D, airfoil) — use the hydro_{1-2-3}d drivers instead of newtonian A non-MPI or task-based runtime (Legion, Kokkos) is required — the current FleCSPH version is limited to only the MPI backend Exact N-body gravitational forces are required — FMM's first-order multipole expansion conserves linear momentum but exact angular momentum only at first order

skills.description: Use when a 3D self-gravitating particle problem (e.g. single/binary stars, Noh 3D) must be evolved under Newtonian gravity with SPH, with initial data generated and snapshots stored in H5part.
skills.name: self-gravitating-particle-system-evolution
skills.search_text: self-gravitating-particle-system-evolution Use when a 3D self-gravitating particle problem (e.g. single/binary stars, Noh 3D) must be evolved under Newtonian gravity with SPH, with initial data generated and snapshots stored in H5part. The problem is a pure hydrodynamics test without gravity (e.g. 1D/2D Sod tube or Sedov blast) — use the hydro_{1-2-3}d drivers instead of newtonian_3d Higher-than-first-order multipole accuracy is required — FleCSPH implements only the first order of the multipole expansion, at which angular momentum is conserved exactly A non-MPI runtime backend (Legion, Kokkos) is required — the current FleCSPH version is limited to only the MPI backend http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Evolve a 3D self-gravitating SPH particle system with FleCSPH's Newtonian driver, computing gravitational forces with the fast multipole method (FMM) on FleCSI's parallel octree, starting from an initial dataset generated in H5part format. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.softx.2020.100602
skills.summary: Evolve a 3D self-gravitating SPH particle system with FleCSPH's Newtonian driver, computing gravitational forces with the fast multipole method (FMM) on FleCSI's parallel octree, starting from an initial dataset generated in H5part format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The problem is a pure hydrodynamics test without gravity (e.g. 1D/2D Sod tube or Sedov blast) — use the hydro_{1-2-3}d drivers instead of newtonian_3d Higher-than-first-order multipole accuracy is required — FleCSPH implements only the first order of the multipole expansion, at which angular momentum is conserved exactly A non-MPI runtime backend (Legion, Kokkos) is required — the current FleCSPH version is limited to only the MPI backend

skills.description: Use when verifying or benchmarking an SPH/hydro code on a strong point-explosion problem: the goal is to check that a simulated blast wave reproduces the canonical self-similar Sedov density structure in 2D or 3D.
skills.name: self-similar-sedov-solution-comparison
skills.search_text: self-similar-sedov-solution-comparison Use when verifying or benchmarking an SPH/hydro code on a strong point-explosion problem: the goal is to check that a simulated blast wave reproduces the canonical self-similar Sedov density structure in 2D or 3D. The target problem includes self-gravity or long-range forces — use FleCSPH's gravity-enabled path (e.g. newtonian_3d driver with FMM) instead of the hydro-only Sedov setup You need a pure 1D shock-capture check — the paper provides Sod shock tubes in 1D/2D/3D, whereas Sedov is only offered in 2D and 3D The goal is testing gravitational dynamics (single/binary stars) rather than hydrodynamic shock structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_0003 Validates an SPH code's hydro solver by running the FleCSPH Sedov blast-wave cases (2D and 3D), extracting azimuthally/radially averaged density profiles from H5part snapshots, and comparing them against the analytical self-similar Sedov solution. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.softx.2020.100602
skills.summary: Validates an SPH code's hydro solver by running the FleCSPH Sedov blast-wave cases (2D and 3D), extracting azimuthally/radially averaged density profiles from H5part snapshots, and comparing them against the analytical self-similar Sedov solution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target problem includes self-gravity or long-range forces — use FleCSPH's gravity-enabled path (e.g. newtonian_3d driver with FMM) instead of the hydro-only Sedov setup You need a pure 1D shock-capture check — the paper provides Sod shock tubes in 1D/2D/3D, whereas Sedov is only offered in 2D and 3D The goal is testing gravitational dynamics (single/binary stars) rather than hydrodynamic shock structure

skills.name: semi-analytical-disc-structure-modelling

skills.name: shock-tube-riemann-problem-setup
skills.search_text: shock-tube-riemann-problem-setup Use when validating a numerical scheme for 1D special relativistic hydrodynamics (1DRHD) against a known exact solution: a shock tube with a discontinuity at x = 0.5, evolved under the CFL bound lambda*dt/dx < 1 (Eq 40). The PDE system is not hyperbolic-conservative (e.g. the non-conservative primitive-variable Eq 10 alone), since a Riemann-problem validation presumes conservative fluxes that satisfy the entropy and Rankine-Hugoniot jump conditions. No exact analytic Riemann solution or reference data (S1_File.tar.gz-style) is available for the problem's equation of state e = nm + p/(kappa-1), so L1-norm validation cannot be performed. Sets up the relativistic Sod shock-tube (Riemann) problem as a discontinuous initial-value problem on [0,1] with left/right states from Table 1, so that conservative schemes can be validated against the exact Riemann solution via L1-norm errors. astronomy/v1 10.1371/journal.pone.0195494
skills.summary: Sets up the relativistic Sod shock-tube (Riemann) problem as a discontinuous initial-value problem on [0,1] with left/right states from Table 1, so that conservative schemes can be validated against the exact Riemann solution via L1-norm errors.

Applied here to compare the CHEOPS+TESS-derived radius of HIP 29442 d (1.538 ± 0.049 R⊕) against the median radius from the TESS-only discovery paper. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202450472
skills.summary: Computes the uncertainty-weighted (sigma) deviation between a newly derived planetary radius and a previously published value, to test whether two photometric determinations of the same planet are statistically consistent. Applied here to compare the CHEOPS+TESS-derived radius of HIP 29442 d (1.538 ± 0.049 R⊕) against the median radius from the TESS-only discovery paper.

skills.search_text: simulation-ensemble-generation Use when you need to gauge statistical properties of IXPE polarization estimates—e.g., posterior distributions, pull distributions, or spectro-polarimetric fit biases—by Monte Carlo sampling many realizations of the same observation rather than analyzing a single simulated event list. skills.search_text: single-core-throughput-benchmarking Use when measuring single-core write/read throughput (MiB/s) of a rounding or compression routine on radio-telemetry visibility data, or when validating a vectorized (SSE2/AVX2) variant against a scalar baseline. Input data are not strongly correlated typed binary data (e.g. adjacent elements of the fastest-varying index are dissimilar) — Bitshuffle and its rounding/benchmarks assume high inter-element correlation. The goal is multi-threaded throughput measurement — this skill benchmarks a single core explicitly, whereas Bitshuffle itself is parallelized with OpenMP. The data are float or otherwise non-integer typed arrays where the power-of-two rounding granularity routine for signed 32-bit integers does not apply. skills.name: spectral-method-pde-simulation
skills.search_text: spectral-method-pde-simulation Use when a PDE-based physical simulation (fluid dynamics, waves, eigenvalue problems) must be solved at high accuracy with spectral methods, e.g. reproducing resolution-comparison benchmarks or spectral-convergence series. The problem needs only finite-volume or finite-difference accuracy and a code like Athena is already available — this skill targets the spectral-method route and its convergence properties, not generic CFD. The equations cannot be expressed in Dedalus's symbolic vectorial form or the domain/basis geometry does not match Dedalus's supported bases. You need validated off-the-shelf solver binaries without installing dependencies — Dedalus requires source builds (numpy/FFTW/HDF5/OpenBLAS) or the conda-forge feedstock. Simulate partial differential equations with Dedalus, a Python framework that translates plain-text vectorial equations into parallelized global spectral-method solvers, as used in benchmarks such as the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability comparison (2048^2 spectral modes vs 16384^2 finite-volume cells). astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.023068

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are already binned band powers from a likelihood whose window-function binning has already been applied downstream (binning twice would double-count mode weighting) The analysis targets unbinned (per-multipole) likelihoods where a window-function binning step is not part of the data model The likelihood is not a candl-style power-spectrum likelihood (e.g. low-ell commander-style likelihoods handled via clipy), since the binned band-power/vector ordering contract does not apply

skills.search_text: sph-neighbor-list-construction Use when constructing per-particle smoothing-neighbor lists from particle data (e.g. a Sod shock tube run) with FleCSPH/FleCSI, especially in a distributed MPI setting where some octree nodes are owned by other ranks and blocking traversal would stall the rank. Input already consists of exported neighbor lists — go directly to comparison/validation rather than rebuilding them The physics requires exact all-pairs N-body summation rather than smoothing-neighborhood neighbors (FleCSPH's tree/FMM approach targets neighbor affinity and long-range interactions with linear or sublinear complexity) The runtime is not MPI — FleCSPH's current version supports only the MPI backend, so the asynchronous request mechanism cannot be applied in a task-based runtime such as Legion or Kokkos http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Builds per-particle SPH neighbor lists by traversing FleCSI's parallel octree in FleCSPH: particles are inserted into the octree and branches refined until each particle's smoothing neighborhood is isolated, then non-local nodes are fetched via asynchronous MPI requests. The constructed lists are validated entry-by-entry against the neighbor lists from FleCSPH's own tree (hydro_1d). astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.softx.2020.100602
skills.summary: Builds per-particle SPH neighbor lists by traversing FleCSI's parallel octree in FleCSPH: particles are inserted into the octree and branches refined until each particle's smoothing neighborhood is isolated, then non-local nodes are fetched via asynchronous MPI requests. The constructed lists are validated entry-by-entry against the neighbor lists from FleCSPH's own tree (hydro_1d).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input already consists of exported neighbor lists — go directly to comparison/validation rather than rebuilding them The physics requires exact all-pairs N-body summation rather than smoothing-neighborhood neighbors (FleCSPH's tree/FMM approach targets neighbor affinity and long-range interactions with linear or sublinear complexity) The runtime is not MPI — FleCSPH's current version supports only the MPI backend, so the asynchronous request mechanism cannot be applied in a task-based runtime such as Legion or Kokkos

skills.description: Use when validating an analytic equilibrium radiative-transfer solver against a reference code for a spherically symmetric gas distribution with a central point source, by comparing radial ionization-fraction and temperature profiles.
skills.name: spherical-hii-region-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: spherical-hii-region-benchmark-comparison Use when validating an analytic equilibrium radiative-transfer solver against a reference code for a spherically symmetric gas distribution with a central point source, by comparing radial ionization-fraction and temperature profiles. The problem geometry is a semi-infinite slab in an isotropic background rather than a spherical gas distribution with a central point source — use rabacus's slab solver setup instead. Non-equilibrium (time-dependent) ionization or temperature evolution is required — rabacus only provides equilibrium solvers and metal line cooling is not yet included. A cosmological radiation background (e.g. HM12) rather than a central blackbody point source drives the ionization field. Reproduces a published Strömgren-sphere style H II region benchmark (Iliev et al. 2006 Test 2: spherically symmetric gas with a central T_eff = 1e5 K blackbody point source, Ln = 5e48 photons/s over 1–10 Rydbergs, with self-consistent equilibrium temperature evolution) using rabacus, then quantifies agreement against Cloudy 13.03 reference profiles. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.004
skills.summary: Reproduces a published Strömgren-sphere style H II region benchmark (Iliev et al. 2006 Test 2: spherically symmetric gas with a central T_eff = 1e5 K blackbody point source, Ln = 5e48 photons/s over 1–10 Rydbergs, with self-consistent equilibrium temperature evolution) using rabacus, then quantifies agreement against Cloudy 13.03 reference profiles.

skills.description: Use when a lossless compression pipeline needs a high-throughput bit-level transpose of typed arrays (e.g. CHIME 32-bit visibility integers) and naive per-bit looping is too slow.
skills.name: sse2-avx2-vectorized-transpose-optimization
skills.search_text: sse2-avx2-vectorized-transpose-optimization Use when a lossless compression pipeline needs a high-throughput bit-level transpose of typed arrays (e.g. CHIME 32-bit visibility integers) and naive per-bit looping is too slow. Consecutive elements of the dataset are not highly correlated (Bitshuffle requires neighbouring elements to be correlated, with exploitable correlations spanning at least 24 elements) — the transpose overhead yields no compression benefit Data must remain byte-addressable for byte-level shuffle filters or for sophisticated entropy coders like GZIP/BZIP2, which are unlikely to beat simple duplicate-string elimination after bit-level transposition Target CPU lacks the required instruction set — binary wheels are built with AVX2 support and will crash with SIGILL on older processors (pre-Haswell Intel / pre-Excavator AMD) Implements the Bitshuffle bit-transpose pre-filter using vectorized SSE2/SSE and AVX instructions so that rearranging typed binary data into bit-plane-major order runs at roughly 1 byte per clock cycle on modern x86 CPUs, keeping the pre-filter cost negligible relative to I/O. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.07.002
skills.summary: Implements the Bitshuffle bit-transpose pre-filter using vectorized SSE2/SSE and AVX instructions so that rearranging typed binary data into bit-plane-major order runs at roughly 1 byte per clock cycle on modern x86 CPUs, keeping the pre-filter cost negligible relative to I/O.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Consecutive elements of the dataset are not highly correlated (Bitshuffle requires neighbouring elements to be correlated, with exploitable correlations spanning at least 24 elements) — the transpose overhead yields no compression benefit Data must remain byte-addressable for byte-level shuffle filters or for sophisticated entropy coders like GZIP/BZIP2, which are unlikely to beat simple duplicate-string elimination after bit-level transposition Target CPU lacks the required instruction set — binary wheels are built with AVX2 support and will crash with SIGILL on older processors (pre-Haswell Intel / pre-Excavator AMD)

skills.search_text: starlet-wavelet-sparsity-regularization Use when fitting spectral parameters pixel-by-pixel on hyperspectral (IFU) data leaves noisy, ill-posed parameter maps that need spatial regularization to stay physically meaningful at fine scales. The parameter maps are not expected to be sparse in the starlet domain (e.g. highly structured extended targets where the patches are too large for the regularization to compensate, as happened for weak synchrotron emission in Cas A) The data reduction goal is a plain per-spectrum 1D fit with no spatial coupling, where the wavelet proximal step would bias genuinely pixel-local solutions Spatial regularization of latent spectral parameter maps in the SUSHI non-stationary unmixing loop: the starlet (isotropic undecimated) wavelet transform of each parameter map theta_c is soft-thresholded with an MAD-based l1 proximal step, constraining the ill-posed per-pixel spectral fitting. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202347518

skills.when_to_use_negative: The parameter maps are not expected to be sparse in the starlet domain (e.g. highly structured extended targets where the patches are too large for the regularization to compensate, as happened for weak synchrotron emission in Cas A) The data reduction goal is a plain per-spectrum 1D fit with no spatial coupling, where the wavelet proximal step would bias genuinely pixel-local solutions

skills.search_text: starlink-test-dataset-generation Use when reproducing the Section 7.1 benchmark datasets of the HDS/HDF5 reimplementation paper, or when concrete HDSv4, gzipped-HDSv4, and HDF5-backend HDSv5 test files are needed for format-comparison experiments. The goal is converting or migrating existing HDSv4 files to HDF5 rather than generating fresh benchmark files — the README explicitly defers migration ('I'm not yet worrying about migration of HDS v4 files to HDF5'). Benchmarking raw HDF5 write/read throughput independent of the HDS API layer — the HDSv5 library inserts HDS semantics (Fortran dimension order, EMS error wrapping, HDSCELL emulation) that dominate the results. The target format already supports arrays of structures natively (unlike HDF5), so the structural-emulation overhead being measured is absent. Generate the four HDS benchmark datasets used in the HDSv4 vs HDSv5 file-size and performance comparison (AGI graphics database, ADAM parameter file, SCUBA-2 acquisition file, kappa logo NDF) so each exists as a concrete HDS/NDF file on disk in multiple storage variants. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.02.003

skills.description: Use when you need hydrogen recombination line emissivities or excited-state (n, l) level populations for a gas parcel with known electron/proton/neutral-H densities and temperature, e.g. H alpha at ne=100 cm^-3, T=1e4 K.
skills.name: statistical-equilibrium-solver-invocation
skills.search_text: statistical-equilibrium-solver-invocation Use when you need hydrogen recombination line emissivities or excited-state (n, l) level populations for a gas parcel with known electron/proton/neutral-H densities and temperature, e.g. H alpha at ne=100 cm^-3, T=1e4 K. The gas is not atomic hydrogen recombination/line emission (e.g. metal-line or molecular cooling is needed) — HyLight models hydrogen only. Case A (optically thin to Lyman photons) or fully non-equilibrium conditions outside typical photoionised nebular conditions are required and cannot be represented by the caseB/recom/coll flags. A full photoionization code treatment (e.g. Cloudy) of the ionization balance is needed; HyLight takes ne, nHI, nHII, and T as given inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Invoke the HyLight (hylightpy) HIAtom statistical equilibrium model to compute hydrogen excited-state level populations and recombination line emissivities (e.g. H alpha, n=3 to n=2) from gas density, temperature, and ionization state under nebular conditions. astronomy/v1 10.1093/mnras/stag429
skills.summary: Invoke the HyLight (hylightpy) HIAtom statistical equilibrium model to compute hydrogen excited-state level populations and recombination line emissivities (e.g. H alpha, n=3 to n=2) from gas density, temperature, and ionization state under nebular conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gas is not atomic hydrogen recombination/line emission (e.g. metal-line or molecular cooling is needed) — HyLight models hydrogen only. Case A (optically thin to Lyman photons) or fully non-equilibrium conditions outside typical photoionised nebular conditions are required and cannot be represented by the caseB/recom/coll flags. A full photoionization code treatment (e.g. Cloudy) of the ionization balance is needed; HyLight takes ne, nHI, nHII, and T as given inputs.

skills.description: Use when a spectral axis must be transformed between systems defined by different StdOfRest, System or Unit attributes - e.g. heliocentric radio velocity (VRAD) to LSR frequency (FREQ) - using AST SpecFrames.
skills.name: stdofrest-reference-frame-handling
skills.search_text: stdofrest-reference-frame-handling Use when a spectral axis must be transformed between systems defined by different StdOfRest, System or Unit attributes - e.g. heliocentric radio velocity (VRAD) to LSR frequency (FREQ) - using AST SpecFrames. Both spectral frames already share identical System, Unit and StdOfRest attributes - no inter-system Mapping is required. AST cannot generate the Mapping (convert only produces one 'if possible'), e.g. the velocity/frequency frame lacks a RestFreq, so the conversion cannot be realised. The goal is general world-coordinate attachment or FITS-WCS retrieval for images/cubes rather than 1-D spectral reference-frame conversion. Generates a Mapping between two AST SpecFrames whose System, Unit and StdOfRest attributes differ - e.g. heliocentric radio velocity (System=VRAD, RestFreq=345.8 GHz) versus LSR frequency (System=FREQ, Unit=Hz). The convert method returns this Mapping inside a FrameSet that also contains copies of both Frames, and the result can be serialised through an AST Channel for reuse. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2016.02.003
skills.summary: Generates a Mapping between two AST SpecFrames whose System, Unit and StdOfRest attributes differ - e.g. heliocentric radio velocity (System=VRAD, RestFreq=345.8 GHz) versus LSR frequency (System=FREQ, Unit=Hz). The convert method returns this Mapping inside a FrameSet that also contains copies of both Frames, and the result can be serialised through an AST Channel for reuse.

skills.search_text: stellar-age-metallicity-distribution-mapping Use when a simulated stellar population (e.g. a HESTIA snapshot) must be divided into galactic components (bulge, thin disk, thick disk, halo) via age- and metallicity-based classification before assigning planet occurrence rates per region. skills.description: Use when a population-synthesis result (e.g. heavy BBH formation channels, fallback fractions, remnant masses) rests on a supernova engine choice and you need to demonstrate the pathway finding is robust to switching between the delayed and rapid Fryer prescriptions.
skills.name: supernova-remnant-mass-prescription-selection
skills.search_text: supernova-remnant-mass-prescription-selection Use when a population-synthesis result (e.g. heavy BBH formation channels, fallback fractions, remnant masses) rests on a supernova engine choice and you need to demonstrate the pathway finding is robust to switching between the delayed and rapid Fryer prescriptions. When the scientific claim concerns total BBH merger rates already shown to be sensitive to other parameters (e.g. optimistic common-envelope treatment raising rates ~3x, or alpha_lambda 0.1→0.01 dropping rates ~2-4x) — vary those parameters instead; the rapid-vs-delayed check targets pathway robustness, not rate calibration. When studying sub-50 Msun progenitors where the single-star model grid is not extrapolated — the fallback-based heavy-BBH comparison is motivated by primaries up to 100 Msun where SSE grids extend only to 50 Msun. When the model already includes physics (stellar rotation, tides, wind accretion) outside the Fiducial scope, since prescription swaps should be tested one-at-a-time against a fixed Fiducial baseline. A sensitivity-check workflow for binary population synthesis that swaps the supernova remnant-mass prescription (e.g. the Fiducial 'delayed' model for the 'rapid' model of Fryer et al.) in COMPAS and verifies whether evolutionary pathways to heavy BBH mergers are robust. High-mass BH formation proceeds through almost complete fallback under both prescriptions, so pathway conclusions should not hinge on this choice. astronomy/v1 10.1038/ncomms14906
skills.summary: A sensitivity-check workflow for binary population synthesis that swaps the supernova remnant-mass prescription (e.g. the Fiducial 'delayed' model for the 'rapid' model of Fryer et al.) in COMPAS and verifies whether evolutionary pathways to heavy BBH mergers are robust. High-mass BH formation proceeds through almost complete fallback under both prescriptions, so pathway conclusions should not hinge on this choice.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the scientific claim concerns total BBH merger rates already shown to be sensitive to other parameters (e.g. optimistic common-envelope treatment raising rates ~3x, or alpha_lambda 0.1→0.01 dropping rates ~2-4x) — vary those parameters instead; the rapid-vs-delayed check targets pathway robustness, not rate calibration. When studying sub-50 Msun progenitors where the single-star model grid is not extrapolated — the fallback-based heavy-BBH comparison is motivated by primaries up to 100 Msun where SSE grids extend only to 50 Msun. No trained surrogate exists yet — the greedy reduced basis, empirical interpolant, and c_fit fits must be built offline first (see the 4-step construction loop skill) The requested parameter point lies outside the training interval of the surrogate (e.g., q beyond the surrogate's fitted range); extrapolation is not supported by the empirical-interpolant construction Validation requires reproducing waveform physics beyond the fiducial solver's fidelity (e.g., precessing or memory effects) — use the corresponding NR/CCE-trained models like NRSur7dq4 or NRHybSur3dq8_CCE instead of the EOB surrogates here http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Evaluate a reduced-basis surrogate gravitational waveform online at generic parameter choices and benchmark its speedup and accuracy (L2/L∞ errors, evaluation time) against direct fiducial EOB-LAL waveform generation, targeting >3 orders of magnitude faster evaluation. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevx.4.031006
skills.summary: Evaluate a reduced-basis surrogate gravitational waveform online at generic parameter choices and benchmark its speedup and accuracy (L2/L∞ errors, evaluation time) against direct fiducial EOB-LAL waveform generation, targeting >3 orders of magnitude faster evaluation.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how much faster a surrogate waveform model evaluates than the fiducial solver (e.g., EOB-LAL) across sampling rates, or to verify linear-in-L surrogate prediction cost.

skills.search_text: surrogate-vs-fiducial-timing-comparison Use when you need to quantify how much faster a surrogate waveform model evaluates than the fiducial solver (e.g., EOB-LAL) across sampling rates, or to verify linear-in-L surrogate prediction cost. When the goal is waveform accuracy validation (faithfulness, mismatches) rather than computational cost — this skill only measures timing and speedup. When the fiducial waveform family is not generated by a differential-equation solver (e.g., waveforms already produced by a surrogate or lookup table), since the EOB-LAL timing baseline would not be meaningful. When a single fixed sampling rate suffices and no scaling-with-L verification is needed; the sweep across rates is the core of this skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Benchmarks the wall-clock cost of evaluating a gravitational-wave surrogate model against fiducial EOB waveform generation (EOB-LAL) as a function of sampling rate, quantifying the speedup (O(mL + m*c_fit) scaling, ~2,300x at 2,048 Hz). astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevx.4.031006

skills.search_text: survey-classification-merging-rules Decision support for assigning suggested quality-of-match (QOP) classes to automatic redshift matches from autoz-style cross-correlation peaks, or for deciding which classification disagreements require manual merging. Only a single correlation peak exists with no second peak v2 (the modified xcor normalisation sets a normalisation factor of 1 instead of NaN, but the FOM ratio v1/v2 is undefined in a meaningful way) The spectra were not redshifted via the autoz cross-correlation matcher, so v1/v2 peak heights on the Marz normalised scale are unavailable The goal is manual redshifting by template comparison or feature marking rather than classifying automatic matches Applies the Marz Figure-of-Merit quality classification, which converts cross-correlation peak strengths (v1, v2) into a suggested QOP class via the threshold ladder of Eq. 5, and encodes the OzDES merging rule that any QOP 3 vs QOP 4 disagreement must be merged. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2016.03.001

skills.search_text: survey-instrument-calibration Use when simulating survey photometry of transients under real observing conditions and you must match simulated flux uncertainties to measured survey uncertainties (e.g. ZTF g/r/i sky-noise and error floors). Input is already observed (measured) photometry rather than simulated light curves — no sky-noise correction or error floor needs to be inferred. Calibrate a survey simulation's per-point flux uncertainties against real observing conditions by applying band-dependent sky-noise correction factors and fractional error floors, as validated on the ZTF SN Ia DR2 sample with the skysurvey framework. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202452134

skills.description: Use when building or adapting an Einstein-Boltzmann solver from symbolic equations and you need automated stage separation plus analytical sparse Jacobians instead of approximation-switching schemes and finite-difference Jacobians.
skills.name: symbolic-cosmology-model-specification
skills.search_text: symbolic-cosmology-model-specification Use when building or adapting an Einstein-Boltzmann solver from symbolic equations and you need automated stage separation plus analytical sparse Jacobians instead of approximation-switching schemes and finite-difference Jacobians. You need fast reverse-mode automatic differentiation of scalar loss functions — the paper states this is not yet implemented and more work is needed. You want an approximation-switching solver (tight-coupling, ultrarelativistic fluid or radiation-streaming approximations); SymBoltz intentionally solves the full equations at all times, so this skill is the wrong fit for replicating TCA/UFA/RSA-style codes. The model is a hand-coded numerical pipeline with no symbolic equation representation — stage separation and symbolic Jacobian generation require the symbolic System input. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Specify cosmological models as symbolic equation systems (via ModelingToolkit in SymBoltz.jl) so the symbolic-numeric compiler can automatically separate computational stages (background, thermodynamics, perturbations) and generate analytical, sparse Jacobians. This replaces hand-coded stage splitting and numerical Jacobians with exact, sparsity-aware generated code. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202557450
skills.summary: Specify cosmological models as symbolic equation systems (via ModelingToolkit in SymBoltz.jl) so the symbolic-numeric compiler can automatically separate computational stages (background, thermodynamics, perturbations) and generate analytical, sparse Jacobians. This replaces hand-coded stage splitting and numerical Jacobians with exact, sparsity-aware generated code.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need fast reverse-mode automatic differentiation of scalar loss functions — the paper states this is not yet implemented and more work is needed. You want an approximation-switching solver (tight-coupling, ultrarelativistic fluid or radiation-streaming approximations); SymBoltz intentionally solves the full equations at all times, so this skill is the wrong fit for replicating TCA/UFA/RSA-style codes. The model is a hand-coded numerical pipeline with no symbolic equation representation — stage separation and symbolic Jacobian generation require the symbolic System input.

skills.search_text: task-parsing Use when building or extending a websocket-based scientific server that must accept, validate, authenticate, and queue task-execution requests (e.g. send_task messages with module/task/parameters) from browser clients. skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending Dedalus-style sparse spectral pencils for a 1D boundary-value problem (e.g. Chebyshev Poisson on x in [-1,1]) where you need the staged tau-augmented, recombined, and interleaved banded matrices, not just a solution vector.
skills.name: tau-method-boundary-row-construction
skills.search_text: tau-method-boundary-row-construction Use when reproducing or extending Dedalus-style sparse spectral pencils for a 1D boundary-value problem (e.g. Chebyshev Poisson on x in [-1,1]) where you need the staged tau-augmented, recombined, and interleaved banded matrices, not just a solution vector. The problem has no boundary conditions requiring tau rows or basis recombination (e.g. a pure spectral eigenvalue problem already solved densely, as in the paper's Mathieu example using solver.solve_dense) You only need PDE solutions or eigenvalues, not the underlying staged pencil matrices for method-level reconstruction The domain or basis is not the Chebyshev/Ultraspherical setting assumed by the T-to-U conversion relations Reconstructs Dedalus's sparse tau-method pipeline for assembling staged, fully banded pencil matrices for a 1D Chebyshev Poisson problem with Dirichlet conditions (Eq. 19, Fig. 3), combining first-order system formulation, T-to-U test-basis conversion, Dirichlet basis recombination, and mode-interleaved ordering. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.023068
skills.summary: Reconstructs Dedalus's sparse tau-method pipeline for assembling staged, fully banded pencil matrices for a 1D Chebyshev Poisson problem with Dirichlet conditions (Eq. 19, Fig. 3), combining first-order system formulation, T-to-U test-basis conversion, Dirichlet basis recombination, and mode-interleaved ordering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The problem has no boundary conditions requiring tau rows or basis recombination (e.g. a pure spectral eigenvalue problem already solved densely, as in the paper's Mathieu example using solver.solve_dense) You only need PDE solutions or eigenvalues, not the underlying staged pencil matrices for method-level reconstruction The domain or basis is not the Chebyshev/Ultraspherical setting assumed by the T-to-U conversion relations

skills.description: Use when extracting RV time series from echelle S2D spectra (HARPS or ESPRESSO) and you need a statistically principled per-spectrum RV posterior instead of a per-order weighted average of template-matching shifts.
skills.name: template-matching-radial-velocity-estimation
skills.search_text: template-matching-radial-velocity-estimation Use when extracting RV time series from echelle S2D spectra (HARPS or ESPRESSO) and you need a statistically principled per-spectrum RV posterior instead of a per-order weighted average of template-matching shifts. The spectra are not from HARPS or ESPRESSO — S-BART 'can currently be applied to HARPS and ESPRESSO data' only The goal is a full analysis of planetary or activity signals in the RV series — the paper explicitly leaves this for future work The spectra are already reduced to CCF-based RVs by the ESO official pipeline and only a cross-method scatter comparison is needed without re-extraction Estimate precise stellar radial velocities and uncertainties by template matching stellar spectra against a template built from available observations, using S-BART's semi-Bayesian formulation with a Laplace-approximated posterior. It was validated on HARPS archival data of Barnard's star against HARPS-TERRA and SERVAL. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202142262
skills.summary: Estimate precise stellar radial velocities and uncertainties by template matching stellar spectra against a template built from available observations, using S-BART's semi-Bayesian formulation with a Laplace-approximated posterior. It was validated on HARPS archival data of Barnard's star against HARPS-TERRA and SERVAL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spectra are not from HARPS or ESPRESSO — S-BART 'can currently be applied to HARPS and ESPRESSO data' only The goal is a full analysis of planetary or activity signals in the RV series — the paper explicitly leaves this for future work The spectra are already reduced to CCF-based RVs by the ESO official pipeline and only a cross-method scatter comparison is needed without re-extraction

skills.search_text: template-matching-rv-extraction Use when extracting RV time-series from ESPRESSO or HARPS S2D echelle spectra and you need a template-matching alternative to CCF methods with lower RV scatter (e.g. ~10% for M-type stars). You need per-order RV estimates combined by weighted average (the traditional template-matching mode) rather than a common RV shift across orders Input is not HARPS or ESPRESSO data — the paper states S-BART 'can currently be applied to HARPS and ESPRESSO data' only A full analysis of planetary and activity signals is the goal — the authors leave this for future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Extract precise radial velocities via the semi-Bayesian template-matching approach (S-BART), in which a common RV shift describes the difference between each spectral order and a stellar template built from the available observations, with posteriors obtained through Laplace approximation. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202142262

skills.description: Use when a mature, externally-maintained pipeline (e.g. casapy/CASA routines, AMI-reduce) accepts only command-line input and must be incorporated into a fully automated Python reduction pipeline without altering the original code.
skills.name: terminal-emulation-subprocess-control
skills.search_text: terminal-emulation-subprocess-control Use when a mature, externally-maintained pipeline (e.g. casapy/CASA routines, AMI-reduce) accepts only command-line input and must be incorporated into a fully automated Python reduction pipeline without altering the original code. When the target package offers a native scripting interface or can host third-party packages directly (e.g. installing astropy into CASA), since terminal emulation and output-format-dependent parsing add avoidable fragility. When the external tool's output format changes frequently or cannot be guaranteed, because fixed parser rules that detect errors may silently break. When non-cli, API-level control or return-value access is required — terminal emulation only emulates a human typing commands and must parse logged text. Drive legacy command-line scientific tools (here, the casapy process running NRAO CASA routines) from Python by spawning them in a sub-process and emulating interactive terminal input with pexpect, enabling CASA to be embedded in a fully automated Python reduction pipeline. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.08.003
skills.summary: Drive legacy command-line scientific tools (here, the casapy process running NRAO CASA routines) from Python by spawning them in a sub-process and emulating interactive terminal input with pexpect, enabling CASA to be embedded in a fully automated Python reduction pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target package offers a native scripting interface or can host third-party packages directly (e.g. installing astropy into CASA), since terminal emulation and output-format-dependent parsing add avoidable fragility. When the external tool's output format changes frequently or cannot be guaranteed, because fixed parser rules that detect errors may silently break. When non-cli, API-level control or return-value access is required — terminal emulation only emulates a human typing commands and must parse logged text.
