skills.search_text: terminal-velocity-data-normalization Use when kinematic measurements (e.g. terminal velocities from gas tracers) were published under different Galactocentric parameter assumptions (R0, solar motion) and must be made consistent before combining into a unified rotation curve. The user wants the raw published values as given in each original reference — galkin/data/data_*.dat and output/rawdata.dat are not normalized to the selected input parameters and should only be used with full awareness of each reference's assumptions and nomenclature Data are already expressed in the target Galactic parameter frame — reprocessing through galkin_data.py would add no value The analysis requires Galactocentric radii outside ~3–20 kpc, the range the galkin compilation is optimised for http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Normalize Milky Way rotation-curve tracer data (gas, stars, masers, including terminal velocities) compiled under heterogeneous Galactic parameters onto a single user-chosen parameter frame (e.g. R0, peculiar solar motion) using the galkin package. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.softx.2016.12.006
skills.summary: Normalize Milky Way rotation-curve tracer data (gas, stars, masers, including terminal velocities) compiled under heterogeneous Galactic parameters onto a single user-chosen parameter frame (e.g. R0, peculiar solar motion) using the galkin package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The user wants the raw published values as given in each original reference — galkin/data/data_*.dat and output/rawdata.dat are not normalized to the selected input parameters and should only be used with full awareness of each reference's assumptions and nomenclature Data are already expressed in the target Galactic parameter frame — reprocessing through galkin_data.py would add no value The analysis requires Galactocentric radii outside ~3–20 kpc, the range the galkin compilation is optimised for

skills.description: Use when analyzing TESS SPOC PDCSAP or TPF/FFI photometry of a target where nearby Gaia sources may dilute the aperture, or when judging whether a transit/activity signal could originate from a contaminant rather than the target.
skills.name: tess-aperture-flux-contamination-quantification
skills.search_text: tess-aperture-flux-contamination-quantification Use when analyzing TESS SPOC PDCSAP or TPF/FFI photometry of a target where nearby Gaia sources may dilute the aperture, or when judging whether a transit/activity signal could originate from a contaminant rather than the target. When the goal is exoplanet parameter inference from radial velocities or light-curve fitting (e.g. Bayesian analysis of HARPS RVs) rather than aperture contamination — use dedicated transit/RV pipelines instead When the required spatial resolution to exclude contaminants exceeds what TESS photometry alone can provide; TESS-cont can rank implied depths but cannot discard contaminants below the 100% depth threshold When a custom aperture is needed on a tight deadline without author support: the custom-aperture feature is explicitly undocumented http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Quantify the fraction of flux in a TESS photometric aperture contributed by the target star versus nearby Gaia DR2/DR3 contaminants, using TESS-cont's PRF-based modelling of the target's TPF/FFI pixels. This distinguishes dilution-driven transit-depth biases and identifies contaminant sources that could mimic transit or activity signals. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451656
skills.summary: Quantify the fraction of flux in a TESS photometric aperture contributed by the target star versus nearby Gaia DR2/DR3 contaminants, using TESS-cont's PRF-based modelling of the target's TPF/FFI pixels. This distinguishes dilution-driven transit-depth biases and identifies contaminant sources that could mimic transit or activity signals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is exoplanet parameter inference from radial velocities or light-curve fitting (e.g. Bayesian analysis of HARPS RVs) rather than aperture contamination — use dedicated transit/RV pipelines instead When the required spatial resolution to exclude contaminants exceeds what TESS photometry alone can provide; TESS-cont can rank implied depths but cannot discard contaminants below the 100% depth threshold When a custom aperture is needed on a tight deadline without author support: the custom-aperture feature is explicitly undocumented

skills.description: Use when you have a TIC/TOI or Simbad-resolvable target with TESS photometry and need to determine which nearby Gaia stars contaminate the SPOC aperture, whether inside or outside the TPF.
skills.name: tess-contaminant-flux-ranking
skills.search_text: tess-contaminant-flux-ranking Use when you have a TIC/TOI or Simbad-resolvable target with TESS photometry and need to determine which nearby Gaia stars contaminate the SPOC aperture, whether inside or outside the TPF. When the goal is to confidently discard contaminant sources as the origin of a transit signal and TESS-cont DILUTION shows the contaminant depths (e.g. 2–28%) cannot be excluded from the TESS photometry alone — higher-spatial resolution observations (ground-based photometry/spectroscopy) are needed instead When generating custom apertures at a target-flux-percentage threshold — this feature is currently not documented in TESS-cont and requires contacting the author When you need a single authoritative catalogue run only — the README encourages running with BOTH DR2 and DR3 catalogues to ensure no major differences Identifies and ranks the main Gaia DR2/DR3 contaminant sources contributing flux to a TESS target's photometric aperture using TESS-cont, which builds PRFs of nearby sources and computes their flux distributions across TPFs/FFIs. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451656
skills.summary: Identifies and ranks the main Gaia DR2/DR3 contaminant sources contributing flux to a TESS target's photometric aperture using TESS-cont, which builds PRFs of nearby sources and computes their flux distributions across TPFs/FFIs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to confidently discard contaminant sources as the origin of a transit signal and TESS-cont DILUTION shows the contaminant depths (e.g. 2–28%) cannot be excluded from the TESS photometry alone — higher-spatial resolution observations (ground-based photometry/spectroscopy) are needed instead When generating custom apertures at a target-flux-percentage threshold — this feature is currently not documented in TESS-cont and requires contacting the author When you need a single authoritative catalogue run only — the README encourages running with BOTH DR2 and DR3 catalogues to ensure no major differences

skills.description: Use when a planet's radius has been refit with higher-quality or joint photometry (e.g. CHEOPS+TESS) and you need to check whether the revised value is statistically inconsistent (>3σ) with the TESS-only discovery value, especially for small planets with low per-transit SNR.
skills.name: tess-discovery-photometry-radius-comparison
skills.search_text: tess-discovery-photometry-radius-comparison Use when a planet's radius has been refit with higher-quality or joint photometry (e.g. CHEOPS+TESS) and you need to check whether the revised value is statistically inconsistent (>3σ) with the TESS-only discovery value, especially for small planets with low per-transit SNR. The planet radius posterior samples are not available and only the discovery-paper median radius exists (nothing to compare against) The analysis goal is internal-structure inference or formation-history modelling rather than validating/refuting a published radius measurement The comparison target is not a TESS-only discovery value (e.g. comparing two independent high-SNR photometric fits, where the low per-transit SNR caveat does not apply) http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Quantifies the uncertainty-weighted deviation between a revised planet radius (derived from joint CHEOPS+TESS photometry) and the median radius from a TESS-only discovery paper, to test whether TESS photometry alone yields biased radii for small planets. skills.summary: Quantifies the uncertainty-weighted deviation between a revised planet radius (derived from joint CHEOPS+TESS photometry) and the median radius from a TESS-only discovery paper, to test whether TESS photometry alone yields biased radii for small planets. Applied here to HIP 29442 (TOI-469) planet d, whose 1.538 ± 0.049 R⊕ radius deviates by more than 3σ from the discovery-paper median.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The planet radius posterior samples are not available and only the discovery-paper median radius exists (nothing to compare against) The analysis goal is internal-structure inference or formation-history modelling rather than validating/refuting a published radius measurement The comparison target is not a TESS-only discovery value (e.g. comparing two independent high-SNR photometric fits, where the low per-transit SNR caveat does not apply)

skills.description: Use when a TESS TPF/FFI photometric aperture contains flux from Gaia nearby sources and you need to quantify each contaminant's contribution to the aperture or check whether a transit/activity signal could originate there.
skills.name: tess-photometric-aperture-flux-fraction-computation
skills.search_text: tess-photometric-aperture-flux-fraction-computation Use when a TESS TPF/FFI photometric aperture contains flux from Gaia nearby sources and you need to quantify each contaminant's contribution to the aperture or check whether a transit/activity signal could originate there. The goal is exoplanet parameter inference (radial velocities, transit fitting, internal structure modelling) rather than aperture flux-contamination quantification Only higher-spatial-resolution data (ground-based photometry/spectroscopy) can confidently discard contaminants — TESS photometry alone cannot discard contaminants whose DILUTION depths fall below 100% No Gaia sources fall within the aperture/search radius, so no contamination computation is meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes the per-pixel and per-source flux contributions of nearby stars to a TESS photometric aperture by building PRFs of Gaia DR2/DR3 contaminants and locating them on the TESS TPF/FFI pixels, yielding the target's flux fraction (e.g. TOI-5005 contributes 84.4% in Sector 65) and CROWDSAP/FLFRCSAP metrics. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451656
skills.summary: Computes the per-pixel and per-source flux contributions of nearby stars to a TESS photometric aperture by building PRFs of Gaia DR2/DR3 contaminants and locating them on the TESS TPF/FFI pixels, yielding the target's flux fraction (e.g. TOI-5005 contributes 84.4% in Sector 65) and CROWDSAP/FLFRCSAP metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is exoplanet parameter inference (radial velocities, transit fitting, internal structure modelling) rather than aperture flux-contamination quantification Only higher-spatial-resolution data (ground-based photometry/spectroscopy) can confidently discard contaminants — TESS photometry alone cannot discard contaminants whose DILUTION depths fall below 100% No Gaia sources fall within the aperture/search radius, so no contamination computation is meaningful

skills.description: Use when quantifying what fraction of flux in a TESS SPOC aperture (or FFI tesscut) comes from the target star versus nearby Gaia contaminants, or when judging whether a transit/activity signal could originate in a contaminant.
skills.name: tess-pixel-response-function-modelling
skills.search_text: tess-pixel-response-function-modelling Use when quantifying what fraction of flux in a TESS SPOC aperture (or FFI tesscut) comes from the target star versus nearby Gaia contaminants, or when judging whether a transit/activity signal could originate in a contaminant. The photometry is not from TESS (no TPF/FFI data available), since the PRF modelling is specific to TESS pixels You need a definitive origin attribution for a transit signal: dilution depths below the 100% unphysical threshold only rule contaminants in, not out — higher-spatial-resolution ground-based photometry/spectroscopy is required Only a rough first-look contamination estimate is acceptable and runtime is critical — even then, approximate method_prf results should not be used for final analyses or publications Modelling of TESS Pixel Response Functions (PRFs) of nearby Gaia sources to quantify flux contamination in a target's photometric aperture, as implemented by TESS-cont: contaminant Gaia DR2/DR3 sources are identified, their PRFs are interpolated across TESS TPF/FFI pixels, and target-vs-nearby flux fractions (CROWDSAP, FLFRCSAP) are computed. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451656
skills.summary: Modelling of TESS Pixel Response Functions (PRFs) of nearby Gaia sources to quantify flux contamination in a target's photometric aperture, as implemented by TESS-cont: contaminant Gaia DR2/DR3 sources are identified, their PRFs are interpolated across TESS TPF/FFI pixels, and target-vs-nearby flux fractions (CROWDSAP, FLFRCSAP) are computed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The photometry is not from TESS (no TPF/FFI data available), since the PRF modelling is specific to TESS pixels You need a definitive origin attribution for a transit signal: dilution depths below the 100% unphysical threshold only rule contaminants in, not out — higher-spatial-resolution ground-based photometry/spectroscopy is required Only a rough first-look contamination estimate is acceptable and runtime is critical — even then, approximate method_prf results should not be used for final analyses or publications

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how much flux Gaia neighbours contribute inside a TESS SPOC aperture or FFI cutout — e.g. to compute CROWDSAP/FLFRCSAP, correct dilution, or attribute a transit/activity signal to contaminant stars.
skills.name: tess-prf-interpolation-and-placement
skills.search_text: tess-prf-interpolation-and-placement Use when you need to quantify how much flux Gaia neighbours contribute inside a TESS SPOC aperture or FFI cutout — e.g. to compute CROWDSAP/FLFRCSAP, correct dilution, or attribute a transit/activity signal to contaminant stars. The analysis goal is to definitively confirm which star hosts a transit/activity signal — the README notes higher-spatial resolution observations (ground-based photometry/spectroscopy) are needed to confidently discard contaminants when the DILUTION depth thresholds are below the unphysical 100% limit Working with non-TESS data (no TPF or FFI pixels onto which Gaia-source PRFs can be placed) — the skill is specific to TESS TPFs/FFIs Only the PRF shape itself is needed for one source at a fixed position without aperture flux accounting — the surrounding aperture-summing machinery of TESS-cont is unnecessary overhead Builds the TESS PRF of each nearby Gaia DR2/DR3 source, interpolates it onto the pixels of the TESS TPF/FFI cutout, and places it at each source's sky position so per-source flux contributions inside the SPOC photometric aperture can be computed pixel-by-pixel. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451656

skills.description: Use when a generative time-series model (e.g. a latent ODE VAE) trained on irregularly-sampled series over a short interval must be evaluated on a much longer test horizon, and its samples need to be visualised against held-out trajectories.
skills.name: time-series-extrapolation-visualization
skills.search_text: time-series-extrapolation-visualization Use when a generative time-series model (e.g. a latent ODE VAE) trained on irregularly-sampled series over a short interval must be evaluated on a much longer test horizon, and its samples need to be visualised against held-out trajectories. The model was trained on the same interval it is being evaluated on — no extrapolation beyond the training window is being tested, so the four-times-longer rollout and its visual comparison are unnecessary. Data are regularly sampled grids where discrete RNN/sequence models suffice and a continuous-time neural ODE with interpolation-based control path adds no benefit. Time series are non-oscillatory or trend-dominated such that continuation beyond the training window cannot be meaningfully validated against ground truth. Roll a trained latent ODE far beyond its training time window (e.g. from [0, 3] to [0, 12]) with a JAX/Diffrax neural ODE solver, decode the latent trajectory back to data space, and plot generated sample paths against ground-truth trajectories to assess extrapolation quality. astronomy/v1 10.48550/arxiv.2202.02435
skills.summary: Roll a trained latent ODE far beyond its training time window (e.g. from [0, 3] to [0, 12]) with a JAX/Diffrax neural ODE solver, decode the latent trajectory back to data space, and plot generated sample paths against ground-truth trajectories to assess extrapolation quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model was trained on the same interval it is being evaluated on — no extrapolation beyond the training window is being tested, so the four-times-longer rollout and its visual comparison are unnecessary. Data are regularly sampled grids where discrete RNN/sequence models suffice and a continuous-time neural ODE with interpolation-based control path adds no benefit. Time series are non-oscillatory or trend-dominated such that continuation beyond the training window cannot be meaningfully validated against ground truth.

skills.search_text: timing-ratio-computation Use when two builds of the same data-access library (e.g. native HDSv4 and the HDF5-backed hds-v5) have been benchmarked on identical routines and you must assemble a seconds-based timing table and v5/v4 ratio comparison to assess whether the replacement performs comparably. skills.description: Use when you need the differential or cumulative dark matter halo mass function (dndlnm, ngtm) from a linear power spectrum normalised to sigma_8 with a top-hat window function, as implemented in the hmf/HMFcalc framework.
skills.name: top-hat-mass-variance-integration
skills.search_text: top-hat-mass-variance-integration Use when you need the differential or cumulative dark matter halo mass function (dndlnm, ngtm) from a linear power spectrum normalised to sigma_8 with a top-hat window function, as implemented in the hmf/HMFcalc framework. You need CMB power spectra, the age of the universe, or angular diameter distances rather than halo mass functions — call pycamb.camb, pycamb.age or pycamb.angular_diameter directly instead of driving hmf. Your transfer function comes from a non-CAMB source or a file not in CAMB format — hmf will not read it, and Eisenstein & Hu extrapolation (extrapolate_with_eh=True) only applies to high-k CAMB transfer functions. You need halo abundances for dark matter models outside the CDM scope of the paper (e.g. bespoke WDM models) that the current hmf/HMFcalc fitting-function set does not cover. Computes the dark matter halo mass function (dn/dlnM and ngtm) by normalising the linear power spectrum to sigma_8 (mass variance on the 8 h^-1 Mpc scale at z=0 with a top-hat window), applying the linear growth factor, and integrating the mass variance over a top-hat filter to evaluate fitting functions such as Tinker (2008) via the hmf engine. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.11.001
skills.summary: Computes the dark matter halo mass function (dn/dlnM and ngtm) by normalising the linear power spectrum to sigma_8 (mass variance on the 8 h^-1 Mpc scale at z=0 with a top-hat window), applying the linear growth factor, and integrating the mass variance over a top-hat filter to evaluate fitting functions such as Tinker (2008) via the hmf engine.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need CMB power spectra, the age of the universe, or angular diameter distances rather than halo mass functions — call pycamb.camb, pycamb.age or pycamb.angular_diameter directly instead of driving hmf. Your transfer function comes from a non-CAMB source or a file not in CAMB format — hmf will not read it, and Eisenstein & Hu extrapolation (extrapolate_with_eh=True) only applies to high-k CAMB transfer functions. You need halo abundances for dark matter models outside the CDM scope of the paper (e.g. bespoke WDM models) that the current hmf/HMFcalc fitting-function set does not cover.

skills.description: Use when candidate neutron-star EOSs sampled from a low-density chiral-EFT/AFDMC band must be extended to high density and converted into mass-radius-Lambda arrays via the TOV equations for astrophysical (e.g., GW170817-style) constraints.
skills.name: tov-solver-implementation
skills.search_text: tov-solver-implementation Use when candidate neutron-star EOSs sampled from a low-density chiral-EFT/AFDMC band must be extended to high density and converted into mass-radius-Lambda arrays via the TOV equations for astrophysical (e.g., GW170817-style) constraints. The task is kilonova or GRB-afterglow light-curve modeling via NMMA's lightcurve-analysis / create-lightcurve-slurm entry points rather than EOS structure and TOV solving. The inputs are already mass-radius-Lambda arrays from a prior TOV run and only need likelihood evaluation or posterior combination, not a new solve. The density regime of interest lies entirely below 1.5 nsat, where the chiral-EFT Quantum Monte Carlo band is sufficient and no speed-of-sound extension is needed. Implements the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff (TOV) solve inside the NMMA framework to convert candidate EOSs — chiral-EFT-constrained up to 1.5 nsat and extended above 2*nsat with a parametric speed-of-sound model — into mass-radius sequences and tidal deformability (Lambda) predictions, enabling EOS candidates to be tested against ~2 solar-mass pulsar constraints. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6

skills.description: Use when photometric magnitudes must be transformed into principal components as GLM covariates and training and test galaxies risk being decomposed on different bases, skewing photo-z predictions.
skills.name: train-test-projection-consistency
skills.search_text: train-test-projection-consistency Use when photometric magnitudes must be transformed into principal components as GLM covariates and training and test galaxies risk being decomposed on different bases, skewing photo-z predictions. The test set must remain fully blind at fitting time — this method deliberately fits robust PCA on training and test data together, so it violates strict blind-validation protocols. Covariates are already expressed in a shared, consistent basis (e.g. precomputed PCs or colours), so a new decomposition of the combined magnitudes would be redundant. A simple formulation without interaction terms is adequate — the paper notes such simple formulations are 'inadequate in capturing the complexity of the data', but if your task only needs plain linear covariates the full projection-plus-crossing machinery is overkill. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Ensures that PCA covariates used for gamma-GLM photometric redshift regression are computed on a single consistent basis: robust PCA is fitted on the COMPLETE magnitude data set (training and test galaxies together), and the test set is scored by projection onto that stored basis rather than by a separate decomposition. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2015.01.002
skills.summary: Ensures that PCA covariates used for gamma-GLM photometric redshift regression are computed on a single consistent basis: robust PCA is fitted on the COMPLETE magnitude data set (training and test galaxies together), and the test set is scored by projection onto that stored basis rather than by a separate decomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The test set must remain fully blind at fitting time — this method deliberately fits robust PCA on training and test data together, so it violates strict blind-validation protocols. Covariates are already expressed in a shared, consistent basis (e.g. precomputed PCs or colours), so a new decomposition of the combined magnitudes would be redundant. A simple formulation without interaction terms is adequate — the paper notes such simple formulations are 'inadequate in capturing the complexity of the data', but if your task only needs plain linear covariates the full projection-plus-crossing machinery is overkill.

skills.description: Reference for reproducing how hmf interpolates and re-grids CAMB transfer functions (CAMB-format files or pycamb output) in log-space with linear splines before power-spectrum construction.
skills.name: transfer-function-interpolation-logspace
skills.search_text: transfer-function-interpolation-logspace Reference for reproducing how hmf interpolates and re-grids CAMB transfer functions (CAMB-format files or pycamb output) in log-space with linear splines before power-spectrum construction. You need a transfer function at k values beyond the tabulated range and cannot accept an Eisenstein & Hu extrapolation (extrapolate_with_eh=True) instead of an actual CAMB evaluation Your transfer function is not produced by CAMB and is not in CAMB format — hmf will not read it and the interpolation step cannot proceed You are re-running CAMB itself to evaluate T(k) directly at each required k rather than re-gridding a fixed table Interpolate a CAMB-produced matter transfer function T(k) with linear splines in log-space and re-grid it between k-bounds, so that hmf can form the unnormalised power spectrum P0(k) = k^n * T^2. This is the standard pre-processing step in the hmf HMF pipeline between transfer-function acquisition and sigma_8 normalisation. astronomy/v1 10.1016/j.ascom.2013.11.001
skills.summary: Interpolate a CAMB-produced matter transfer function T(k) with linear splines in log-space and re-grid it between k-bounds, so that hmf can form the unnormalised power spectrum P0(k) = k^n * T^2. This is the standard pre-processing step in the hmf HMF pipeline between transfer-function acquisition and sigma_8 normalisation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a transfer function at k values beyond the tabulated range and cannot accept an Eisenstein & Hu extrapolation (extrapolate_with_eh=True) instead of an actual CAMB evaluation Your transfer function is not produced by CAMB and is not in CAMB format — hmf will not read it and the interpolation step cannot proceed You are re-running CAMB itself to evaluate T(k) directly at each required k rather than re-gridding a fixed table

skills.name: transit-depth-radius-retrieval
skills.search_text: transit-depth-radius-retrieval Use when photometric time series from two or more missions (e.g. CHEOPS + TESS) contain transit signals of small planets (≲3.5 R⊕) whose radii need per-transit-SNR-aware joint retrieval with uncertainty validation. The target's transits are already characterized with high per-transit SNR from a single instrument — the joint multi-sector fit is motivated by small, low-SNR planets. Only RVs (ESPRESSO/HIRES) are available and no transit photometry exists — transit-depth retrieval cannot produce radii without light curves. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Jointly model multi-instrument transit photometry (e.g. 9.6 days of CHEOPS light curves plus two TESS sectors) to retrieve per-planet transit depths, radii, and orbital periods with posterior uncertainties. Required because TESS-only radii for small, low-SNR planets can be biased (planet d of HIP 29442 deviates >3σ from the discovery-paper median). astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202450472
skills.summary: Jointly model multi-instrument transit photometry (e.g. 9.6 days of CHEOPS light curves plus two TESS sectors) to retrieve per-planet transit depths, radii, and orbital periods with posterior uncertainties. skills.description: Use when scoring a candidate EOS sample against radio-timing pulsar mass posteriors (Gaussian in mass, with EOS-dependent support up to M_TOV), e.g. to build per-EOS prior log-likelihoods for NMMA neutron-star EOS inference.
skills.name: truncated-gaussian-cdf-evaluation
skills.search_text: truncated-gaussian-cdf-evaluation Use when scoring a candidate EOS sample against radio-timing pulsar mass posteriors (Gaussian in mass, with EOS-dependent support up to M_TOV), e.g. to build per-EOS prior log-likelihoods for NMMA neutron-star EOS inference. The quantity of interest is a joint mass-radius likelihood (e.g. NICER for PSR J0740+6620) rather than a mass-only likelihood — the NICER term is evaluated from the joint M-R posterior, not a truncated Gaussian in mass alone. The mass distribution has no EOS-dependent upper bound, so there is no truncation at M_TOV and an ordinary (untruncated) Gaussian likelihood suffices. You are sampling GW/kilonova event parameters rather than computing per-EOS prior weights in the NMMA EOS-constraint workflow. Evaluates the mass-only pulsar likelihood used by the NMMA EOS-inference framework by integrating Gaussian pulsar mass posteriors over neutron-star masses up to each candidate EOS's maximum mass M_TOV, i.e. a truncated-Gaussian CDF computed via the error function. This encodes how ~2 solar-mass radio-timing pulsars (PSR J0348+0432, PSR J1614-2230) constrain the neutron-star equation of state beyond densities probed by inspiral gravitational waves. astronomy/v1 10.1038/s41467-023-43932-6

skills.description: Use when typed binary arrays with highly correlated consecutive elements (e.g. radio-telescope correlator data) must be bit-transposed as a pre-filter before LZ4/LZF/ZSTD compression, or validated against the reference Bitshuffle library.

skills.search_text: typed-binary-buffer-manipulation Use when typed binary arrays with highly correlated consecutive elements (e.g. radio-telescope correlator data) must be bit-transposed as a pre-filter before LZ4/LZF/ZSTD compression, or validated against the reference Bitshuffle library. This is the paper's sanctioned extension for improving flux-density accuracy over image-plane measurements.

skills.description: Use when fitting parametric radial profiles to ALMA visibilities (e.g. exported ms data like HD109573.12m*npy or hr4796.selfcal.npy) and you need fast initial runs or coarse-but-robust radially averaged profiles.
skills.name: uv-space-visibility-averaging
skills.search_text: uv-space-visibility-averaging Use when fitting parametric radial profiles to ALMA visibilities (e.g. exported ms data like HD109573.12m*npy or hr4796.selfcal.npy) and you need fast initial runs or coarse-but-robust radially averaged profiles. When you need robust, high-precision posterior parameter estimates: aggressive --sz near the disk size yields coarse fits; re-run with larger --sz instead. When radially dependent vertical structure must be modelled — vis-r assumes a single disk plane with vertical scale height fixed with radius, beyond ALMA's capability for most debris discs regardless of averaging. When the data require image-plane analysis (e.g. morphological features that are not axisymmetric radial profiles) — this skill is specific to u,v-space radial averaging. http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Aggressive hard averaging of ALMA interferometric visibilities in u,v space (element (i) of the vis-r method), controlled by the --sz parameter, to produce a radially averaged visibility profile that makes radial-profile fitting fast enough to run on a laptop. astronomy/v1 10.1093/rasti/rzaf004
skills.summary: Aggressive hard averaging of ALMA interferometric visibilities in u,v space (element (i) of the vis-r method), controlled by the --sz parameter, to produce a radially averaged visibility profile that makes radial-profile fitting fast enough to run on a laptop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need robust, high-precision posterior parameter estimates: aggressive --sz near the disk size yields coarse fits; re-run with larger --sz instead. When radially dependent vertical structure must be modelled — vis-r assumes a single disk plane with vertical scale height fixed with radius, beyond ALMA's capability for most debris discs regardless of averaging. When the data require image-plane analysis (e.g. morphological features that are not axisymmetric radial profiles) — this skill is specific to u,v-space radial averaging.

skills.description: Use when you have vapour pressure measurements at multiple isothermal temperatures (e.g. 40-120°C in 20°C increments) and need the enthalpy of vaporization from the Clausius-Clapeyron slope.
skills.name: vaporization-enthalpy-derivation-from-slope
skills.search_text: vaporization-enthalpy-derivation-from-slope Use when you have vapour pressure measurements at multiple isothermal temperatures (e.g. 40-120°C in 20°C increments) and need the enthalpy of vaporization from the Clausius-Clapeyron slope. Input is a single vapour pressure at one temperature rather than a pressure-temperature series — the slope requires multiple isothermal points The goal is to estimate vapour pressures of unknown tetraorganostannanes from a reference compound (Equation 9 theory section) rather than to derive thermodynamic quantities from an existing P-T series The compound is solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) and solid-state vapour pressure is needed via entropy of fusion correction, rather than the liquid-form Clausius-Clapeyron enthalpy Derives the enthalpy of vaporization (AHv) of a compound by fitting a least-squares linear regression of log10(vapour pressure, kPa) versus reciprocal absolute temperature (1/T, K^-1) and converting the slope via AHv = -slope x 2.303 x R, as done for tetramethylstannane (Me4Sn) in Hawker's 1992 Chemosphere study of tetraorganostannane vapour pressures. astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w
skills.summary: Derives the enthalpy of vaporization (AHv) of a compound by fitting a least-squares linear regression of log10(vapour pressure, kPa) versus reciprocal absolute temperature (1/T, K^-1) and converting the slope via AHv = -slope x 2.303 x R, as done for tetramethylstannane (Me4Sn) in Hawker's 1992 Chemosphere study of tetraorganostannane vapour pressures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single vapour pressure at one temperature rather than a pressure-temperature series — the slope requires multiple isothermal points The goal is to estimate vapour pressures of unknown tetraorganostannanes from a reference compound (Equation 9 theory section) rather than to derive thermodynamic quantities from an existing P-T series The compound is solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) and solid-state vapour pressure is needed via entropy of fusion correction, rather than the liquid-form Clausius-Clapeyron enthalpy

skills.description: Use when estimating ambient-temperature (20°C) vapour pressures of tetraalkyl- or tetraalkenylstannanes (e.g. Et4Sn, Vi4Sn) and boiling-point data are available for hydrocarbon analogues.
skills.name: vapour-pressure-estimation-organostannanes
skills.search_text: vapour-pressure-estimation-organostannanes Use when estimating ambient-temperature (20°C) vapour pressures of tetraalkyl- or tetraalkenylstannanes (e.g. Et4Sn, Vi4Sn) and boiling-point data are available for hydrocarbon analogues. The compound is a tetraorganostannane lacking appropriate boiling point data — the paper states estimation adequacy is uncertain 'because of lack of appropriate boiling point data' The target is a triorganostannane — little vapour pressure data exists and published values vary considerably, so applicability is uncertain The tetraorganostannane is solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) — Equation (9) data need conversion to solid vapour pressure using entropy of fusion and melting point, an extra required input not covered here Estimates 20°C vapour pressures of tetraorganostannanes by building hydrocarbon analogues (central Sn replaced by carbon) and applying hydrocarbon-based estimators — the Antoine equation and the Modified Watson correlation — parameterized from normal boiling points, then validating against GC-measured experimental values. astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w

skills.when_to_use_negative: The compound is a tetraorganostannane lacking appropriate boiling point data — the paper states estimation adequacy is uncertain 'because of lack of appropriate boiling point data' The target is a triorganostannane — little vapour pressure data exists and published values vary considerably, so applicability is uncertain The tetraorganostannane is solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) — Equation (9) data need conversion to solid vapour pressure using entropy of fusion and melting point, an extra required input not covered here

skills.description: Use when you have measured or extrapolated vapour pressures (e.g. 20°C values for Me4Sn through n-Bu4Sn) plus a molecular descriptor (MW or fragment-additivity intrinsic molar volume) and need to fit and validate lnP QSPR equations.
skills.name: vapour-pressure-regression-analysis
skills.search_text: vapour-pressure-regression-analysis Use when you have measured or extrapolated vapour pressures (e.g. 20°C values for Me4Sn through n-Bu4Sn) plus a molecular descriptor (MW or fragment-additivity intrinsic molar volume) and need to fit and validate lnP QSPR equations. Applying an MW-based relationship fitted on hydrocarbons to tetraorganostannanes — the article states 'any existing relationship involving MW for hydrocarbons can not be used with tetraorganostannes' Predicting vapour pressures of triorganostannanes or other stannanes where published data are scarce or inconsistent, so the validity of Equation (9) is untested Estimating vapour pressures of tetraorganostannanes that are solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) without converting Equation (9) output using entropy of fusion (ΔSf) and melting point http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Fits ordinary least-squares linear regressions of lnP (kPa) on molecular weight (Eq. 8, organostannanes only) and on intrinsic molar volume (Eq. 9, hydrocarbons and tetraorganostannanes combined) to quantify QSPR relationships for 20°C vapour pressures. astronomy/v1 10.1016/0045-6535(92)90276-w

skills.when_to_use_negative: Applying an MW-based relationship fitted on hydrocarbons to tetraorganostannanes — the article states 'any existing relationship involving MW for hydrocarbons can not be used with tetraorganostannes' Predicting vapour pressures of triorganostannanes or other stannanes where published data are scarce or inconsistent, so the validity of Equation (9) is untested Estimating vapour pressures of tetraorganostannanes that are solid at room temperature (MP > 25°C) without converting Equation (9) output using entropy of fusion (ΔSf) and melting point

skills.description: Use when a Bayesian spectral fit with MCMC/NUTS is too slow for high-resolution data (many channels, e.g. microcalorimeter spectra), a GPU is available, and approximate posteriors within ~10 minutes wall-clock are acceptable.
skills.name: variational-inference-gpu-acceleration
skills.search_text: variational-inference-gpu-acceleration Use when a Bayesian spectral fit with MCMC/NUTS is too slow for high-resolution data (many channels, e.g. microcalorimeter spectra), a GPU is available, and approximate posteriors within ~10 minutes wall-clock are acceptable. When exact, fully-sampled posteriors are required — VI is approximate; jaxspec's no U-turn sampler (MCMCFitter.fit with num_chains/num_warmup/num_samples) is the alternative for accurate posteriors When the parameter estimates must be unbiased at low count rates under chi-square-style fitting — jaxspec's guidance is to fit under a Poisson likelihood (C-stat) regardless, and VI adds approximation error on top When no GPU is available and the dataset is small enough that CPU MCMC finishes quickly — the <10-minute GPU advantage does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Solve Bayesian X-ray spectral inference with variational inference (VI) on a GPU-compiled, differentiable likelihood built from jaxspec/JAX/numpyro, replacing slow MCMC sampling when high-resolution data (e.g. Hitomi microcalorimeter spectra) make NUTS too expensive. The paper shows VI produces convincing results on the Hitomi Perseus cluster observation in under 10 minutes on a GPU. astronomy/v1 10.1051/0004-6361/202451736
skills.summary: Solve Bayesian X-ray spectral inference with variational inference (VI) on a GPU-compiled, differentiable likelihood built from jaxspec/JAX/numpyro, replacing slow MCMC sampling when high-resolution data (e.g. Hitomi microcalorimeter spectra) make NUTS too expensive. The paper shows VI produces convincing results on the Hitomi Perseus cluster observation in under 10 minutes on a GPU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When exact, fully-sampled posteriors are required — VI is approximate; jaxspec's no U-turn sampler (MCMCFitter.fit with num_chains/num_warmup/num_samples) is the alternative for accurate posteriors When the parameter estimates must be unbiased at low count rates under chi-square-style fitting — jaxspec's guidance is to fit under a Poisson likelihood (C-stat) regardless, and VI adds approximation error on top When no GPU is available and the dataset is small enough that CPU MCMC finishes quickly — the <10-minute GPU advantage does not apply

skills.name: velocity-frequency-mapping-construction
skills.search_text: velocity-frequency-mapping-construction Use when spectral data must be transformed between incompatible spectral coordinate systems (e.g. radio velocity under one standard of rest to frequency under another) and a reproducible, serialisable coordinate Mapping is required. The two SpecFrames already share the same System, Unit, and StdOfRest attributes, so no coordinate conversion Mapping is needed The task is a general WCS/FITS-WCS interpretation rather than a conversion between two explicitly defined spectral coordinate systems http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Constructs an AST Mapping between two different spectral coordinate systems — e.g. heliocentric radio velocity (System=VRAD, RestFreq=345.8 GHz) and LSR frequency (System=FREQ, Unit=Hz, StdOfRest=LSR) — by invoking the convert method on one SpecFrame with another as argument. skills.summary: Constructs an AST Mapping between two different spectral coordinate systems — e.g. heliocentric radio velocity (System=VRAD, RestFreq=345.8 GHz) and LSR frequency (System=FREQ, Unit=Hz, StdOfRest=LSR) — by invoking the convert method on one SpecFrame with another as argument. The returned Mapping is encapsulated in a FrameSet that also holds copies of both Frames.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two SpecFrames already share the same System, Unit, and StdOfRest attributes, so no coordinate conversion Mapping is needed The task is a general WCS/FITS-WCS interpretation rather than a conversion between two explicitly defined spectral coordinate systems

skills.description: Use when a full-grid Eulerian Vlasov or hybrid-Vlasov simulation is intractable in memory (e.g. ~10^18 cells / 4 EiB) and the distribution function is negligible in most velocity cells, so sparse velocity-space storage is needed.
skills.name: velocity-space-sparse-storage
skills.search_text: velocity-space-sparse-storage Use when a full-grid Eulerian Vlasov or hybrid-Vlasov simulation is intractable in memory (e.g. ~10^18 cells / 4 EiB) and the distribution function is negligible in most velocity cells, so sparse velocity-space storage is needed. The distribution function has significant phase-space density in most velocity cells, so sparsity provides no saving and buffer-layer overhead dominates. The target is a fluid (MHD) closure where no velocity distribution function is stored at all. Only posterior analysis of existing .vlsv output files is needed — use Analysator/vlsv readers instead of modifying the solver's storage. Stores and propagates the Vlasiator distribution function only where phase-space density is non-negligible, using an f_min threshold, a buffer layer of marginally populated cells, and fixed 4×4×4 velocity cell blocks, reducing the memory footprint of a full Eulerian 3D–3V hybrid-Vlasov magnetospheric run (≥4 EiB without sparsity) by a factor of 10^2–10^3. astronomy/v1 10.1007/s41115-018-0003-2
skills.summary: Stores and propagates the Vlasiator distribution function only where phase-space density is non-negligible, using an f_min threshold, a buffer layer of marginally populated cells, and fixed 4×4×4 velocity cell blocks, reducing the memory footprint of a full Eulerian 3D–3V hybrid-Vlasov magnetospheric run (≥4 EiB without sparsity) by a factor of 10^2–10^3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The distribution function has significant phase-space density in most velocity cells, so sparsity provides no saving and buffer-layer overhead dominates. The target is a fluid (MHD) closure where no velocity distribution function is stored at all. Only posterior analysis of existing .vlsv output files is needed — use Analysator/vlsv readers instead of modifying the solver's storage.

skills.summary: Fit parametric radial surface brightness profiles (e.g. Gaussian, power-law) directly to interferometric visibilities using vis-r, which combines hard u,v-space averaging with a Discrete Hankel Transform, running one to two orders of magnitude faster than image-based modelling on a laptop.

skills.description: Use when a full 3D-3V Vlasov grid is intractable (memory in the EiB range) and the distribution function must be stored and propagated only where phase-space density is non-negligible.
skills.name: vlasov-solver-integration
skills.search_text: vlasov-solver-integration Use when a full 3D-3V Vlasov grid is intractable (memory in the EiB range) and the distribution function must be stored and propagated only where phase-space density is non-negligible. The problem is adequately handled by a magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) fluid model — Vlasiator's hybrid-Vlasov approach exists precisely to describe multi-temperature plasmas and non-MHD processes that MHD cannot self-consistently capture. The phase-space density is broadly populated everywhere, so the f_min-based sparsity discards little and the bookkeeping overhead of blocks and buffer layers yields no savings. Only post-processing or visualization of existing Vlasiator VLSV output is needed — Analysator should be used instead of integrating sparse storage into the solver. Integrates a sparse velocity-space representation into a hybrid-Vlasov solver (Vlasiator) by storing and propagating the ion distribution function only where phase-space density is non-negligible, cutting memory and compute demand of a full Eulerian 3D-3V magnetospheric run from ~4 EiB to a feasible footprint. astronomy/v1 10.1007/s41115-018-0003-2
skills.summary: Integrates a sparse velocity-space representation into a hybrid-Vlasov solver (Vlasiator) by storing and propagating the ion distribution function only where phase-space density is non-negligible, cutting memory and compute demand of a full Eulerian 3D-3V magnetospheric run from ~4 EiB to a feasible footprint.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The problem is adequately handled by a magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) fluid model — Vlasiator's hybrid-Vlasov approach exists precisely to describe multi-temperature plasmas and non-MHD processes that MHD cannot self-consistently capture. The run is proton-only (single-population): there is no second-species field to verify, only standard proton moments. You need to modify simulation physics or run configuration rather than inspect existing output — this skill reads .vlsv files, it does not change or re-run simulations. Your sample is already volume-limited or flux-limited such that selection effects on stretch/colour are absent — no redshift-dependence study is needed. The analysis does not involve the σ(M) mass-variance integral or top-hat window function (e.g. only the differential HMF fitting functions are being evaluated) — the kR rule is specific to window-function integral convergence. skills.search_text: weak-scaling-efficiency-evaluation Use when benchmarking an MPI-parallel spectral/FFT solver at fixed work per core and you need to quantify normalized weak-scaling cost across core counts and compare it to a 1/log2(N) reference trend. You are studying strong scaling (fixed problem size, varying cores) rather than fixed work per core — use a strong-scaling efficiency metric instead. The solver does not rely on global FFT-based transforms with all-to-all transposes, so the 1/log2(N) expectation does not apply as the acceptance criterion. skills.description: Use when integrating second-order linear oscillatory ODEs of the form x'' = -(w(t)^2)x - g(t)x' with a specified frequency w(t) and friction g(t) that oscillate rapidly but vary slowly over part of the range, where standard RK alone is inefficient.
skills.name: wkb-runge-kutta-hybrid-solving
skills.search_text: wkb-runge-kutta-hybrid-solving Use when integrating second-order linear oscillatory ODEs of the form x'' = -(w(t)^2)x - g(t)x' with a specified frequency w(t) and friction g(t) that oscillate rapidly but vary slowly over part of the range, where standard RK alone is inefficient. Problems where the frequency does not vary slowly relative to the integration timescale anywhere in the range — the WKB approximation is invalid and the hybrid offers no advantage Non-oscillatory ODEs solvable efficiently with a standard RK integrator, where the hybrid machinery adds overhead without benefit Cases requiring error-controlled stepping with no user-supplied frequency function, since the method relies on w(t) and g(t) being specified as arrays or functions http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 A hybrid ODE integration strategy that dynamically switches between a Runge-Kutta estimate and the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation in regions of slowly varying frequency, implemented in the oscode C++ solver / pyoscode Python package, so many oscillation periods are skipped per step without losing accuracy. astronomy/v1 10.1103/physrevresearch.2.013030
skills.summary: A hybrid ODE integration strategy that dynamically switches between a Runge-Kutta estimate and the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation in regions of slowly varying frequency, implemented in the oscode C++ solver / pyoscode Python package, so many oscillation periods are skipped per step without losing accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Problems where the frequency does not vary slowly relative to the integration timescale anywhere in the range — the WKB approximation is invalid and the hybrid offers no advantage Non-oscillatory ODEs solvable efficiently with a standard RK integrator, where the hybrid machinery adds overhead without benefit Cases requiring error-controlled stepping with no user-supplied frequency function, since the method relies on w(t) and g(t) being specified as arrays or functions

The task is EXAFS path fitting, where the transform is embedded in feffit_transform (kmin=3, kmax=12, kweight=2, dk=4, kaiser, rmin=1.0, rmax=3.0) rather than a standalone xftf call. http://edamontology.org/topic_3418 Fourier-transform stage of XAFS analysis in Larch: applying an FT window to autobk-derived chi(k) with xftf() to produce a chi(R) spectrum, and characterizing how window parameters (kmin, kmax, dk, kweight, window type) shape the result. astronomy/v1 10.1088/1742-6596/430/1/012007

skills.summary: Jointly fits X-ray surface brightness, X-ray spectroscopic temperature, and Sunyaev–Zel'dovich pressure profiles in a global Bayesian framework (hydromass) to reconstruct hydrostatic mass and thermodynamic profiles of galaxy clusters, including nonparametric log-normal mixture temperature deprojection with PSF deconvolution.

skills.search_text: zodiacal-emission-extrapolation-beyond-model-validity-range Use when you need zodiacal emission forecasts for a future experiment whose observing bands fall below 1.25 µm or above 240 µm (or below 30 GHz / above 857 GHz), outside the DIRBE/Planck model ranges built into ZodiPy. The target observing bands already lie within the built-in 1.25–240 µm / 30–857 GHz validity ranges, where interpolation alone suffices and extrapolation is unnecessary. The analysis requires zodiacal emission timestreams validated against an existing instrument such as DIRBE rather than out-of-range forecasts. You need a physically recalibrated dust model, not a linear extrapolation of built-in model parameters, since extrapolation is a forecast tool, not a validated model extension.
